This head does not build that refusal. Only the grader's stubs land. The body's `## Forward-carry` moves the refusal to "part 3" with `Carry: R11-PRE-ROUND-CHECK-GATE`. An own-group carry is allowed only for a pending owner or orchestrator ruling, or for a split part the approved plan names. The body names no ruling for the split (its one orchestrator ruling covers finder-criticality), and no roster group, carry or resume note names a part 3. The cause of the split is real and I confirmed it: governance.yml's wave-script job restores `tools/policy/check-wave-script.mjs` from `$PINNED` (governance.yml:1665) before "Drive the wave script's branching" (governance.yml:1810), so the refusal and its grader arms cannot land in one pull request. The cure needs no code. Either the orchestrator records part 3 as this group's next part in the roster (carry or resume), or the body names the split as pending the orchestrator's ruling. Every other code, test and figure check below passed, so a re-review is the body or roster delta plus the one test arm below.
- A surviving mutant, which must be fixed in this pull request because it is this group's own seam (card E11-N-NULL-REVIEWER). The brief says the two-seats rule "refuses an evaluator or reviewer that is not a non-empty string". The fix, `norm(ev[k]) if full(ev.get(k)) else ""` with `full = isinstance(v, str) and bool(v.strip())`, does that. Its arm "a null, absent or blank reviewer or evaluator is refused" tries only falsy values (None, "", "  ", 0, []). My mutant C7, `norm(str(ev.get(k) or ""))`, accepts a truthy non-string such as `1` or `["x"]` as the seat name "1". It SURVIVED the whole `check_scopes.py --self-test` (rc 0, ev/mutants-2.txt). The dual that restores the base line, `norm(ev.get(k, ""))` (C7b), is KILLED (ev/mutants-3.txt), so the arm pins null but not the non-string half of the stated domain. The cure is one more value in that arm, for example `1` or `["x"]`, shown killing C7.

+## v10.0.2
+
+**Patch stamp: 12 merges since v10.0.1 (`git log --first-parent --merges --format=%h v10.0.1..HEAD | wc -l`): the card's "Apply this plan" now works when the published plan runs past the manual-plan window, and a floor-return reading far above the room no longer seeds the slab estimate; the rest is tooling and records.**
+
+### Action needed
+
+None: no step is asked of you. No option is added, no default changed, no entity renamed, and no store needs a migration. If a "floor return implausible" repair appears after the upgrade, it names the sensor to check (#3640, below).
+
+### #3649 "Apply this plan" applies the plan only up to the manual-plan window (R11-OUTSIDE-APPLY-PLAN-CEILING, issue #3636)
+
+"Apply this plan" failed whenever the published plan had a run starting 20 hours or more from now, because the card sent runs that start past the manual-plan window and the service refuses any such slot. The card now drops every run starting at or after now plus the published manual-plan window, less one plan step for clock skew between the browser and the server. A run that straddles the window is still sent whole, and a zoomed-in view does not change what is applied. Reported, with the suggested fix, by rasenschachmatt in issue #3636; thanks.
+
+### #3640 A floor-return reading far above the room no longer seeds the slab estimate (R11-OUTSIDE-SLAB-SEED-GUARD, issue #3616)
+
+A heat-pump return reading wired to the floor-return field, far above any floor loop, was believed as stored heat and the plan held none. A reading more than 12 K above the room, or one taken during a hot-water run or a defrost, is now refused and the slab follows the model's own estimate, as on an install with no floor-return sensor. A new repair, `floor_return_implausible`, names the sensor, its reading, the room and the bound, and clears on the next plausible cycle. The floor-return option text (en, de, sv) and the README say which sensor belongs there. Issue #3616's multi-zone request stays open.
+
+### Development process
+
+Developer tooling, CI, audit machinery and records only, no change to the integration: #3652 (self-test scope re-record, part 4), #3629 (self-test red on main), #3622 (plan render), #3642 (brief texts), #3638 (RCA latch clauses), #3646 (new audit dimensions), #3626 (rulings file), #3566 (nudge retirement), #3650 (delivery rows, autofix), #3634 (delivery rows, autofix).
+
+## v10.0.1
+
+**Patch stamp: 20 merges since v10.0.0 (`git log --first-parent --merges --format=%h v10.0.0..HEAD | wc -l`): compressor starts are counted from the running signal's own on and off edges, so a short cycle between two refreshes is no longer missed, and the COP learner's power floor follows what the pump is metered drawing; the rest is tooling and records.**
+
+### Action needed
+
+None: no step is asked of you. No option is added, no default changed, no entity renamed, and no store needs a migration: the start counter keeps its stored lifetime, monthly and running figures and continues from them, and a compressor running across the upgrade is not counted again. If your install has both a compressor frequency sensor and a power meter, starts are now read from the frequency sensor (#3598, below).
+
+### #3598 Compressor starts are counted from the running signal's edges (R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES)
+
+The compressor start counter used to sample the running signal once per refresh and needed two running samples in a row, so a compressor that stopped and restarted between two refreshes counted no start. It now listens to the running signal itself, in every Pump duty control mode including off, and counts each confirmed off-to-on edge, so short cycles are counted. On a power meter, a rise counts as a start once two refreshes read the pump settled running, or when it stops again after a real stop; the brief partial reading an averaging meter shows while the immersion element cuts in or out is not a start. An unavailable or unknown reading counts nothing. Where a frequency sensor and a meter are both set, the counter reads the frequency sensor. The count feeds the month receipt's compressor starts, the wear line of the cost ledger (when a wear price is set) and the insights; the plan itself does not read it, so plans are unchanged. Built on outside design pull request 3420 by Bankaifan, with thanks for the report and the design.
+
+### #3593 The COP learner's power floor follows the pump's metered draw (R10-COP-LEARNER-DRAW-FLOOR)
+
+The measured-COP learner refuses intervals whose power is below a floor taken from your configuration, so a pump that genuinely runs below that figure was refused as if it were cycling and its COP was never learned. Where you set a minimum electrical power, the floor is now capped by the low end of the draws metered while the plan asked the pump to run at or above that minimum, never below the on-threshold; with too few such samples, or no minimum set, it is the configured figure as before. A COP departure from the planned power is now held until the metered draw shows whether the pump follows the plan's ask, then learned if it does and dropped if it does not; while held, the card reads "Waiting to see whether the power draw follows the plan." A held interval is judged by the earlier rule after a week without that evidence, and held intervals are not kept across a restart. The diagnostics download shows the held count (`held_intervals`).
+
+### Development process
+
+Developer tooling, CI, audit machinery and records only, no change to the integration: #3631 (owner criteria, part 1), #3624 (CI predict timeout), #3614 (figure block base), #3618 (brief texts), #3621 (finder contract), #3612 (round metrics, part 1), #3619 (outside contributor cycle, part 3), #3521 (outside contributor cycle, part 2), #3615 (policy-docs timeout), #3551 (self-test scope union guard), #3613 (self-test flake arms), #3606 (self-test scope re-record, part 3), #3610 (test-only Python dependency bumps), #3609 (round-10 round-end triage), #3451 (process slimming, part 2), #3611 (round-10 objective record), #3607 (round-10 closure record), #3617 (delivery rows, autofix).
+

-    wait for it: ``ASK_PENDING`` while the window is still filling, else

+    span's top and low end within ``DISAGREE_FACTOR`` of each other. The
+    COP learner reads a departure as an efficiency shift on ``ASK_FOLLOWS``,
+    and a shift scales every draw alike; a slope of 0.7 over asks spanning
+    3.9 moved the level from 2.1 to 1.4 times the ask. Without that
+    evidence the state says whether to wait for it: ``ASK_PENDING`` while
+    the window is still filling, else
     ``ASK_UNOBTAINABLE`` -- no window at all, asks that never moved, or a

diff --git a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/running_signal.py b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/running_signal.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..e941eb78c3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/running_signal.py
@@ -0,0 +1,194 @@
+"""The compressor's running signal: one listener per pump, its edges, and who hears them.
+
+Design: R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES, part D of Bankaifan's outside pull request
+3420. The class of one reading is ``wear.compressor_running``'s and its
+debounced edges ``wear.EdgeTracker``'s; this module is the Home Assistant glue
+that owns them for one coordinator, in every duty mode, from the coordinator's
+construction (:func:`attach`) to its release (:func:`detach`). It never
+triggers a pass and writes nothing.
+
+**Source** (:func:`source`): the actual-frequency sensor where one is
+configured (never the number entity, a set-point register that echoes the last
+write), else the meter against ``thermal_model.on_threshold_kw``. On the meter
+a reading the coordinator's ``element`` callable calls the immersion element's
+is no signal: a resistive draw is not the compressor (#11).
+
+**Edges.** Each state event of the signal entity is one reading
+(:func:`note`); the coordinator re-reads once per refresh too, since the
+element's latch and the commanded draw change there without a meter event
+(:func:`refresh`), and each subscriber's tick then hears whether the class
+reads settled running: the start counter holds a meter's rise for them. A
+change pending at a reading is confirmed by a timer at
+``wear.EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S`` (:func:`confirm`), because a sensor whose state holds
+fires no event that could confirm it. Each confirmed edge is handed to every
+subscriber (:func:`subscribe`): the start counter always, the duty-switch
+learner while the arbiter listens.
+
+**Running now** (:func:`running_now`): ``True`` or ``False`` for a settled
+class with no change pending; ``None`` before the first confirmed edge, with no
+source configured, while the entity is unavailable or non-numeric, on the meter
+while the element rule holds, and while a change is pending.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+from typing import Any, Callable
+from weakref import WeakKeyDictionary
+
+from homeassistant.core import callback
+from homeassistant.helpers.event import async_call_later, async_track_state_change_event
+from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
+
+from . import wear
+from .drift import utc_elapsed_seconds, utc_shift
+from .entry_config import EntryConfig
+from .freq_control import resolve_reading
+from .inputs import state_power_kw
+from .thermal_model import on_threshold_kw
+
+#: ``() -> (frequency Hz, power kW, threshold kW, by frequency)``, the
+#: arguments of ``wear.compressor_running``.
+Reader = Callable[[], tuple[float | None, float | None, float | None, bool]]
+#: A confirmed edge: (its first changed reading's time, the new class).
+Edge = tuple[datetime, bool | None]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Signal:
+    """One pump's running signal: the tracker, the listener, the timer, the subscribers."""
+
+    hass: Any = None
+    tracker: wear.EdgeTracker = field(default_factory=wear.EdgeTracker)
+    reader: Reader | None = None
+    unsub: Callable[[], None] | None = None
+    #: (the pending change the timer confirms, its cancel), while one is armed.
+    timer: tuple[Any, Callable[[], None]] | None = None
+    subscribers: list[Callable[[Edge], None]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    #: Who hears each refresh's read: ``True`` for a settled running class.
+    ticks: list[Callable[[bool], None]] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+_SIGNALS: WeakKeyDictionary[Any, Signal] = WeakKeyDictionary()
+
+
+def signal_for(coord: Any) -> Signal:
+    """The pump's signal, made on first use; one config entry is one pump."""
+    return _SIGNALS.get(coord) or _SIGNALS.setdefault(coord, Signal(coord.hass))
+
+
+def source(
+    hass: Any, cfg: EntryConfig, params: Callable[[], Any], element: Callable[[float], bool],
+) -> tuple[str | None, Reader]:
+    """The entity whose changes say the compressor started or stopped, and its reader.
+
+    ``params`` returns the live thermal parameters the meter's threshold is
+    read from; ``element`` says whether a meter reading, kW, is the immersion
+    element's. The frequency source reads neither.
+    """
+    sensor, meter, states = cfg.compressor_freq_sensor, cfg.heat_pump_power_entity, hass.states
+
+    def reader() -> tuple[float | None, float | None, float | None, bool]:
+        if sensor:
+            return resolve_reading(None, sensor, states.get, 0.0, 0.0)[0], None, None, True
+        kw = state_power_kw(states.get(meter), "clamp")
+        if kw is not None and element(kw):
+            return None, None, None, False
+        return None, kw, on_threshold_kw(params()), False
+
+    return sensor or meter, reader
+
+
+def attach(sig: Signal, entity: str | None, reader: Reader) -> None:
+    """Listen on ``entity`` and read it once; idempotent, and a no-op without one."""
+    if sig.unsub is not None or not entity:
+        return
+    sig.reader = reader
+
+    @callback
+    def _changed(_event: Any) -> None:
+        note(sig, dt_util.now())
+
+    sig.unsub = async_track_state_change_event(sig.hass, [entity], _changed)
+    note(sig, dt_util.now())
+
+
+def detach(sig: Signal) -> None:
+    """Stop listening, cancel the timer and drop the subscribers and ticks; idempotent.
+
+    The subscribers, the ticks and the reader close over the coordinator, and the
+    table's value would otherwise keep its own weak key alive: a released
+    coordinator is collected only once they are gone. The settled class is kept.
+    """
+    unsub, timer, sig.unsub, sig.timer, sig.reader = sig.unsub, sig.timer, None, None, None
+    sig.subscribers.clear()
+    sig.ticks.clear()
+    if unsub is not None:
+        unsub()
+    if timer is not None:
+        timer[1]()
+
+
+def subscribe(sig: Signal, hear: Callable[[Edge], None], tick: Callable[[bool], None] | None = None) -> None:
+    """Hand ``hear`` every confirmed edge from now on, and ``tick`` each refresh's read; idempotent."""
+    if hear not in sig.subscribers:
+        sig.subscribers.append(hear)
+    if tick is not None and tick not in sig.ticks:
+        sig.ticks.append(tick)
+
+
+def unsubscribe(sig: Signal, hear: Callable[[Edge], None]) -> None:
+    if hear in sig.subscribers:
+        sig.subscribers.remove(hear)
+
+
+def note(sig: Signal, when: datetime) -> None:
+    """One reading of the signal; a no-op before the attach and after the detach."""
+    if sig.reader is not None:
+        _publish(sig, sig.tracker.note(when, wear.compressor_running(*sig.reader())))
+
+
+def refresh(sig: Signal, when: datetime) -> None:
+    """The coordinator's per-refresh re-read; then each tick hears whether the class reads settled running."""
+    note(sig, when)
+    read = running_now(sig) is True
+    for tick in list(sig.ticks):
+        tick(read)
+
+
+def confirm(sig: Signal, when: datetime) -> None:
+    """Settle a change that has held the debounce by ``when``."""
+    _publish(sig, sig.tracker.confirm(when))
+
+
+def running_now(sig: Signal) -> bool | None:
+    """The settled class with no change pending, else ``None``."""
+    return sig.tracker.settled if sig.tracker.pending is None else None
+
+
+def _publish(sig: Signal, edge: Edge | None) -> None:
+    if edge is not None:
+        for hear in list(sig.subscribers):
+            hear(edge)
+    _arm_timer(sig)
+
+
+def _arm_timer(sig: Signal) -> None:
+    """Hold one timer for the pending change, none without one; a held one is kept."""
+    pending = sig.tracker.pending if sig.unsub is not None else None
+    if sig.timer is not None and sig.timer[0] == pending:
+        return
+    if sig.timer is not None:
+        sig.timer[1]()
+        sig.timer = None
+    if pending is None:
+        return
+    due = utc_shift(pending[1], timedelta(seconds=wear.EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S))
+
+    @callback
+    def _due(_now: Any) -> None:
+        sig.timer = None
+        confirm(sig, due)
+
+    delay = max(0.0, wear.EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S - utc_elapsed_seconds(dt_util.now(), pending[1]))
+    sig.timer = (pending, async_call_later(sig.hass, delay, _due))
diff --git a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/slab_seed.py b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/slab_seed.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..8e20a7a368
--- /dev/null
+++ b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/slab_seed.py
@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+"""Whether a floor-return reading may seed the slab estimate (#3616).
+
+The floor-return field seeds the slab every cycle
+(``ThermalModel.update_slab_from_return_temp``), and a seed far above the
+room tells the planner that heat is already stored, so it plans none. That is
+what a heat-pump return on a buffer plant does when it is configured in that
+field: the plan held 0 kWh of space heating with the rooms below target.
+
+A refused reading is not replaced by a guess: the slab keeps the model's own
+estimate, which the coordinator advances exactly as it does with no sensor.
+Pure: no Home Assistant import; the coordinator passes the readings in.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any, Final
+
+from .freq_control import defrost_interval
+
+#: The warmest a floor-loop return may read above the room air it heats, K.
+#: Floor-loop water runs 3-9 K above that air (the repository's working band,
+#: see the ``lower_floor_modelled`` repair text), and EN 1264's surface limits,
+#: 29 C in an occupied zone and 33 C in a bathroom over 20 and 24 C design
+#: rooms, both put the floor 9 K above its room. The 3 K over that is margin
+#: for a sensor on the manifold and a peripheral zone. A buffer or heat-pump
+#: return, which runs at the heating curve's flow temperature, clears it.
+SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K: Final = 12.0
+
+#: The issue raised while a reading is refused for its level, naming the sensor.
+ISSUE_FLOOR_RETURN_IMPLAUSIBLE: Final = "floor_return_implausible"
+
+REFUSED_ABOVE_ROOM: Final = "above_room"
+REFUSED_HOT_WATER: Final = "hot_water_run"
+REFUSED_DEFROST: Final = "defrost"
+
+
+def above_room(return_c: float, room_c: float) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``return_c`` is too far above ``room_c`` to be a floor loop."""
+    return return_c - room_c > SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K
+
+
+def hot_water_run(signals: Any) -> bool:
+    """Whether the pump's observed mode is hot water alone.
+
+    A return probe then reads tank water. Only an observed mode counts: the
+    unknown-mode fallback can do everything and so says nothing either way.
+    """
+    mode = signals.mode
+    return bool(signals.mode_observed and mode.dhw and not mode.space_heat)
+
+
+def refusal(return_c: float, room_c: float, signals: Any) -> str | None:
+    """Why ``return_c`` may not seed the slab now, or ``None`` when it may."""
+    if above_room(return_c, room_c):
+        return REFUSED_ABOVE_ROOM
+    if hot_water_run(signals):
+        return REFUSED_HOT_WATER
+    if defrost_interval(signals.defrosting):
+        return REFUSED_DEFROST
+    return None
+
+
+def seed(model: Any, state: Any, return_c: float | None, signals: Any) -> None:
+    """Advance ``state``'s slab from ``return_c`` unless the reading is refused.
+
+    Called before this cycle's pump signals are read, so ``signals`` are last
+    cycle's; :func:`judge` re-decides on this cycle's before the state publishes.
+    """
+    if return_c is not None and refusal(return_c, state.room_temperature, signals) is None:
+        model.update_slab_from_return_temp(state, return_c)
+
+
+def judge(notices: Any, hass: Any, reading: Any, room_c: float, signals: Any) -> bool:
+    """Whether this cycle's floor-return ``reading`` seeds the slab.
+
+    A refused reading leaves the slab to the model, as no sensor does. The
+    repair naming the sensor is raised while its level is refused and cleared
+    otherwise: judged on the level alone, since a hot-water run or a defrost
+    refuses a reading for that cycle only, which is the plant working, not a
+    wrong sensor.
+    """
+    value = reading.value if reading.ok else None
+    high = value is not None and above_room(value, room_c)
+    notices.report(
+        hass, ISSUE_FLOOR_RETURN_IMPLAUSIBLE, reading.entity_id if high else None,
+        {
+            "entity": str(reading.entity_id),
+            "reading": f"{value:.1f}",
+            "room": f"{room_c:.1f}",
+            "bound": f"{SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K:g}",
+        } if high else None,
+    )
+    return value is not None and refusal(value, room_c, signals) is None

       "description": "Two-zone planning is on and no lower-floor thermometer is configured, so the lower zone starts from the main room sensor and is carried forward by the thermal model — the “Lower floor (modelled)” trace on the plan chart. That is how the zone has to be planned without a sensor, and it is not something the floor-return sensor can supply: return water runs 3–9 K above the room it heats, so it drives the slab estimate, which is what it is genuinely a proxy for. What a modelled zone cannot do is correct itself, so over a long cold spell it can drift from the real downstairs. Assigning “Lower floor temperature sensor” under the zone options closes that loop; this notice clears when you do."
diff --git a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py
index 2f724899f8..05f21f899b 100644
--- a/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py
+++ b/custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py
@@ -1955,6 +1955,27 @@ def on_threshold_kw(params: ThermalParameters) -> float:
     return max(MIN_RUNNING_DRAW_KW, float(params.min_electrical_power) * 0.5)
 
 
+def immersion_level_kw(params: ThermalParameters) -> float:
+    """The MEASURED draw over which the meter carries more than the compressor (#11), in kW."""
+    return float(params.max_electrical_power) * const.IMMERSION_FACTOR
+
+
+def immersion_over(measured_kw: float | None, params: ThermalParameters, commanded_kw: float) -> bool:
+    """Whether one reading is the immersion element wearing the pump's meter (#11).
+
+    Over :func:`immersion_level_kw` while the plan commands heat: no
+    compressor pulls that. The coordinator's latch counts two of these, and
+    the running signal reads the meter as no signal on one, so the two never
+    disagree on what over means.
+    """
+    return (
+        measured_kw is not None
+        and float(params.max_electrical_power) > 0.1
+        and measured_kw > immersion_level_kw(params)
+        and commanded_kw > 0.1
+    )
+
+

       "title": "Ein konfiguriertes Netzentgelt ist negativ",
       "description": "Die Netzentgelt-Ebene enthält einen Satz von {rate} {currency}/kWh (aus der Eingabe {source}). Ein Übertragungsentgelt ist eine Gebühr, ein negativer Wert daher fast immer ein Vorzeichenfehler – und der Plan bepreist jede betroffene Stunde als subventioniert und bevorzugt genau die Stunden, für die der Netzbetreiber Gebühren verlangt. Es wird nichts geändert oder begrenzt: Der Plan rechnet weiter genau mit dem konfigurierten Wert. Korrigiere den Wert auf der Optionsseite \"Netzentgelte und Vertrag\" (oder repariere den Entgeltsensor), dann verschwindet dieser Hinweis im nächsten Planungszyklus."
     },
+    "floor_return_implausible": {
+      "title": "Der Fußboden-Rücklaufsensor misst weit wärmer als jeder Fußbodenkreis",
+      "description": "{entity} misst {reading} °C bei {room} °C im Raum, also mehr als {bound} K darüber. Das Rücklaufwasser eines Fußbodenkreises liegt nur wenige Kelvin über dem beheizten Raum; meist ist hier der Rücklauf der Wärmepumpe selbst oder ein Pufferspeichersensor im Feld für den Fußboden-Rücklauf eingetragen. Aus diesem Feld schätzt die Integration, wie viel Wärme der Estrich hält: Ein so warmer Wert ließ den Plan glauben, der Estrich sei schon voll, und er plante wenig oder keine Heizung, obwohl die Räume unter dem Ziel lagen. Bis dieser Hinweis verschwindet, wird der Wert ignoriert und der Estrich vom Modell geschätzt, wie ohne Sensor. Wähle in den Sensoroptionen einen Sensor im Fußbodenkreis selbst, nach Pufferspeicher oder Mischventil, oder lass das Feld leer; der Hinweis verschwindet im nächsten Zyklus, sobald der Wert plausibel ist."
+    },
     "lower_floor_modelled": {
       "title": "Die Temperatur im Untergeschoss wird modelliert, nicht gemessen",
       "description": "Die Zwei-Zonen-Planung ist aktiv und es ist kein Thermometer für das Untergeschoss konfiguriert, daher startet die untere Zone vom Hauptraumsensor und wird vom thermischen Modell fortgeschrieben – die Kurve „Lower floor (modelled)“ im Plandiagramm. So muss die Zone ohne Sensor geplant werden, und der Fußboden-Rücklaufsensor kann sie nicht ersetzen: Das Rücklaufwasser ist 3–9 K wärmer als der beheizte Raum und speist daher die Estrich-Schätzung, wofür es tatsächlich ein Stellvertreter ist. Eine modellierte Zone kann sich nicht selbst korrigieren und kann daher bei langer Kälte vom echten Untergeschoss abweichen. Weise in den Zonenoptionen den „Lower floor temperature sensor“ zu, um diese Lücke zu schließen; dann verschwindet dieser Hinweis."

diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/draw_map_linearity.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/draw_map_linearity.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..62a2735ad5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/draw_map_linearity.py
@@ -0,0 +1,217 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Set-point-to-draw linearity and the ask judgement (#3106 item 4, R10-DRAW-MAP-EVIDENCE).
+
+The measurement a local seat ran on one owner diagnostics download, ported to
+run on a synthetic fixture this script generates (no row of that download is
+in the tree), and on a seat's own bundle where one is handed to it. It asks
+whether the metered draw follows the electrical level the code maps to a flow
+set-point, and reads every answer beside the control that would have read the
+same if it were false.
+
+  map       the code's own map (``thermal_model.flow_setpoint_for_level``,
+            inverted on a grid, floor from ``modulation_floor_flow_c``),
+            no fitted parameter: residual draw by model fraction over steady
+            heating minutes, and how many minutes the band's middle (0.25 to
+            1.0) held
+  fit       draw on held set-point over the minutes, linear; NULL: held
+            set-points shuffled across segments (1000 permutations)
+  store     the ``DrawRange`` rows (drawn, asked, written, ceiling): draw on
+            written set-point, linear; NULL: written set-points shuffled
+            across rows; PERTURBATION: a planted mid-band bump ``c*4u(1-u)``
+            on the linear fit plus resampled residuals, counting the runs
+            (of 50) where a quadratic beats the line on leave-one-out error
+  ask       the run-asked rows judged by ``draw_range.ask_evidence`` (the
+            production judgement), with their log-log slope, drawn over asked
+            summed, and the factor the fitted level moves across the asks'
+            span; NULL: the same asks drawn at one ratio (the summed level),
+            which must follow
+  steps     the draw's response to each set-point step, before against
+            after (closed-loop levels are confounded: the feedback loop
+            lowers the set-point because the draw is high); NULL: step sizes
+            shuffled across events; PERTURBATION: a planted gain recovered
+  ceiling   the ceiling store's gates (``draw_range.fold``): rows written at
+            the ceiling, ceiling-store rows, and (bundle only) cycles whose
+            action ran the system-identification experiment, the only
+            intervals the store takes
+
+Inputs. Default: the synthetic fixture, seeded, shaped like the measured
+install (a 0.5 to 4.0 kW band, asks piled at the floor, drawn 1.75 x
+ask**0.7, a shallow closed-loop draw on set-point). ``--bundle PATH``: a
+diagnostics download's store rows and cycle rows only (no entity id is read);
+``--minutes CSV`` adds minute rows ``setpoint_c,draw_kw,inlet_c,ok`` a seat
+extracted from the bundle's replay out of tree (``ok`` 1 for a steady
+heating minute, no booster, defrost or hot-water charge).
+
+  PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components python3 dev/audit/harnesses/draw_map_linearity.py
+  ... --bundle diag.json [--minutes minutes.csv]
+
+Synthetic, at R10-DRAW-MAP-EVIDENCE's head: RESULT ask_evidence=does_not_follow
+and RESULT ask_null_proportional=follows; at its base both read follows.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import csv
+import json
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from heatpump_optimizer import draw_range as dr
+from heatpump_optimizer.pump_arbiter import FLOW_GATE_C
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import flow_setpoint_for_level, modulation_floor_flow_c
+
+SEED = 3106
+
+
+def expected_kw(sp, inlet, p_min, p_max, heat_c, lift):
+    """The draw the code books for a held set-point: its own map, inverted."""
+    floor = modulation_floor_flow_c(inlet, FLOW_GATE_C, lift)
+    levels = np.linspace(p_min, p_max, 351)
+    sps = np.array([flow_setpoint_for_level(p, p_min, p_max, heat_c, floor) for p in levels])
+    frac = (sp - floor) / (heat_c - floor) if heat_c > floor else float("nan")
+    return float(np.interp(sp, sps, levels)), frac
+
+
+def linfit(x, y):
+    b = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
+    yh = np.polyval(b, x)
+    return b, 1.0 - np.sum((y - yh) ** 2) / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
+
+
+def loo_rmse(x, y, deg):
+    e = [y[i] - np.polyval(np.polyfit(np.delete(x, i), np.delete(y, i), deg), x[i]) for i in range(len(x))]
+    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(e))))
+
+
+def synthetic(rng):
+    """(config, store rows, minute rows, cycle rows) shaped like the measured install."""
+    cfg = {"p_min": 0.5, "p_max": 4.0, "heat_c": 55.0, "lift": 10.0}
+    asks = ([0.5] * 46 + [0.55 + 0.4 * i / 23 for i in range(24)] + [1.05 + 0.4 * i / 8 for i in range(9)]
+            + [1.6, 1.9, 2.2, 2.4, 2.9] + [3.1 + 0.8 * i / 5 for i in range(6)])
+    store = []
+    for i, a in enumerate(asks):
+        inlet = 30.0 + 10.0 * rng.random()
+        floor = modulation_floor_flow_c(inlet, FLOW_GATE_C, cfg["lift"])
+        written = flow_setpoint_for_level(a, cfg["p_min"], cfg["p_max"], cfg["heat_c"], floor)
+        store.append((1.75 * a ** 0.7 * (1.15, 0.87, 1.0)[i % 3], a, written, cfg["heat_c"]))
+    store += [(1.46 + 0.2 * rng.standard_normal(), 0.5, FLOW_GATE_C, cfg["heat_c"]) for _ in range(26)]
+    minutes, sp = [], 40.0
+    while len(minutes) < 1440:
+        sp = float(rng.choice([30, 35, 38, 41, 44, 47, 50, 55]))
+        inlet = 33.0 + 4.0 * rng.random()
+        for _ in range(int(rng.integers(4, 40))):
+            draw = 3.2 if sp >= 54.5 else 2.2 + 0.04 * (sp - 40.0)
+            minutes.append((sp, draw + 0.35 * rng.standard_normal(), inlet, int(rng.random() > 0.2)))
+    return cfg, store, minutes[:1440], None
+
+
+def from_bundle(path, minutes_csv):
+    data = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))["data"]
+    c = data["config"]
+    cfg = {"p_min": float(c["heat_pump_min_power"]), "p_max": float(c["heat_pump_max_power"]),
+           "heat_c": float(c.get("flow_heat_c") or 55.0), "lift": float(c.get("flow_min_lift_k") or 5.0)}
+    acc = next(v for k, v in data["debug"]["stores"].items() if k.endswith("_accuracy"))["accuracy"]["draw"]
+    store = [tuple(r[:4]) for r in acc["samples"] if len(r) >= 4]
+    cycles = [r.get("action_mode") for r in data["debug"].get("cycle_rows", []) if isinstance(r, dict)]
+    minutes = None
+    if minutes_csv:
+        with open(minutes_csv, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+            minutes = [tuple(float(v) for v in row[:4]) for row in csv.reader(fh) if row and row[0][0].isdigit()]
+    return cfg, store, minutes, (cycles, len(acc.get("ceiling", [])), acc)
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
+    if "--bundle" in argv:
+        mins = argv[argv.index("--minutes") + 1] if "--minutes" in argv else None
+        cfg, store, minutes, extra = from_bundle(argv[argv.index("--bundle") + 1], mins)
+    else:
+        cfg, store, minutes, extra = synthetic(rng)
+    p_min, p_max, heat_c, lift = cfg["p_min"], cfg["p_max"], cfg["heat_c"], cfg["lift"]
+
+    if minutes:
+        m = np.array([r for r in minutes if r[3] and r[0] > FLOW_GATE_C + dr.GATE_TOLERANCE_K and r[1] > dr.RUNNING_FLOOR_KW])
+        exp = np.array([expected_kw(sp, inlet, p_min, p_max, heat_c, lift) for sp, _, inlet, _ in m])
+        res, frac = m[:, 1] - exp[:, 0], np.where(m[:, 0] >= heat_c - dr.CEILING_TOLERANCE_K, 1.0, exp[:, 1])
+        print(f"RESULT map_minutes={len(m)}")
+        print(f"RESULT map_bias_kw={res.mean():+.3f}")
+        print(f"RESULT map_rms_kw={np.sqrt(np.mean(res ** 2)):.3f}")
+        print(f"RESULT map_resid_floor_end_kw={res[frac < 0.25].mean():+.3f}")
+        print(f"RESULT map_resid_ceiling_kw={res[frac >= 1.0].mean():+.3f}" if (frac >= 1.0).any() else "RESULT map_resid_ceiling_kw=none")
+        print(f"RESULT minutes_mid_band={int(np.sum((frac >= 0.25) & (frac < 1.0)))}")
+        seg = np.cumsum(np.r_[1, np.diff(m[:, 0]) != 0])
+        (b, _), r2 = linfit(m[:, 0], m[:, 1])
+        segs = np.unique(seg)
+        means = np.array([m[seg == s, 0][0] for s in segs])
+        null = []
+        for _ in range(1000):
+            perm = dict(zip(segs, rng.permutation(means)))
+            null.append(linfit(np.array([perm[s] for s in seg]), m[:, 1])[1])
+        print(f"RESULT fit_gain_kw_per_k={b:.4f} fit_r2={r2:.3f} fit_null_p95={np.percentile(null, 95):.3f}")
+        steps(np.array([r for r in minutes]), rng)
+    else:
+        print("RESULT map_minutes=none")
+
+    s = np.array([[np.nan if v is None else v for v in r] for r in store], float)
+    hs = s[s[:, 2] > FLOW_GATE_C + dr.GATE_TOLERANCE_K]
+    xs, ys = hs[:, 2], hs[:, 0]
+    (b, a0), r2 = linfit(xs, ys)
+    null = np.array([linfit(rng.permutation(xs), ys)[1] for _ in range(1000)])
+    print(f"RESULT store_rows={len(s)} store_heating_rows={len(hs)}")
+    print(f"RESULT store_gain_kw_per_k={b:.4f} store_r2={r2:.3f} store_null_p95={np.percentile(null, 95):.3f} "
+          f"store_null_p={(1 + np.sum(null >= r2)) / (1 + len(null)):.4f}")
+    base, u = np.polyval((b, a0), xs), (xs - xs.min()) / max(xs.max() - xs.min(), 1e-9)
+    for c in (0.0, 0.35, 1.0):
+        wins = sum(loo_rmse(xs, yy, 2) < loo_rmse(xs, yy, 1)
+                   for yy in (base + rng.permutation(ys - base) + c * 4 * u * (1 - u) for _ in range(50)))
+        print(f"RESULT curvature_c{c:.2f}_wins={wins}/50")
+
+    window = dr.DrawRange()
+    for d, asked, w, ceil in s:
+        window.observe(d, asked, p_min, p_max, None if np.isnan(w) else (w, ceil))
+    pairs = np.array(window._run_asked(), float)
+    la, ld = np.log(pairs[:, 1]), np.log(pairs[:, 0])
+    slope = float(np.polyfit(la, ld, 1)[0])
+    lo, hi = np.percentile(pairs[:, 1], (dr.LOW_PERCENTILE, dr.HIGH_PERCENTILE))
+    level = pairs[:, 0].sum() / pairs[:, 1].sum()
+    print(f"RESULT ask_pairs={len(pairs)} ask_slope={slope:.3f} ask_level_sum={level:.3f} "
+          f"ask_level_moves={(hi / lo) ** abs(1.0 - slope):.3f}")
+    print(f"RESULT ask_evidence={dr.ask_evidence(window)}")
+    flat = dr.DrawRange()
+    for _, asked in pairs:
+        flat.observe(level * asked, asked, p_min, p_max)
+    print(f"RESULT ask_null_proportional={dr.ask_evidence(flat)}")
+
+    at_ceiling = int(np.sum(s[:, 2] >= s[:, 3] - dr.CEILING_TOLERANCE_K))
+    print(f"RESULT store_rows_at_ceiling={at_ceiling}")
+    if extra is not None:
+        cycles, ceiling_rows, _ = extra
+        print(f"RESULT ceiling_store_rows={ceiling_rows} cycles={len(cycles)} "
+              f"experiment_cycles={sum(1 for c in cycles if c == 'system_identification')}")
+    return 0
+
+
+def steps(mins, rng, pre=2, lo=1, hi=3):
+    """Event study over minute rows: draw after a set-point step minus before."""
+    ev = []
+    for i in range(pre, len(mins) - hi):
+        old, new = mins[i - 1, 0], mins[i, 0]
+        if old == new or min(old, new) <= FLOW_GATE_C + dr.GATE_TOLERANCE_K:
+            continue
+        w = mins[i - pre:i + hi]
+        if not w[:, 3].all() or np.any(np.diff(mins[i:i + hi, 0]) != 0) or np.any(np.diff(mins[i - pre:i, 0]) != 0):
+            continue
+        ev.append((new - old, mins[i + lo:i + hi, 1].mean() - mins[i - pre:i, 1].mean()))
+    if len(ev) < 3:
+        print(f"RESULT steps_n={len(ev)}")
+        return
+    x, y = np.array(ev).T
+    g = float(np.dot(x, y) / np.dot(x, x))
+    null = np.array([np.dot(p := rng.permutation(x), y) / np.dot(p, p) for _ in range(2000)])
+    planted = np.median([np.dot(x, 0.27 * x + rng.permutation(y - g * x)) / np.dot(x, x) for _ in range(500)])
+    print(f"RESULT steps_n={len(ev)} step_gain_kw_per_k={g:.3f} step_null_p97_5={np.percentile(np.abs(null), 95):.3f} "
+          f"step_planted_0.27_recovered={planted:.3f}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py
index a1a18579ba..1b23a600e4 100644
--- a/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py
@@ -35,10 +35,21 @@ nothing mutated, must print failed=0. A pattern not found exactly once aborts.
                 (OPENER-LIVE-TIP, P603): the line at A no longer opens at B.
   M-moved-gone  drops the SKIP moved on an absent handoff ref: the null control
                 (a gone ref still prints SKIP moved) fails.
+  M-stale-env   every rc 1 is the environment's (P627 (iv)): a merge conflict
+                neither backs off nor counts.
+  M-stale-key   the HEAD key is dropped: a STALE CHECKOUT result is retried
+                every pass.
+  M-stale-count a STALE CHECKOUT result counts toward MAX_TRIES.
+  M-stale-unread an unreadable tools HEAD reads as a changed one.
+  M-stale-notice a NOTICE under HPO_ALLOW_STALE_TOOLS classifies as the refusal.
+  M-retry-nowrite the retry verb writes nothing (P678 (iii)).
+  M-retry-refuse  the retry verb does not refuse a topic with no entry.
+  M-retry-namesake the retry verb matches a topic by prefix: r10-cp drops r10-cp-2.
+  M-unlisted    a topic held by the cap draws no line: a board topic goes unlisted.
 
     python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_open_driver_mutants.py
 
-EXPECTED RESULT mutants=24
+EXPECTED RESULT mutants=33
 EXPECTED RESULT survived=0
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
@@ -98,6 +109,15 @@ PLANTS = {
     "M-reap-log": ('{reason(d / f"t-{stem(t)}.log")}', '{reason(d / f"t-{t}.log")}'),
     "M-escape": ('topic.replace("%", "%25").replace("/", "%2F")', 'topic.replace("/", "%2F")'),
     "M-maxtries": ('        elif fails.get(f"{topic} {sha}", {}).get("n", 0) >= MAX_TRIES:\n', "        elif False:\n"),

diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_denominator_planted.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_denominator_planted.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..b2cd30ef15
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_denominator_planted.py
@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Planted control for the finder's denominator (COMMON.md, "The denominator"; group R11-PRE-FINDER-CONTRACT).
+
+Metric: of two planted coverage rows, one with no denominator and one carrying enumerator, universe and
+examined, how many the driver's `denominatorGaps` (.claude/workflows/audit-find.js, DISPATCH block) passes
+and how many the start evaluation's reader counts as carrying the pair (dimension_read.py's
+WITH_EXAMINED_UNIVERSE, read at the evaluation sha, never copied into this tree).
+Run:      python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_denominator_planted.py [--eval-sha SHA]   (from the repository root)
+Expected: RESULT driver_refuses_bare=1, driver_passes_full=1, reader_rows=2, reader_counted=1, reader_counts_bare=0
+Null:     the full row is the null control of the bare one: same seat shape, same step, the pair added.
+Baseline: the head of the pull request that lands the denominator; the driver half fails at a driver
+          without `denominatorGaps` (it prints driver_missing=1).
+"""
+import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "..", "tests"))
+from throwaway_git import throwaway_git_init  # noqa: E402
+
+BARE = {"step": "D1.M1", "evidence": "read every file of the step"}
+FULL = {"step": "D2.M1", "enumerator": "git ls-files custom_components | head -3", "universe": 3, "examined": 3,
+        "not_reached": [], "redispatched": [], "evidence": "read every file of the step"}
+
+
+def driver(root):
+    src = open(os.path.join(root, ".claude/workflows/audit-find.js"), encoding="utf-8").read()
+    blk = re.search(r"// DISPATCH:BEGIN[\s\S]*?// DISPATCH:END", src)
+    if not blk or "denominatorGaps" not in blk.group(0):
+        print("RESULT driver_missing=1")
+        return None
+    js = blk.group(0) + "\nconst out = {};\n" + "".join(
+        f"out[{json.dumps(k)}] = denominatorGaps({{ dim: {json.dumps(r['step'][:2])}, steps: ['M1'] }}, {{ coverage: [{json.dumps(r)}] }}, []);\n"
+        for k, r in (("bare", BARE), ("full", FULL))) + "console.log(JSON.stringify(out))\n"
+    r = subprocess.run(["node", "-e", js], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
+    return json.loads(r.stdout)
+
+
+def reader(root, sha):
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
+        script = os.path.join(d, "dimension_read.py")
+        with open(script, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            f.write(subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "show", f"{sha}:dev/audit/rounds/round11/evaluation/dimension_read.py"],
+                                   capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
+        repo = os.path.join(d, "repo")
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo, "dev/audit/rounds/round99"))
+        rep = {"reports": {"D1-s1": {"dimension": "D1", "coverage": [BARE]}, "D2-s1": {"dimension": "D2", "coverage": [FULL]}}}
+        json.dump(rep, open(os.path.join(repo, "dev/audit/rounds/round99/reports-B1.json"), "w"))
+        json.dump({"groups": []}, open(os.path.join(repo, "roster.json"), "w"))
+        env = throwaway_git_init(repo, "-q")
+        for c in (["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-qm", "planted"]):
+            subprocess.run(["git", *c], cwd=repo, env=env, check=True)
+        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", script, "--repo", repo, "--ref", "HEAD", "--round", "99", "--roster", "HEAD:roster.json"],
+                             capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
+    tot = re.search(r"ROWS (\d+) WITH_EXAMINED_UNIVERSE (\d+)", out)
+    per = {l.split("\t")[0]: int(l.split("\t")[11]) for l in out.splitlines() if re.match(r"D\d+\t", l)}
+    return int(tot[1]), int(tot[2]), per.get("D1", 0)
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--eval-sha", default="c6ce415b7711d76cf6c08f926f30da91f7bda924")
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    root = os.getcwd()
+    gaps = driver(root)
+    if gaps is not None:
+        print(f"RESULT driver_refuses_bare={int(bool(gaps['bare']))} count")
+        print(f"RESULT driver_passes_full={int(gaps['full'] == [])} count")
+        print(f"GAPS bare={json.dumps(gaps['bare'])}")
+    rows, counted, bare = reader(root, a.eval_sha)
+    print(f"RESULT reader_rows={rows} count")
+    print(f"RESULT reader_counted={counted} count")
+    print(f"RESULT reader_counts_bare={bare} count")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_main_cancel_mutants.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_main_cancel_mutants.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..44dafcf046
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_main_cancel_mutants.py
@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R11-PRE-TOOLCHAIN-PIN carry 3 (MAIN-CANCEL-BOUNDED): each guard of the `main` arm dies alone.
+
+Each mutant is one exact one-occurrence replacement in a COPY of
+tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py (never the tree); the copy's own `--self-test`
+is then run and must FAIL. Null control: M0, nothing mutated, must print
+failed=0. A pattern not found exactly once aborts.
+
+  M-newest     the newest main run of a workflow may be cancelled.
+  M-row        the bound on a row of runs with no concluded one is dropped.
+  M-bound      the bound is four, not three.
+  M-older-side the row is not counted toward older runs.
+  M-newer-side the row is not counted toward newer runs.
+  M-planned    a cancel planned in this pass is not counted in later rows.
+  M-full       a row reaching the old end of a full listing is cancelled.
+  M-verdicts   a run that completed `skipped` counts as concluded.
+  M-event      a main run of any event is read, not only `push`.
+  M-branch     a push run on any branch is read, not only main.
+  M-dry        `--dry-run` posts the cancels.
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_main_cancel_mutants.py
+
+EXPECTED RESULT mutants=11
+EXPECTED RESULT survived=0
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def repo_root(start):
+    """The directory holding custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+    here = Path(start).resolve()
+    if here.is_file():
+        here = here.parent
+    marker = Path("custom_components") / "heatpump_optimizer" / "manifest.json"
+    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
+        if (cand / marker).is_file():
+            return cand
+    raise RuntimeError(f"no repository root above {start}")
+
+
+ROOT = repo_root(__file__)
+TARGET = "tools/pr/cancel_superseded.py"
+PLANTS = {
+    "M-newest": ("        if i == len(rs) - 1:\n", "        if False:\n"),
+    "M-row": ("        elif hi - lo + 1 > MAIN_ROW_MAX:\n", "        elif False:\n"),
+    "M-bound": ("MAIN_ROW_MAX = 3 ", "MAIN_ROW_MAX = 4 "),
+    "M-older-side": ("        while lo > 0 and empty[lo - 1]:\n", "        while False:\n"),
+    "M-newer-side": ("        while hi < len(rs) - 1 and empty[hi + 1]:\n", "        while False:\n"),
+    "M-planned": ("            empty[i] = True\n", "            pass\n"),
+    "M-full": ("        elif lo == 0 and full:\n", "        elif False:\n"),
+    "M-verdicts": ('VERDICTS = ("success", "failure", "timed_out")', 'VERDICTS = ("success", "failure", "timed_out", "skipped")'),
+    "M-event": ('r.get("head_branch") == "main" and r.get("event") == "push"),', 'r.get("head_branch") == "main"),'),
+    "M-branch": ('r.get("head_branch") == "main" and r.get("event") == "push"),', 'r.get("event") == "push"),'),
+    "M-dry": ('            if a.dry_run:\n                print(f"cancel_superseded: would cancel {rid}")\n            else:\n'
+              "                post_cancel(api, a.repo, rid, {}, time.time())\n        print(f\"CANCEL-MAIN",
+              "            post_cancel(api, a.repo, rid, {}, time.time())\n        print(f\"CANCEL-MAIN"),
+}
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    src = (ROOT / TARGET).read_text()
+    survived = 0
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        for name in ["M0", *PLANTS]:
+            text = src
+            if name != "M0":
+                old, new = PLANTS[name]
+                if src.count(old) != 1:
+                    print(f"ABORT {name}: pattern occurs {src.count(old)} times")
+                    return 2
+                text = src.replace(old, new)
+            copy = Path(tmp) / name / "tools" / "pr" / "cancel_superseded.py"
+            copy.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
+            copy.write_text(text)
+            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(copy), "--self-test"], capture_output=True, text=True)
+            failed = sum(1 for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith("FAIL"))
+            if name == "M0":
+                print(f"RESULT mutant=M0 failed={failed} verdict={'null-ok' if r.returncode == 0 and not failed else 'NULL-RED'}")
+                if r.returncode:
+                    return 2
+                continue
+            dead = r.returncode != 0 and failed > 0
+            survived += not dead
+            print(f"RESULT mutant={name} failed={failed} verdict={'killed' if dead else 'SURVIVED'}")
+    print(f"RESULT mutants={len(PLANTS)}")
+    print(f"RESULT survived={survived}")
+    return 1 if survived else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_owner_criteria.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_owner_criteria.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..da8048d25a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_owner_criteria.py
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R11-PRE-OWNER-CRITERIA: the round-11 unset gaps, and each criteria file
+applied to one planted finding that meets it and one that does not.
+
+Written by the R11-PRE-OWNER-CRITERIA fixer. Run from a worktree root:
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_owner_criteria.py gaps <eval-ref> <head-ref>
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_owner_criteria.py plants
+
+``gaps``: for each ref, a scratch commit (never a branch) whose
+``dev/audit/yardstick/round11/EVALUATION.json`` marks every ``E11-T-*`` and
+``E11-K-*`` card accepted, then ``tools/audit/check_scopes.py --round 11``
+at it; prints each "still leaves unset" and "unset and no card" gap. Pass
+``<eval-ref>`` as eval/r11's tip and ``<head-ref>`` as a merge of the head
+with it: the eval ref is the null control, printing the gaps the head's
+``objective.json`` must close.
+
+``plants``: one met and one unmet plant per criteria file under
+``dev/governance/dimensions/criteria/``, each applying the statement's own
+rule (D10 Q1's command over a planted copy of ``quality_scale.yaml``, D4
+P2's WCAG ratio, D5 C5's word count, D9 B1's 60 s budget times F = 5).
+Each line prints the plant, the measured value and FAILS or PASSES; a met
+plant must print FAILS and an unmet one PASSES, else the run exits 1.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+EVAL = "dev/audit/yardstick/round11/EVALUATION.json"
+YAML = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/quality_scale.yaml"
+CRIT = "dev/governance/dimensions/criteria/"
+
+
+def git(*args, **kw):
+    return subprocess.check_output(["git", *args], text=True, **kw).strip()
+
+
+def overlay(ref):
+    ev = json.loads(git("show", f"{ref}:{EVAL}"))
+    n = 0
+    for cid, card in ev["cards"].items():
+        if cid.startswith(("E11-T-", "E11-K-")):
+            card.update(decision="accepted", ruling="scratch overlay")
+            n += 1
+    blob = git("hash-object", "-w", "--stdin", input=json.dumps(ev, indent=1))
+    fd, index = tempfile.mkstemp()
+    os.close(fd)
+    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_INDEX_FILE=index)
+    try:
+        subprocess.check_call(["git", "read-tree", ref], env=env)
+        subprocess.check_call(["git", "update-index", "--cacheinfo", f"100644,{blob},{EVAL}"], env=env)
+        tree = git("write-tree", env=env)
+    finally:
+        os.unlink(index)
+    return git("commit-tree", tree, "-p", ref, "-m", "scratch overlay"), n
+
+
+def gaps(refs):
+    for ref in refs:
+        sha, n = overlay(ref)
+        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "tools/audit/check_scopes.py", "--repo", ".", "--ref", sha, "--round", "11"],
+                             capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()
+        hit = [ln.strip() for ln in out if "still leaves unset" in ln or "is unset and no card" in ln]
+        print(f"== {ref} (overlay {sha[:10]}, {n} cards accepted): {len(hit)} unset gap(s)")
+        for ln in hit:
+            print("  " + ln.split(" card ", 1)[-1])
+
+
+def q1_rows(text):
+    import yaml
+    rules = yaml.safe_load(text)["rules"]
+    st = lambda v: v if isinstance(v, str) else v["status"]
+    return [k for k, v in rules.items() if st(v) not in ("done", "exempt")
+            or (st(v) == "exempt" and (isinstance(v, str) or not str(v.get("comment", "")).strip()))]
+
+
+def luminance(hexrgb):
+    def lin(c):
+        c /= 255
+        return c / 12.92 if c <= 0.03928 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
+    r, g, b = (int(hexrgb[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5))
+    return 0.2126 * lin(r) + 0.7152 * lin(g) + 0.0722 * lin(b)
+
+
+def contrast(fg, bg):
+    a, b = sorted((luminance(fg), luminance(bg)), reverse=True)
+    return (a + 0.05) / (b + 0.05)
+
+
+def plants():
+    for f in ("D4", "D5", "D9", "D10"):
+        if not os.path.isfile(f"{CRIT}{f}-criteria.md"):
+            sys.exit(f"{CRIT}{f}-criteria.md is not in this tree")
+    live = open(YAML).read()
+    rows = []
+    todo = live.replace("\n  has-entity-name: done\n", "\n  has-entity-name: todo\n", 1)
+    bare = live.replace("\n  async-dependency: done\n", "\n  async-dependency: exempt\n", 1)
+    assert todo != live and bare != live, "a plant matched nothing"
+    rows += [("D10 Q1", "met: has-entity-name: todo", q1_rows(todo), True),
+             ("D10 Q1", "met: async-dependency exempt, no comment", q1_rows(bare), True),
+             ("D10 Q1", "unmet: the live register", q1_rows(live), False)]
+    for fg, met in (("#777777", True), ("#767676", False)):
+        r = contrast(fg, "#ffffff")
+        rows.append(("D4 P2", f"{'met' if met else 'unmet'}: body text {fg} on #ffffff", round(r, 3), r < 4.5))
+    long = " ".join(["word"] * 41) + "."
+    short = "The cap keeps a slow plan from starving the event loop."
+    for txt, met in ((long, True), (short, False)):
+        n = max(len(s.split()) for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", txt) if s)
+        rows.append(("D5 C5", f"{'met' if met else 'unmet'}: a comment's longest sentence", n, n > 40))
+    for host_s, met in ((13.0, True), (3.6, False)):
+        pi = host_s * 5
+        rows.append(("D9 B1", f"{'met' if met else 'unmet'}: {host_s} s host solver CPU per cycle, x F=5", pi, pi > 60))
+    bad = 0
+    for crit, plant, value, fails in rows:
+        verdict = bool(value) if isinstance(value, list) else fails
+        want = plant.startswith("met")
+        bad += verdict != want
+        print(f"{crit}\t{plant}\t{value}\t{'FAILS' if verdict else 'PASSES'}{'' if verdict == want else '  <-- WRONG'}")
+    print(f"plants: {len(rows)}, wrong: {bad}")
+    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["gaps"] and len(sys.argv) == 4:
+        gaps(sys.argv[2:])
+    elif sys.argv[1:] == ["plants"]:
+        plants()
+    else:
+        sys.exit(__doc__)
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_plan_page_inventory.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_plan_page_inventory.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..1ecc14ad2f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_plan_page_inventory.py
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R11-PRE-PLAN-RENDER: what a plan page carries, as a set of structural items.
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_plan_page_inventory.py BASE.html [OTHER.html ...]
+
+Prints the inventory of BASE: one line per item, kind and value, every digit
+run read as `#` so a figure that moved between two snapshots is the same item.
+The kinds: heading, table header row, legend entry, filter control, element
+id, class name, data attribute, event listener, link target shape, and a
+tooltip on a chart bar. For each OTHER it then prints `MISSING <item>` for
+every BASE item OTHER lacks, `ADDED <item>` for every item only OTHER has,
+and `RESULT other=<path> missing=<n> added=<n>`. Exit 1 when any OTHER misses
+an item. Null control: a page against itself prints missing=0 added=0.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def _n(s: str) -> str:
+    return re.sub(r"\d+", "#", re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)).strip()
+
+
+def inventory(text: str) -> set:
+    items = set()
+    for lvl, h in re.findall(r"<h([123])[^>]*>(.*?)</h\1>", text, re.S):
+        items.add(f"heading h{lvl}: {_n(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', h))}")
+    for head in re.findall(r"<thead>(.*?)</thead>", text, re.S):
+        items.add("table: " + " | ".join(_n(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", c))
+                                         for c in re.findall(r"<th[^>]*>(.*?)</th>", head, re.S)))
+    for leg in re.findall(r'<div class="legend">(.*?)</div>', text, re.S):
+        for span in re.findall(r"<span>(.*?)</span>", leg, re.S):
+            items.add(f"legend: {_n(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', span))}")
+    items |= {f"filter: {f}" for f in re.findall(r'data-f="([^"]+)"', text)}
+    items |= {f"id: {i}" for i in re.findall(r'<\w+[^>]*?\sid="([^"]+)"', text)}
+    items |= {f"class: {c}" for cs in re.findall(r'\sclass="([^"]+)"', text) for c in cs.split()}
+    items |= {f"data attribute: {d}" for d in re.findall(r"\s(data-[a-z-]+)=", text)}
+    items |= {f"listener: {ev}" for ev in re.findall(r"addEventListener\('([a-z]+)'", text)}
+    items |= {f"link: {_n(h)}" for h in re.findall(r'href="([^"]+)"', text)}
+    if re.search(r'<g class="grp"[^>]*>\s*<title>', text):
+        items.add("tooltip: chart bar title")
+    return items
+
+
+def main(argv: list) -> int:
+    if not argv:
+        print(__doc__)
+        return 2
+    base = inventory(Path(argv[0]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    for item in sorted(base):
+        print(item)
+    lost = 0
+    for other in argv[1:]:
+        inv = inventory(Path(other).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        for item in sorted(base - inv):
+            print(f"MISSING {item}")
+        for item in sorted(inv - base):
+            print(f"ADDED {item}")
+        print(f"RESULT other={Path(other).name} missing={len(base - inv)} added={len(inv - base)}")
+        lost += len(base - inv)
+    return 1 if lost else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..366281f9f4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py
@@ -0,0 +1,132 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""R11-PRE-RELAY-REBUILD carry 0: #3358's silent skip, replayed on its real commits.
+
+#3358 (branch fix/r10-combi-tank-pr) sat behind handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr 62542627 for
+hours with no trace on the relay's level. This drives one `cloud_relay.sh pass` from a
+given seat directory against a scratch origin holding those commits (objects borrowed
+from this checkout through alternates, refs written directly, nothing pushed):
+
+  case     PR head    handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr   handoff/r10-combi-tank   bodied
+  defect   88f4d521   62542627 (+ body)            577c6974 (+ body)        r10-combi-tank's
+  null     d07f8e9e   62542627 (+ body)            577c6974 (+ body)        both
+
+577c6974 is the head's first parent and stands for the older handoff the relay had applied
+(its last update of #3358 ended OK on 2026-11-09 at an older tip); d07f8e9e is the head the
+handoff was applied at by hand, which contains 62542627. update_pr.sh, approve and dispatch
+are stubs; the stub update records its arguments. Prints, per case:
+
+  RESULT <case>_updated=<0|1> <case>_owed=<level lines naming the PR or the -pr handoff>
+
+Defect at the base seat: updated=0 owed=0 (the silent skip). At the fixed seat: updated=1.
+Null at either seat: updated=0 owed=0 (a head holding its handoff is owed nothing).
+
+    python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r11_relay_3358_skip.py --seat tools/audit/seat
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def repo_root(start):
+    """The directory holding custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+    here = Path(start).resolve()
+    if here.is_file():
+        here = here.parent
+    marker = Path("custom_components") / "heatpump_optimizer" / "manifest.json"
+    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
+        if (cand / marker).is_file():
+            return cand
+    raise RuntimeError(f"no repository root above {start}")
+
+
+ROOT = repo_root(__file__)
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tests"))
+from throwaway_git import throwaway_git_init  # noqa: E402  the scratch repositories' one builder
+PR = "3358"
+BRANCH = "fix/r10-combi-tank-pr"
+HEAD_DEFECT = "88f4d521eb55e62a5b11246396c3f298e932d5b9"
+HEAD_NULL = "d07f8e9ea5a78bf44ea405ef233ae11ad7e1c211"
+HANDOFF_PR = "6254262796cdec57bec1dec5c0d038ba933a215a"
+HANDOFF_OLD = "577c6974205926e7dbaa178b91af96a229ea02f3"
+MAIN = "b8f67a775137a8032d5c71b34ea64165c1d4613a"
+
+
+def git(*argv: str, cwd: Path, env=None, stdin: str | None = None) -> str:
+    return subprocess.run(["git", *argv], cwd=cwd, env=env, input=stdin, text=True,
+                          capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
+
+
+def body_commit(origin: Path, names: str) -> str:
+    """An orphan commit holding BODY.md that names the handoff tip (HELD-BODY reads its first 8)."""
+    blob = git("hash-object", "-w", "--stdin", cwd=origin, stdin=f"Closes #9999\n\nCode head: {names}\n")
+    tree = git("mktree", cwd=origin, stdin=f"100644 blob {blob}\tBODY.md\n")
+    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="h", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="h@h", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="h",
+               GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="h@h")
+    return git("commit-tree", tree, "-m", "body", cwd=origin, env=env)
+
+
+def run_case(seat: Path, case: str, head: str, scratch: Path) -> "tuple[int, int]":
+    d = scratch / case
+    origin, work, state = d / "o.git", d / "w", d / "state"
+    for p in (origin, work, state, d / "bus"):
+        p.mkdir(parents=True)
+    objects = git("rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir", cwd=ROOT) + "/objects"
+    throwaway_git_init(origin, "-q", "--bare")
+    (origin / "objects" / "info" / "alternates").write_text(objects + "\n")
+    bodies = {t: body_commit(origin, tip) for t, tip in (("r10-combi-tank-pr", HANDOFF_PR), ("r10-combi-tank", HANDOFF_OLD))}
+    for ref, sha in (("main", MAIN), (BRANCH, head), ("handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr", HANDOFF_PR),
+                     ("handoff/r10-combi-tank", HANDOFF_OLD), ("handoff-body/r10-combi-tank-pr", bodies["r10-combi-tank-pr"]),
+                     ("handoff-body/r10-combi-tank", bodies["r10-combi-tank"])):
+        git("update-ref", f"refs/heads/{ref}", sha, cwd=origin)
+    throwaway_git_init(work, "-q")
+    (work / ".git" / "objects" / "info" / "alternates").write_text(objects + "\n")
+    git("remote", "add", "origin", str(origin), cwd=work)
+    applied = ["r10-combi-tank " + bodies["r10-combi-tank"]]
+    if case == "null":
+        applied.append("r10-combi-tank-pr " + bodies["r10-combi-tank-pr"])
+    (state / "cloud-handoff-bodied").write_text("\n".join(applied) + "\n")
+    stubs = d / "stubs"
+    stubs.mkdir()
+    for name, text in (("prs", f"printf '{PR}\\t{BRANCH}\\t{head}\\n'"), ("merged", ":"),
+                       ("update", f"echo \"$@\" >> {d}/updated"), ("approve", ":"),
+                       ("dispatch", "echo 'bus-nonce: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef'")):
+        (stubs / name).write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\n{text}\n")
+        (stubs / name).chmod(0o755)
+    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "HPO_"))}
+    env.update(HPO_STATE_DIR=str(state), HPO_BUS_STATE=str(d / "bus"), HPO_RELAY_PRS=str(stubs / "prs"),
+               HPO_RELAY_MERGED=str(stubs / "merged"), HPO_RELAY_UPDATE=str(stubs / "update"),
+               HPO_RELAY_APPROVE=str(stubs / "approve"), HPO_RELAY_DISPATCH=str(stubs / "dispatch"))
+    log = state / "cloud-relay.log"
+    subprocess.run(["bash", str(seat / "cloud_relay.sh"), "pass", "--log", str(log)], cwd=work, env=env,
+                   capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
+    updated = (d / "updated").read_text() if (d / "updated").exists() else ""
+    level = Path(str(log) + ".level")
+    owed = [l for l in (level.read_text().splitlines() if level.exists() else [])
+            if f"#{PR}" in l or "handoff/r10-combi-tank-pr" in l]
+    return int(f"{BRANCH} {HANDOFF_PR}" in updated), len(owed)
+
+
+def main(argv) -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
+    ap.add_argument("--seat", default=str(ROOT / "tools" / "audit" / "seat"), help="the seat directory whose cloud_relay.sh runs")
+    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    seat = Path(a.seat).resolve()
+    for sha in (HEAD_DEFECT, HEAD_NULL, HANDOFF_PR, HANDOFF_OLD, MAIN):
+        if subprocess.run(["git", "cat-file", "-e", f"{sha}^{{commit}}"], cwd=ROOT).returncode:
+            print(f"UNAVAILABLE: {sha} is not in this checkout (git fetch --unshallow origin)")
+            return 3
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="hpo-r11-3358-") as tmp:
+        for case, head in (("defect", HEAD_DEFECT), ("null", HEAD_NULL)):
+            u, o = run_case(seat, case, head, Path(tmp))
+            print(f"RESULT {case}_updated={u} {case}_owed={o}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
diff --git a/dev/audit/harnesses/start_counter_edges.py b/dev/audit/harnesses/start_counter_edges.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..1697a063e4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/harnesses/start_counter_edges.py
@@ -0,0 +1,225 @@
+"""R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES harness: what the compressor start counter counts on
+the sampled path (the base) and on the running-signal edge path (the head),
+on the same synthetic meter traces through the production coordinator.
+
+Part D of Bankaifan's outside pull request 3420. No finder harness exists
+(an outside report); these arms are the build's own. Each arm replays meter
+state changes (one reading a minute, delivered only when the value changes)
+and a refresh every default optimization interval. On a tree with the
+sampled path a refresh is ``_update_current_state`` then
+``_observe_compressor_start``, which is what ``_record_accuracy`` runs once
+per refresh; on a tree with ``running_signal`` the coordinator's own
+listener, confirm timer and per-refresh re-read count.
+
+  control     a meter-only trace whose every on and off phase spans at least
+              two refresh periods: starts counted (three on phases)
+  perturbed   the same trace with one 5-minute stop and restart inside one
+              refresh period: starts counted
+  restored    one start before the ledger load lands, over a stored lifetime
+              of 7: the lifetime after the load
+  s7_60s      an element cut-in with the compressor off on a meter averaging
+              over 60 s, at 6 offsets inside the window: false starts (offset
+              0 fills its window, so its first report is already over)
+  s7_30s      the same on a 30 s averaging meter, 6 offsets: false starts
+  s7r_60s     s7_60s with a refresh every period, one landing between the
+              partial's confirmation and over, the element running three
+              periods and cutting out through a partial: false starts
+  s7r_30s     the same on a 30 s averaging meter: false starts
+  s7r_real    the null control of the two s7r rows: the same rig and
+              refreshes with a real compressor start at each of the 6 offsets
+              of a 60 s window: starts counted (6, one each)
+
+Synthetic inputs only. Run from a worktree root, the base's or the head's:
+  PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests python3 dev/audit/harnesses/start_counter_edges.py
+
+EXPECTED RESULT control=3
+EXPECTED RESULT perturbed=4
+EXPECTED RESULT restored=8
+EXPECTED RESULT s7_60s=0
+EXPECTED RESULT s7_30s=0
+EXPECTED RESULT s7r_60s=0
+EXPECTED RESULT s7r_30s=0
+EXPECTED RESULT s7r_real=6
+
+The expected values are the head's, the refresh-held start (owner ruling D1);
+the base without it reads s7_60s, s7_30s, s7r_60s and s7r_30s 5 and the rest
+the same.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
+
+from harness import FakeEntry, FakeHass, FakeState
+from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
+from heatpump_optimizer.const import DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL
+from heatpump_optimizer.coordinator import HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import on_threshold_kw
+
+try:
+    from heatpump_optimizer import running_signal  # noqa: F401
+    EDGES = True
+except ImportError:
+    EDGES = False
+
+T0 = datetime(2026, 2, 3, 6, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+PERIOD_S = 60 * DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL
+BASE = {"tibber_token": "x", "weather_entity": "weather.home", "heat_pump_power_entity": "sensor.kw"}
+
+
+class Rig:
+    """One coordinator over the fake bus; fires due timers once, in order."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        dt_util.freeze(T0)
+        self.c = HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator(FakeHass({"sensor.kw": FakeState("0.0", unit="kW")}),
+                                              FakeEntry(data=dict(BASE)))
+        self.now, self.armed = T0, {}
+        self._seen()
+
+    def _seen(self):
+        for entry in getattr(self.c.hass, "timers", []):
+            self.armed.setdefault(id(entry), (self.now, entry))
+
+    def at(self, when):
+        while True:
+            live = getattr(self.c.hass, "timers", [])
+            due = sorted(((t + timedelta(seconds=e[0]), k, e) for k, (t, e) in self.armed.items()
+                          if e in live and t + timedelta(seconds=e[0]) <= when), key=lambda d: d[0])
+            if not due:
+                break
+            fire_at, key, entry = due[0]
+            self.now = max(self.now, fire_at)
+            dt_util.freeze(self.now)
+            live.remove(entry)
+            del self.armed[key]
+            entry[1](self.now)
+            self._seen()
+        self.now = when
+        dt_util.freeze(when)
+
+    def set(self, kw, when):
+        self.at(when)
+        value = f"{kw:.2f}"
+        old = self.c.hass.states.get("sensor.kw")
+        self.c.hass.states.set("sensor.kw", FakeState(value, unit="kW"))
+        if old is not None and old.state == value:
+            return
+        for ids, action in list(getattr(self.c.hass, "state_listeners", [])):
+            if "sensor.kw" in ids:
+                action(NS(data={"new_state": self.c.hass.states.get("sensor.kw")}))
+        self._seen()
+
+    def refresh(self, when):
+        self.at(when)
+        asyncio.run(self.c._update_current_state())
+        if not EDGES:
+            self.c._observe_compressor_start(when)
+        self._seen()
+
+    def load(self, payload):
+        async def _load(_p=payload):
+            return _p
+        self.c._ledger_store.async_load = _load
+        asyncio.run(self.c._async_load_ledger())
+
+
+def replay(readings, refreshes=True, rig=None, load=True):
+    """``readings``: [(second, kW)]; a refresh every period. Returns the rig."""
+    rig = rig or Rig()
+    if load:
+        rig.load(None)
+    refresh_at = PERIOD_S
+    for second, kw in readings:
+        while refreshes and second >= refresh_at:
+            rig.refresh(T0 + timedelta(seconds=refresh_at))
+            refresh_at += PERIOD_S
+        rig.set(kw, T0 + timedelta(seconds=second))
+    rig.at(T0 + timedelta(seconds=readings[-1][0] + 60))
+    return rig
+
+
+PHASES = [(90, 0.0), (120, 2.0), (90, 0.0), (150, 2.0), (120, 0.0), (90, 2.0), (60, 0.0)]
+
+
+def trace(perturb=None):
+    out, t = [], 0
+    for minutes, kw in PHASES:
+        for s in range(t, t + minutes * 60, 60):
+            off = perturb is not None and perturb[0] * 60 <= s < (perturb[0] + perturb[1]) * 60
+            out.append((s, 0.0 if off else kw))
+        t += minutes * 60
+    return out
+
+
+def restored():
+    rig = Rig()
+    rig.set(2.0, T0 + timedelta(minutes=1))
+    rig.set(2.0, T0 + timedelta(minutes=2))
+    for k in (1, 2):  # two refreshes see the draw before the store is read
+        rig.refresh(T0 + timedelta(minutes=2, seconds=k))
+    rig.load({"ledger": {"months": {}}, "starts": {"lifetime": 7, "months": {}, "running": False}})
+    return rig.c._start_counter.lifetime
+
+
+def s7(window_s):
+    """An element cut-in, compressor off, on a meter reporting its window's average.
+
+    The element draws 1.15 x nameplate + 1 kW from offset ``u`` inside a
+    window, so the first report is a partial average; the next is the full
+    level. A start is false here: the compressor never ran.
+    """
+    false = 0
+    for u in [window_s * k / 6 for k in range(6)]:
+        rig = Rig()
+        rig.load(None)
+        rig.c._current_action = {**rig.c._current_action, "power": 2.0, "dhw_power": 0.0}
+        params = rig.c._ctx._thermal_params
+        level = float(params.max_electrical_power) * 1.15 + 1.0
+        partial = level * (window_s - u) / window_s
+        assert partial >= on_threshold_kw(params)
+        rig.set(partial, T0 + timedelta(seconds=600))
+        rig.set(level, T0 + timedelta(seconds=600 + window_s))
+        rig.at(T0 + timedelta(seconds=900))
+        false += rig.c._start_counter.lifetime
+    return false
+
+
+def s7r(window_s, real=False):
+    """``s7`` with the refreshes: one every period from the first, the element
+    running three periods and cutting out through a partial; ``real`` replaces
+    the element by a compressor start at 2 kW at the same instants."""
+    counted = 0
+    for u in [window_s * k / 6 for k in range(6)]:
+        rig = Rig()
+        rig.load(None)
+        rig.c._current_action = {**rig.c._current_action, "power": 2.0, "dhw_power": 0.0}
+        level = 2.0 if real else float(rig.c._ctx._thermal_params.max_electrical_power) * 1.15 + 1.0
+        partial = level * (window_s - u) / window_s
+        rise = T0 + timedelta(seconds=PERIOD_S - 45)
+        rig.set(partial, rise)
+        rig.refresh(T0 + timedelta(seconds=PERIOD_S))
+        rig.set(level, rise + timedelta(seconds=window_s))
+        for k in (2, 3, 4):
+            rig.refresh(T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * PERIOD_S))
+        cut = T0 + timedelta(seconds=4 * PERIOD_S + 60)
+        if not real:
+            rig.set(level * u / window_s, cut)
+            rig.set(0.0, cut + timedelta(seconds=window_s))
+        for k in (5, 6, 7):
+            rig.refresh(T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * PERIOD_S))
+        counted += rig.c._start_counter.lifetime
+    return counted
+
+
+print(f"tree: {'edge path (running_signal)' if EDGES else 'sampled path'}")
+print(f"RESULT control={replay(trace()).c._start_counter.lifetime}")
+print(f"RESULT perturbed={replay(trace(perturb=(90 + 40, 5))).c._start_counter.lifetime}")
+print(f"RESULT restored={restored()}")
+print(f"RESULT s7_60s={s7(60)}")
+print(f"RESULT s7_30s={s7(30)}")
+print(f"RESULT s7r_60s={s7r(60)}")
+print(f"RESULT s7r_30s={s7r(30)}")
+print(f"RESULT s7r_real={s7r(60, real=True)}")
+dt_util.freeze(None)
