+"""R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES mutation proof: each production line the build adds or
+moves, broken one at a time, against the two features.py blocks that pin it.
+
+The blocks are the build's own ("R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: the start counter
+fed from running-signal edges") and part A's ("duty-switch restart learning,
+part A"), each run alone by tools/audit/seat/features_block.py with the
+prelude its --emit-prelude derives from the tree. A mutant is KILLED when a
+check in either block fails or the block raises; the unmutated tree is run
+first and must pass both blocks (the null control). Each file is restored in a
+finally, so run it on a clean checkout and read git status after.
+
+  PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/harnesses/start_counter_edges_mutants.py
+
+Prints one KILLED or SURVIVED line per mutant and RESULT survived=<n>.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import pathlib
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+P = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/"
+SCE = "# --- R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: the start counter fed from running-signal edges"
+DS = "from heatpump_optimizer import duty_switch as _ds_mod"
+DS_END = "# --- R10-CEILING-PROBE (#2498, #2808)"
+M = [
+ ("count-condition", "wear.py", "started, self.running = running and not self.running, running", "started, self.running = running, running"),
+ ("none-guard", "wear.py", "        if running is None:\n            return []\n", "        if False:\n            return []\n"),
+ ("queue-replay", "wear.py", "        return [at for edge in queued for at in self.fold(*edge)]", "        return []"),
+ ("queue-on-unrestored", "wear.py", "        if self.queued is not None:\n            self.queued.append((since, running))\n            return []\n", "        if False:\n            self.queued.append((since, running))\n            return []\n"),
+ ("finally-restore", "coordinator.py", "        finally:\n            self._book_starts(self._start_counter.restore(stored.get(\"starts\") if stored else None))\n", "        finally:\n            pass\n        self._book_starts(self._start_counter.restore(stored.get(\"starts\") if stored else None))\n"),
+ ("released-guard", "coordinator.py", "        if starts and not self._entry_released:\n", "        if starts:\n"),
+ ("stop-edge-save", "coordinator.py", "            self._schedule_ledger_save()\n\n    def _roll_month", "            pass\n\n    def _roll_month"),
+ ("element-instant-term", "coordinator.py", "self._immersion_active or immersion_over(kw, self._ctx._thermal_params, self._commanded_power()))))", "self._immersion_active)))"),
+ ("element-latch-term", "coordinator.py", "self._immersion_active or immersion_over(kw, self._ctx._thermal_params, self._commanded_power()))))", "immersion_over(kw, self._ctx._thermal_params, self._commanded_power()))))"),
+ ("element-both-sources", "running_signal.py", "        if sensor:\n            return resolve_reading", "        if sensor and not element(0.0 if True else 0):\n            return resolve_reading"),
+ ("element-reader-guard", "running_signal.py", "        if kw is not None and element(kw):\n", "        if False:\n"),
+ ("timer-arm", "running_signal.py", "    sig.timer = (pending, async_call_later(sig.hass, delay, _due))", "    sig.timer = None"),
+ ("timer-delay-zero", "running_signal.py", "    delay = max(0.0, wear.EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S - utc_elapsed_seconds(dt_util.now(), pending[1]))", "    delay = 0.0"),
+ ("timer-cancel-on-detach", "running_signal.py", "    if timer is not None:\n        timer[1]()\n", "    if False:\n        timer[1]()\n"),
+ ("per-refresh-reread", "running_signal.py", "    note(sig, when)\n    read = running_now(sig) is True\n", "    read = running_now(sig) is True\n"),
+ ("attach-in-init", "coordinator.py", "        running_signal.attach(running_signal.signal_for(self), *running_signal.source(", "        (lambda *a: None)(running_signal.signal_for(self), *running_signal.source("),
+ ("detach-on-release", "coordinator.py", "        running_signal.detach(running_signal.signal_for(self))\n        # #1755 r1", "        # #1755 r1"),
+ ("detach-clears-subscribers", "running_signal.py", "    sig.subscribers.clear()\n", ""),
+ ("running-now-pending", "running_signal.py", "    return sig.tracker.settled if sig.tracker.pending is None else None", "    return sig.tracker.settled"),
+ ("ds-subscribe", "duty_switch.py", "    running_signal.subscribe(rec.signal, rec.feed)", "    pass"),
+ ("ds-unsubscribe", "duty_switch.py", "    running_signal.unsubscribe(rec.signal, rec.feed)\n", ""),
+ ("ds-pass-confirm", "duty_switch.py", "    running_signal.confirm(rec.signal, when)\n", ""),
+ # S7, the refresh-held start (owner ruling D1).
+ ("hold-off", "coordinator.py", "StartCounter(hold=None if self._ctx._config.compressor_freq_sensor else RiseHold())", "StartCounter(hold=None)"),
+ ("hold-on-frequency", "coordinator.py", "StartCounter(hold=None if self._ctx._config.compressor_freq_sensor else RiseHold())", "StartCounter(hold=RiseHold())"),
+ ("hear-bypasses-hold", "coordinator.py", "            self._start_counter.hear(*edge)), lambda read:", "            self._start_counter.fold(*edge)), lambda read:"),
+ ("refresh-tick-not-subscribed", "coordinator.py", "            self._start_counter.hear(*edge)), lambda read: self._book_starts(self._start_counter.refresh(read)))", "            self._start_counter.hear(*edge)))"),
+ ("refresh-ticks-not-called", "running_signal.py", "    for tick in list(sig.ticks):\n        tick(read)\n", ""),
+ ("tick-before-note", "running_signal.py", "    note(sig, when)\n    read = running_now(sig) is True\n", "    read = running_now(sig) is True\n    note(sig, when)\n"),
+ ("refresh-reads-unsettled", "running_signal.py", "    read = running_now(sig) is True\n", "    read = True\n"),
+ ("refresh-only-note", "coordinator.py", "        running_signal.refresh(running_signal.signal_for(self), dt_util.now())\n", "        running_signal.note(running_signal.signal_for(self), dt_util.now())\n"),
+ ("detach-clears-ticks", "running_signal.py", "    sig.ticks.clear()\n", ""),
+ ("tick-subscribe-dropped", "running_signal.py", "    if tick is not None and tick not in sig.ticks:\n        sig.ticks.append(tick)\n", ""),
+ ("hold-refreshes-one", "wear.py", "HOLD_REFRESHES = 2\n", "HOLD_REFRESHES = 1\n"),
+ ("hold-refreshes-three", "wear.py", "HOLD_REFRESHES = 2\n", "HOLD_REFRESHES = 3\n"),
+ ("hold-seen-not-counted", "wear.py", "        seen += 1\n        if seen < HOLD_REFRESHES:\n", "        if seen < HOLD_REFRESHES:\n"),
+ ("hold-rose-from-any", "wear.py", "            self.held = (since, rose_from is False, 0)\n", "            self.held = (since, True, 0)\n"),
+ ("hold-rose-from-none", "wear.py", "            self.held = (since, rose_from is False, 0)\n", "            self.held = (since, False, 0)\n"),
+ ("hold-short-run-any-edge", "wear.py", "        if held is not None and held[1] and running is False:  # a short run\n", "        if held is not None and held[1]:  # a short run\n"),
+ ("hold-short-run-at-stop", "wear.py", "            return [(held[0], True), (since, running)]\n", "            return [(since, True), (since, running)]\n"),
+ ("hold-refresh-unsettled", "wear.py", "        if self.held is None or not running:\n", "        if self.held is None:\n"),
+ ("hold-release-at-refresh-time", "wear.py", "        self.held = None\n        return [(since, True)]", "        self.held = None\n        return [(since.replace(second=59), True)]"),
+ ("hold-last-not-kept", "wear.py", "        held, rose_from, self.held, self.last = self.held, self.last, None, running\n", "        held, rose_from, self.held = self.held, self.last, None\n"),
+ ("counter-refresh-off", "wear.py", "        edges = [] if self.hold is None else self.hold.refresh(running)\n", "        edges = []\n"),
+]
+
+
+BLOCK = "tools/audit/seat/features_block.py"
+ENV = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": "tests/hastub"}
+
+
+def prelude(tmp: str, marker: str, end: str | None) -> str:
+    out = os.path.join(tmp, f"prelude{abs(hash(marker))}.py")
+    subprocess.run([sys.executable, BLOCK, "--emit-prelude", out, marker] + ([end] if end else []),
+                   env=ENV, check=True, capture_output=True)
+    return out
+
+
+def run(pre: str, marker: str, end: str | None = None) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:
+    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, BLOCK, "--prelude", f"exec(open({pre!r}).read())", marker]
+                       + ([end] if end else []), capture_output=True, text=True, env=ENV, timeout=1800)
+    fails = [ln.strip()[:110] for ln in r.stdout.splitlines() if ln.startswith("  FAIL")]
+    return fails, ("Traceback" in r.stdout + r.stderr and not fails)
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        blocks = [(prelude(tmp, SCE, None), SCE, None), (prelude(tmp, DS, DS_END), DS, DS_END)]
+        base = [run(*b) for b in blocks]
+        print("BASELINE", [(len(f), crash) for f, crash in base], flush=True)
+        if any(f or crash for f, crash in base):
+            print("RESULT survived=unmeasured (the unmutated tree fails a block)")
+            return 1
+        survived = 0
+        for name, f, old, new in M:
+            path = pathlib.Path(P + f)
+            src = path.read_text()
+            if src.count(old) != 1:
+                print(f"STALE    {name}: its line is not in {f} exactly once")
+                survived += 1
+                continue
+            path.write_text(src.replace(old, new))
+            try:
+                out = [run(*b) for b in blocks]
+            finally:
+                path.write_text(src)
+            killed = any(fl or crash for fl, crash in out)
+            survived += not killed
+            print(f"{'KILLED  ' if killed else 'SURVIVED'} {name}: "
+                  + ", ".join(f"{len(fl)} fail{' +raise' if crash else ''}" for fl, crash in out), flush=True)
+            for ln in (out[0][0] + out[1][0])[:2]:
+                print("        ", ln, flush=True)
+        print(f"RESULT survived={survived}")
+        return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SETPOINT-LATCH-DEADLOCK.md b/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SETPOINT-LATCH-DEADLOCK.md

index 0000000000..bafc5310b9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SETPOINT-LATCH-DEADLOCK.md
@@ -0,0 +1,442 @@
+# R10-RCA-SETPOINT-LATCH-DEADLOCK: the off restore's own-write refusal held the space write with no release
+
+This is the root-cause seat for R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK. It follows
+`dev/governance/roles/root-cause.md` and `dev/governance/rules/defect-root-cause.md`.
+It ran beside that fixer, never inside it, and edits nothing under
+`custom_components/` or `tests/`.
+
+- **Trigger:** 1. The defect reached released versions: v7.1.12 (`4596f721f6`,
+  stamped 2026-11-12T10:48Z) and every later tag, since the code is unchanged at
+  `origin/main` `154dbb4c61` (2026-11-13T16:30Z).
+- **Introduced by:** PR #3404 (R10-ARBITER-OFF-RESTORE), merge `1aeaf273a4`. The
+  hold is in its first commit, `413cbb3c90` (2026-11-10).
+- **The fix:** not read. The fixer's branch had not been pushed when this
+  analysis was written. Section 5 says what its head still owes.
+- **Reproduction:** `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_setpoint_latch.py`.
+
+## Result
+
+- **Cause.** The off restore must not take the optimizer's own last write as
+  the person's baseline. `_arm_space` enforces that by refusing the write
+  itself, not only the capture. On an install upgraded from a version without
+  the restore, the persisted record (`ArbiterState.written`, restored by
+  `_load`) equals what the pump reads, usually the idle gate `FLOW_GATE_C`
+  (25). So every space set-point write is refused, boost's included. Only a
+  person can release it: an edit at the pump, or Optimizer active turned off
+  and on again. A restart does not release it.
+- **Process state: (a).** No contract asks that a refusal on an actuator write
+  have a release that needs no person. The upgrade path was not missed: the
+  fixer drove it, tested it, documented it and disclosed it, and the reviewer
+  named it in a verdict. Every seat judged the hold against the stated intent,
+  and the stated intent included the hold. No person accepted the consequence:
+  both owner-account approvals were agent approvals under mandate.
+- **Cost test.** The proposed detector costs about 1 s per run. The policy
+  line costs about 20 min of reviewer time per 30 days. The defect costs at
+  least about 6 h of programme time per occurrence (estimate), plus a house
+  without heat until someone acts. One escape in 30 days of the round. Both
+  countermeasures pass.
+- **Countermeasure.**
+  - Built: the detector, as a hand-run harness. It exits 1 at v7.1.12, at
+    main and at #3404's first commit. It exits 0 at v7.1.11 (the null
+    control) and on a candidate fix. It exits 2 on a tree that writes nothing.
+    6 of 6 hand mutants are killed.
+  - Proposed: the same invariant inside `tests/features.py`, which is the
+    fixer's or main's to land.
+  - Proposed to the owner (policy): one line in `fix-review.md` and one in
+    `fixer.md`.
+  - Recorded refusal: a stamp-time rule for release notes about user action.
+- **Audit class.** No class in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` matches.
+  This is the first instance of the shape, so no class barrier is owed.
+
+## 1. The cause, verified
+
+### The code
+
+At v7.1.12, `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py`:
+
+- `_write` (`:1464-1488`) calls `_held_back` before any service call (`:1473`).
+- `_held_back` (`:1506-1515`) ends with
+  `return slot == "space_setpoint" and not await _arm_space(...)`.
+- `_arm_space` (`:1518-1541`) computes `own`:
+  - the key is not armed, or it is armed on another entity;
+  - and the last record, `written["space_setpoint"]` or else
+    `dropped["space_setpoint"]`, exists;
+  - and the reading does not differ from it.
+- When `own` is true, `_arm_space` logs once through `log_held` with "not
+  writing it until it is set at the controller", then `return False`. That
+  return is the hold.
+
+At `origin/main` `154dbb4c61`, the same functions are at `:1596-1631`, with the
+same logic. `git diff v7.1.12 origin/main -- pump_arbiter.py` changes 257 lines
+of the file, none of them in `own` or its return.
+
+### Why it bites on upgrade
+
+- `_load` (`:1922-1942`) restores `written` from the store, filtered only by
+  `_writable`. The record from before v7.1.12 is therefore present.
+- Since v7.1.12, `armed` comes from `off_restore`'s store, so it is None on
+  every upgraded install.
+- `hold` (`:1388-1409`) rewrites any reading that differs from the record.
+  That makes reading equal to record the steady state of every Control
+  install. On an install that was idle at upgrade, the value is the gate,
+  25 °C.
+
+### What releases the hold
+
+All four exits were checked against the code. Only the first two release it,
+and both need a person.
+
+| exit | releases? | evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| a person sets a different value at the pump | yes | `hold` deletes the record when the reading differs (`:1405`). The next `_arm_space` sees no own value and arms with the person's value. This is the only release `docs/configuration.md:876-879` names ("set it on the pump once"). |
+| Optimizer active Off, then on again (or duty mode away from Control) | yes | `_arbitrate` (`:1649`) → `_forget` (`:1655-1658`, `:1446-1447`) clears `written` and `dropped`. **Code-read, not measured:** the next arm then captures the reading, 25, as the person's baseline. That is the exact capture the refusal exists to prevent. Undocumented. |
+| restart or reload | no | `_load` restores the same record |
+| time, retry, repair issue | no | `_arm_space` has no clock. `log_held` logs once per transition. No issue is raised. |
+
+### Reproduction
+
+`python3 -I dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_setpoint_latch.py --check <root>`. The
+harness drives `pump_arbiter.apply` through the same stub shape as
+`tests/features.py`'s arbiter section (`_PaCoord`): a flow set-point install,
+Control on, a plan that heats the house on every step, 0 °C outdoors, and a
+device that takes every write. All runs below were made from cwd `/tmp`. The
+harness exits 3 if the package loads from outside the named root, and no run
+exited 3.
+
+| tree | rc | states | failed |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| v7.1.11 `50e4b1aa25` (before the hold; null control) | 0 | 9 | 0 |
+| #3404 first commit `413cbb3c90` | 1 | 18 | 1 |
+| v7.1.12 `4596f721f6` | 1 | 36 | 4 |
+| origin/main `154dbb4c61` | 1 | 36 | 4 |
+| main + candidate fix (`_arm_space`'s `return False` → `return True`: refuse the capture, not the write) | 0 | 36 | 0 |
+| main + skip control (`_write` returns first) | 2 | – | – |
+
+The state count differs by tree because two axes depend on the tree:
+`dropped` exists only from `da4ecec213`, and `CONSUMER` only from #3404.
+
+Each failure ends with the entity reading 25 after 10 passes, against a
+demanded 55. The failing states at v7.1.12 and main:
+
+- `written=25 dropped=None reading=25 armed=False`: the upgrade case;
+- `written=None dropped=25 reading=25 armed=False`;
+- `written=25 dropped=25 reading=25 armed=False`;
+- `written=55 dropped=25 reading=25 armed=False`. Here `hold` drops the 55
+  record against the 25 reading, and the dropped 25 then holds. Whether a live
+  install reaches this state was not verified.
+
+The scratch run behind the first report to the orchestrator used the same
+upgrade state with longer horizons:
+
+- 600 one-minute passes at the gate: `space_writes=0 entity_now=25`;
+- the null control (reading 31): `space_writes=1 first=[55]`;
+- a fresh coordinator on the same entry id after 5 passes, which loads the
+  record from the store: `space_writes=0 record=(25.0, ...)`;
+- Off then Auto: `[55, 55]`.
+
+Not verified:
+
+- the boost ceiling path. Boost's write goes through the same `_write` →
+  `_held_back` (`:1502` at main), so the same refusal reaches it, but no boost
+  was driven;
+- the owner's install itself.
+
+### Which side moved
+
+The tests did not drift into the hold. They were written with it, as its
+specification:
+
+- `tests/features.py:63599` `_pa_upgraded` (blamed to `413cbb3c90`) starts
+  from a persisted record of 30 and runs 2 passes. It asserts
+  `_pa_up_first == []`, so the write is refused.
+- Its title says the write "waits". No check asserts that the wait ends.
+
+The fix must invert this check.
+
+## 2. The process state: (a)
+
+**(a) The process did not exist.** No contract asks for the property the
+defect broke: a refusal on an actuator write path must have a release that
+needs no person.
+
+What each seat had, and did:
+
+1. **The brief.** It was written by roster op `fac0e80098` (2026-11-07,
+   "roster_edit batch of 6") and says: "Refuse to capture a value equal to the
+   arbiter's own last write." It refuses the capture and says nothing on
+   whether the write proceeds.
+   - The owner's ruling (#201 comment 6708225978) is only "Arbiter too", and
+     leaves the baseline to "the building group's work". The refusal line is
+     the brief writer's, not the owner's.
+   - `architect_note` is empty and the group is size M, so no designer ran.
+2. **The fixer drove the upgrade state and chose the hold knowingly.**
+   - PR #3404's body, line 5: "`_arm_space` refuses a first capture whose
+     reading equals the arbiter's own last write ..., latched once per entity,
+     and holds the write until the controller reads anything else."
+   - `docs/configuration.md:876-879`: "after an upgrade from a version
+     without this, the set-point is not written until it reads anything else,
+     so set it on the pump once."
+   - `fixer.md:54-56` ("A learner or guard change is measured at both ends of
+     its input range") was obeyed: `_pa_upgraded` is the upgraded end.
+   - Neither the body nor the docs state what the pump does meanwhile. It
+     stays at the last write, the idle gate on an idle install.
+3. **The fix reviewer saw it and pushed the other way.**
+   - The blocked verdict `e76038aacc` (`review/3404`, VERDICT.md:14) says: "on
+     an upgrade with the loop active ... The write stays held until a person
+     changes the controller."
+   - The review blocked because the hold could leak, letting the optimizer's
+     own value be captured. Repair round 3 (`da4ecec213`, `4831cb404f`) made
+     the latch survive run ends (`ArbiterState.dropped`). That widened the set
+     of states that enter it: three of the four failing states above need
+     `dropped`.
+   - The final verdict, `5b85bdeaa0`, was "Fix review: merge" at `aa70efdd`.
+4. **No person accepted it.**
+   - Both approvals by the owner's account (2026-11-11T03:35Z at `561edf4c`,
+     19:59Z at `212e3fc7`) read "Agent approval (the orchestrator, not tvofi
+     in person) ... under mandate 6715477401".
+   - The two `hpo-approver` approvals are bot approvals on the verdict.
+5. **The release note did not carry it.** The v7.1.12 entry for #3404
+   (`RELEASE_NOTES.md`, "Turning the optimizer off restores the pump's space
+   set-point") has no line about the upgrade. The config-flow help at
+   v7.1.12 (`strings.json:595`, `translations/en.json:595`) still reads "Used
+   only to notice when the entity cannot be read. The optimizer never writes a
+   recommended space set-point."
+6. **The contracts.** `git grep -n -i -E "liveness|latch|deadlock|upgrade|actuator"`
+   over `fix-review.md` and `designer.md` returns nothing. In `fixer.md` the
+   only match is `:231` (actuator writes belong in the coordinator or
+   `pump_arbiter.py`, a layering rule).
+   - `D1.md` hunts "turns a corrupt input into a permanent failure". Its store
+     fuzz (step 2) mutates corrupt payloads, not a valid payload from a
+     previous version.
+   - Round 10's D1 audit predates this PR in any case.
+
+**Why not (b).** No rule was disobeyed. The guard edge was measured, the body
+disclosed the hold, and the docs named the person's action.
+
+**Why not (c).** The processes that ran (guard-edge measurement, adversarial
+review) work against the fix's stated intent, and here they produced what
+that intent asked for. The missing piece is the criterion: a refusal must
+end without a person. No process holds that criterion, so a firmer version of
+any existing step would have been obeyed with the same outcome. The nearest
+existing control has the right property in another unit: P5's barrier, "the
+#1524 liveness checks refusing a gate that refuses everything", covers sysid
+adoption gates. Nothing extended it to actuator writes. That is an absent
+process for this unit, not a misfiring one.
+
+**Why not (d).** No precondition changed. The hold was born with its
+human-only release in `413cbb3c90`.
+
+## 3. How far the class reaches
+
+**Rule.** Every hold condition on an actuator write in the three write-owning
+modules this round touched: each `log_held(` site whose true branch skips a
+write. For each, ask what ends it on a valid configuration.
+
+- Enumerator: `git grep -n 'log_held(' -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_arbiter.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/heat_curve.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/off_restore.py`.
+- It prints 17 lines at `154dbb4c61` and none at v7.0.0.
+- `_held_back`'s two non-`log_held` refusals were read too.
+
+| site (main) | refusal | release |
+|---|---|---|
+| `pump_arbiter.py:1625` `_arm_space` | the record equals the reading, key not armed | **a person only: this defect** |
+| `pump_arbiter.py` `_held_back` retry | retry not due | time (`RETRY_MINUTES`) |
+| `pump_arbiter.py` `_held_back` mode domain | mode entity of a read-only domain | configuration; intended, the slot cannot be written |
+| `pump_arbiter.py:644` | indoor set-point whose minimum exceeds the room target | configuration fault, warned |
+| `heat_curve.py:366`, `:504` | entity not a number, no target | configuration fault, warned |
+| `heat_curve.py:376`, `:551` | "not resent until the target changes" | automatic: the plan moves the target |
+| `heat_curve.py:383` | 24 h write cap | time (the deque drains) |
+| `off_restore.py:185` | no readable baseline | automatic: the entity becomes readable |
+| `off_restore.py:215`, `:248` | a restore not sent | retried on the next restore |
+
+**Reach.** One site in about ten holds an actuator write on a valid
+configuration until a person acts, and that site is this defect.
+
+**Escape record.** `RELEASE_NOTES.md` v7.1.0 to v7.1.15 (16 stamps) has no
+other escape of this shape. The nearest is #3497's "no longer refused", which
+was a wrong value, not a held write.
+
+**Register.** No class in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` (61 entries)
+has this mechanism. The nearest are:
+
+- P5, whose barrier carries the liveness check for gates;
+- R9-ROW-STALE, "a record guard refuses the exact rewrite the record beat
+  exists to perform", an instrument class.
+
+As a single instance, it owes no barrier under `defect-root-cause.md`'s
+audit-class clause. Minting a class is the judge's call, not this seat's.
+
+## 4. The cost test
+
+    cost(countermeasure, recurring) < cost(defect) x P(recurrence)
+
+Units are wall-clock, per occurrence, over 30 days (the round's span from
+v7.0.0, 2026-10-14, to now).
+
+**cost(defect).**
+
+| measure | value | basis |
+|---|---|---|
+| released exposure | v7.1.12 stamp (2026-11-12T10:48Z) to 2026-11-13T16:30Z, about 30 h and counting; the fix is not released | tag date, `date -u` |
+| affected installs | every Control install with a space set-point entity, upgraded with reading equal to record, which is the steady state `hold` enforces | code-read; the install count is not known |
+| user harm | the pump holds the last write, the gate on an idle install: the owner's house at 16 °C at 0 °C outdoors | the brief's report; not re-measured |
+| programme cost | a hotfix fixer, its review, this seat, a stamp: at least about 6 h | estimate; no fix PR existed to time |
+
+**P(recurrence).** No measured class frequency exists. The round's record
+holds one escape:
+
+- about 30 actuator-module merges in 30 days
+  (`git log --first-parent origin/main --since=2026-10-14 -- pump_arbiter.py heat_curve.py off_restore.py boost.py supply_hold.py | wc -l` = 30);
+- about 10 new hold sites in those modules (section 3).
+
+The estimate is 0.3 to 1 per 30 days.
+
+**Expected defect cost:** 0.3 × 6 h = 1.8 h, up to 6 h, per 30 days, before
+any user harm.
+
+**cost(countermeasure, recurring).**
+
+- **The invariant in `tests/features.py`.**
+  - Measured: the harness's 36 states × 10 passes take 0.8 to 0.9 s of CPU
+    end to end, imports included (`time`, single tree). Inside
+    `features.py` the imports are already paid.
+  - At 100 selected runs a day, that is under 50 min of CI time per 30 days,
+    with no seat time. It **passes**.
+- **One review line** (section 5).
+  - About 2 min per pull request that adds a refusal on an actuator write.
+  - Of about 30 actuator-module merges per 30 days, an estimated third add one:
+    about 20 min per 30 days. It **passes**.
+- **A stamp-time release-note rule.**
+  - `stamp.py` would refuse a note that omits a PR's declared user action.
+  - Upkeep: a new PR-body field and a parser.
+  - Benefit: none here. The hold was disclosed in the docs and the body, and a
+    note saying "set it on the pump once" would still have left every
+    upgraded house unheated until someone read it. The defect is the
+    behaviour, not its announcement.
+  - It **fails** on benefit, and is refused (section 5).
+- **An upgrade-path fixture** (a previous release's store loaded and run). Its
+  states are a subset of the invariant's. It adds nothing.
+
+## 5. Countermeasures
+
+### Built: the detector, shown failing and passing
+
+`dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_setpoint_latch.py --check <root>` is the detector.
+Its results are the table in section 1:
+
+- rc 1 on the defect: v7.1.12, main and `413cbb3c90`;
+- rc 0 on the null control (v7.1.11) and on a candidate fix;
+- rc 2 on a skip tree that writes nothing;
+- rc 3 on a provenance refusal.
+
+The candidate fix shows that the detector turns green on a fix. It is not
+offered as the fix. It drops the refusal of the write and keeps the refusal of
+the capture. The fixer's design may differ, and the detector is owed a run on
+the fixer's head before merge: the fix review's to run.
+
+**Mutation proof.** The harness is under `dev/` and outside `mutant_run.py`,
+so it was mutated by hand. The scored command requires all of:
+
+- rc 1 at v7.1.12, run from the candidate-fix tree;
+- rc 0 at the candidate fix, run from the v7.1.12 tree;
+- rc 2 on the skip tree;
+- rc 0 at v7.1.11;
+- rc 1 at `413cbb3c90`.
+
+Unmutated, it passes. 6 of 6 mutants are killed:
+
+| mutant | edit | scored rcs (tag, fix, skip, v7.1.11, r1) |
+|---|---|---|
+| Ma | the verdict becomes `return 0` | 0 0 2 0 0 |
+| Mb | the gate dropped from the `written` axis | 1 0 2 0 0 (killed by `413cbb3c90`, which has no `dropped` axis) |
+| Mc | the skip guard becomes `if False:` | 1 0 1 0 1 |
+| Md | the comparison becomes `final != final` | 0 0 2 0 0 |
+| Me | the gate dropped from the reading axis | 0 0 2 0 0 |
+| Mf | `os.chdir(root)` removed | 1 0 2 1 1 (v7.1.11 reads package data relative to the cwd) |
+
+Mb survived until `413cbb3c90` was added to the score. On trees with
+`dropped`, the dropped-gate state covers the same latch.
+
+### Proposed: the invariant in `tests/features.py`
+
+The harness's loop belongs beside the arbiter section's off-restore checks.
+For the fixer of R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK, or main:
+
+- **The invariant:** from every persisted state, the entity reads the
+  demanded target within N passes, with no person acting.
+- **Its null control:** the reference install is written.
+- **It replaces** `_pa_upgraded`'s "the write waits" assertion, which pins the
+  defect.
+
+It addresses the seam, not the state. It is a test and needs no owner
+approval.
+
+### Proposed to the owner (policy): the missing process, state (a)
+
+These are policy changes, owner-gated, or under a mandate scoped `all`. They
+are drafted here and not landed.
+
+- **`fix-review.md`, a new step:**
+  > **A new refusal on an actuator write names its release.** Where the diff
+  > adds a path that skips a write the plan demands (a hold, a latch, a
+  > refusal that returns before the service call), the body names what ends
+  > it on a valid configuration, and a check drives the refusal's entry state
+  > (persisted state from the previous release included) to that end. A
+  > release that needs a person to act at the pump, or to toggle the
+  > optimizer, is `blocked` unless the owner, in person, accepted it on the
+  > pull request.
+- **`fixer.md` step 3, one sentence after "measured at both ends of its input
+  range":**
+  > A guard that refuses an actuator write is also driven from the previous
+  > release's persisted state, and its release needs no person.
+
+Together these supply the criterion that every seat lacked in section 2. The
+"in person" clause addresses item 4 there: mandate approvals carried the hold
+without a person seeing it.
+
+### Recorded refusal
+
+The stamp-time release-note rule is refused (section 4). Its benefit is not
+in this defect's causal path.
+
+## 6. Carries
+
+These are findings outside this seat's edit scope, routed by
+`finding-propagation.md`, for the orchestrator to place in
+R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK's brief (a live group):
+
+- **`_pa_upgraded` pins the defect.** `tests/features.py:63599-63622` asserts
+  that the write waits, and the fix must invert it.
+  Carry: R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK
+- **The Off-and-on release captures the optimizer's own value.** `_forget`
+  clears the record, so the next arm takes the reading (the gate) as the
+  baseline. This was found by code-read and not measured. A fix that keeps any
+  hold should close it; one that drops the hold should say what the restore
+  writes on an install armed with the gate.
+  Carry: R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK
+- **A second entry into the latch.** `written=55 dropped=25 reading=25`:
+  `hold` drops the 55 record, and the dropped 25 then holds (section 1).
+  Reachability on a live install was not verified.
+  Carry: R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK
+- **The config-flow help text.** `strings.json:595` and the translations still
+  say "Used only to notice when the entity cannot be read. The optimizer never
+  writes a recommended space set-point." `pump_duty_mode`'s help (`:1274`)
+  says Control writes the entity. Class I5.
+  Carry: R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK
+- **Docs.** `docs/configuration.md:876-879` ("set it on the pump once")
+  describes the defect as behaviour.
+  Carry: R10-HOTFIX-FLOW-SETPOINT-STUCK
+- **The defect's issue.** `defect-root-cause.md` asks for a short **Root
+  cause** section on the defect's own issue. No issue is on record, and this
+  seat makes no GitHub write. Placing that section is the orchestrator's: state
+  (a), the cost-test verdict and this path.
+
+## Reproduce
+
+    git worktree add --detach /tmp/v7111 v7.1.11
+    git worktree add --detach /tmp/v7112 v7.1.12
+    git worktree add --detach /tmp/r1 413cbb3c90
+    H="$PWD/dev/audit/harnesses/r10_rca_setpoint_latch.py"
+    (cd /tmp && python3 -I "$H" --check /tmp/v7111)   # rc 0, 9 states
+    (cd /tmp && python3 -I "$H" --check /tmp/r1)      # rc 1, 1 of 18
+    (cd /tmp && python3 -I "$H" --check /tmp/v7112)   # rc 1, 4 of 36
+    (cd /tmp && python3 -I "$H" --check "$PWD")       # rc 1 at main until the fix

--- a/dev/governance/config/corpus_excluded.json

@@ -1,8 +1,9 @@
 {
- "_comment": "Round-evidence exclusions for the named-docs check, in the shape .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json takes (a top-level object of keyed entries beside a _comment). policy_lint.mjs merges `excluded` into its CORPUS_EXCLUDED set at load, so each entry here is a named document the corpus cites -- COMMON.md's report-shape line names REPORT.md, fixer.md's baseline line names BASELINE.md -- that holds a finder report, a round baseline or other data a later seat reads rather than policy prose -- or, for `docs/index.html` (the product page D6.md names), a user-facing page, on the ground policy_lint.mjs's own CORPUS_EXCLUDED holds README.md and DISCLAIMER.md as `user-facing`. A `.md` is never excused by location, so they are excluded one by one rather than by prefix. Or, for `tools/audit/seat/beatd_shims/git`, an executable and not a document: the beat jobs' git shim, which must be named `git` to be found on PATH, so the bare-name pass resolves every policy sentence's word `git` to it. Or, for `dev/README.md`, the developer onboarding: it states no policy and binds the reader to CLAUDE.md, while it names the tree's tools and contracts by bare name throughout; excluded by 7ae69419e (R10-ARCH-DOCS-FIRST), and dropped when policy_lint.mjs's resolveCited canon lookup lands.",
+ "_comment": "Round-evidence exclusions for the named-docs check, in the shape .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json takes (a top-level object of keyed entries beside a _comment). policy_lint.mjs merges `excluded` into its CORPUS_EXCLUDED set at load, so each entry here is a named document the corpus cites -- COMMON.md's report-shape line names REPORT.md, fixer.md's baseline line names BASELINE.md -- that holds a finder report, a round baseline or other data a later seat reads rather than policy prose -- or, for `docs/index.html` (the product page D6.md names), a user-facing page, on the ground policy_lint.mjs's own CORPUS_EXCLUDED holds README.md and DISCLAIMER.md as `user-facing`. A `.md` is never excused by location, so they are excluded one by one rather than by prefix. Or, for `tools/audit/seat/beatd_shims/git`, an executable and not a document: the beat jobs' git shim, which must be named `git` to be found on PATH, so the bare-name pass resolves every policy sentence's word `git` to it. Or, for `dev/README.md`, the developer onboarding: it states no policy and binds the reader to CLAUDE.md, while it names the tree's tools and contracts by bare name throughout; excluded by 7ae69419e (R10-ARCH-DOCS-FIRST), and dropped when policy_lint.mjs's resolveCited canon lookup lands. Or, for `dev/programme/RULINGS.md`, the owner's standing rulings, excluded by tvofi's own ruling of 2026-11-15: \"This file should be excluded by the corpus but still needs to be re-read on changes, just like instruments.md\" -- the liveness hook re-reads it by change after a compaction, as it does the instrument pages.",
  "_why_data_not_source": "These entries must be DATA and not a hardcoded block inside .claude/workflows/policy_lint.mjs. The `policy-docs` job's 'Restore the check source from the base commit' step (#1403) rewrites `.claude/workflows/*.mjs` and `*.py` from the base commit before grading, so a round that ships its evidence files and their exclusions in one branch would have the exclusions erased on CI and fail named-docs; pre-registering them first is refused as FIXTURE VACUOUS, because an exclusion that names no tracked file yet is a destination waiting to be used. This file is outside that pathspec, so it arrives with the branch that adds the evidence it excludes -- the same shape the #1403 fix's own comment names for policy_budgets.json, policy_known_bad.json and cfr_exclusions.json: a grader's criteria are data, and a fixture's expected outcome has to be the data under test.",
  "_fail_closed": "A missing or unparseable file, or a non-array `excluded`, makes policy_lint.mjs merge nothing, and the cited-but-unexcluded evidence files then re-arm named-docs on the production run -- so this list cannot silently drop an entry; the check that consumes it notices.",
  "excluded": [
+  "dev/programme/RULINGS.md",
   "dev/archive/README.md",
   "docs/index.html",
   "dev/audit/rounds/round10/D0/s1/REPORT.md",

+# D10 acceptance criteria: platinum, rule by rule
+
+> Adherence to home assistant integration platinum quality requirements.
+
+— the owner, `D10.md`. The tier is the owner's and `manifest.json` already
+declares it; the register is `quality_scale.yaml` in the integration.
+
+Drafted by a fixer seat under mandate 6893738184 (scope all);
+binding as the owner's words until the owner rewrites them.
+A finding names the statement it fails.
+
+- **Q1 the register.** Every rule of bronze, silver, gold and platinum on
+  Home Assistant's current checklist (`D10.md` step 1) has a row, and every
+  row reads `done` or `exempt`; every `exempt` row carries a `comment`
+  stating why the rule cannot apply. Command, printing each row that fails:
+
+      python3 -c "import yaml,sys;r=yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))['rules'];\
+      [print(k,v) for k,v in r.items() if (v if isinstance(v,str) else v['status']) not in ('done','exempt')\
+      or (not isinstance(v,str) and v['status']=='exempt' and not str(v.get('comment','')).strip())\
+      or (v=='exempt')]" custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/quality_scale.yaml
+
+  Pass: no line, and no checklist rule missing a row. Fail: either.
+- **Q2 every site.** A `done` row holds at every site the rule reaches, not
+  at one: every entity, platform, service, flow step, raise and log site the
+  rule's page names. Procedure: `D10.md` step 1's check per rule, run over
+  the enumeration of those sites. Fail: one site that breaks the rule, which
+  makes its row's `done` false.
+- **Q3 exemptions stay true.** An `exempt` row's reason is still true of the
+  code. Fail: the reason contradicted (an exempt discovery row beside a
+  discovery mechanism, for example).

+# D4 acceptance criteria: the card and the config flow
+
+> UI/UX — the card and the config flow, including grouping and setup
+> ergonomics. It should be intuitive, user friendly and look professional.
+
+— the owner, `D4.md`. Each statement below quotes the words it tests.
+
+Drafted by a fixer seat under mandate 6893738184 (scope all);
+binding as the owner's words until the owner rewrites them.
+A finding names the statement it fails.
+
+Surfaces: every state `node tests/card_drift.mjs --list` prints, at the
+viewports, themes, languages and input modes `D4.md` step 1 names; every
+config-flow and options page; every input of every `blueprints/` file.
+
+## "look professional"
+
+- **P1 no collision.** Overlap of two text boxes, and text past its own box,
+  measured with `getBoundingClientRect`. Pass: 0 px in every surface. Fail:
+  more than 0.5 px anywhere.
+- **P2 contrast.** WCAG 2.2 AA from `getComputedStyle` colours: 4.5:1 for
+  body text, 3:1 for text at 24 px or 18.66 px bold and for chart marks.
+  Fail: one pair below its ratio.
+- **P3 one look.** A series keeps one colour across states within a theme;
+  headline numbers in one row share font size and baseline (±0.5 px). Fail:
+  either differs between two states or two cells.
+- **P4 clean console.** Fail: any console error or uncaught exception.
+
+## "user friendly"
+
+- **F1 hit targets.** Every interactive element is at least 24×24 px, 44×44
+  px under the coarse pointer. Fail: one smaller.
+- **F2 keyboard.** Tab reaches every focusable in visual order with a
+  visible focus ring. Fail: one unreachable, out of order or unmarked.
+- **F3 errors say what to change.** Every validation error key has a string
+  in every `translations/*.json`, naming the field and an accepted value or
+  range. Fail: a missing key, or a string that names neither.
+- **F4 help for every term.** Every field whose label holds a unit, an
+  acronym or a physics term carries a `data_description` in every language.
+  Fail: one without.
+
+## "intuitive"
+
+- **I1 one theme per page.** A page's fields answer the question its title
+  asks; related fields sit adjacent or in one section. Fail: a field another
+  page's title claims, or a related pair split by an unrelated field.
+- **I2 answerable defaults.** On the shortest path from adding the
+  integration to the first plan, every required field has a default or is an
+  entity or area picker. Fail: a required free value with neither. The
+  finding states the path's page count as a measurement.
+- **I3 blueprint inputs.** Every input has a name and a description, and a
+  default where one is safe. Fail: one without.

+# D5 acceptance criteria: docs structure and code comments
+
+> Docs structure, flow and content. Verify claims in docs.
+> Comments in code should be concise but precise and easy to understand.
+
+— the owner, `D5.md`. Claims in docs are D6's (`D6.md`).
+
+Drafted by a fixer seat under mandate 6893738184 (scope all);
+binding as the owner's words until the owner rewrites them.
+A finding names the statement it fails.
+
+Comment units: what `python3 tools/audit/text_ledger.py units --dim D5`
+lists for the seat's cells.
+
+## Comments: "concise but precise and easy to understand"
+
+- **C1 precise: true.** Every unit is true of the code it sits on, shown by
+  an executed check of that code (`D5.md` step 4). Fail: a unit the check
+  contradicts.
+- **C2 precise: resolvable.** Every identifier, path and issue a unit names
+  exists (`git grep -n` at the ref, `git ls-files`), and every quantity
+  carries its unit or names a dimensionless quantity. Fail: one that does not.
+- **C3 concise: no restatement.** Delete the unit; if every fact it stated
+  is readable from the identifiers and literals of the statement it sits on,
+  it restated that statement. Fail: such a unit.
+- **C4 concise: why over history.** Split a unit's sentences into those
+  stating a reason, constraint or unit and those recounting history (who
+  measured, which round, what the code used to do). Fail: history sentences
+  are more than half of the unit and deleting them loses no reason or
+  constraint.
+- **C5 easy to understand.** No sentence over 40 words; a term the unit
+  needs is defined in it, in the code it sits on, or in a document it names.
+  Fail: a longer sentence, or an undefined term a reader of the code alone
+  cannot resolve.
+
+## "Docs structure, flow and content"
+
+- **S1 reader paths.** The three paths of `D5.md` step 1 reach their goal.
+  Fail: a dead end, a forward reference, or a needed fact found nowhere.
+- **S2 links.** Every internal link and anchor resolves; every external link
+  answers below HTTP 400. Fail: one that does not.
+- **S3 one home per fact.** No paragraph appears twice across `README.md` and
+  `docs/*.md` (hash of its whitespace-normalised text). Fail: a repeat.

+# D9 acceptance criteria: the Pi-class budget per cost centre
+
+> CPU and memory resource efficiency — target hardware is
+> Raspberry-Pi-class running all of Home Assistant. Measure, don't assert
+> [...] and whether the stress budget should become a real gate
+
+— the owner, `D9.md`. Each cost centre is a metric `D9.md` defines, measured
+by its harness there.
+
+Drafted by a fixer seat under mandate 6893738184 (scope all);
+binding as the owner's words until the owner rewrites them.
+A finding names the statement it fails.
+
+`tests/stress_budgets.json` records the code's own peaks per scenario so
+that `tests/stress.py` can see a regression against them; it is no budget.
+A cost under its recorded row and over a budget here fails; a cost over its
+row and inside every budget here is a regression, not a D9 finding.
+
+## The Pi extrapolation
+
+CPU is measured on the seat's host, pinned to one core with BLAS threads at
+one (`D9.md`, Traps), and multiplied by **F**, the time of
+`tests/stress.py`'s `reference_solve` on one Raspberry Pi 4 core over its
+time on the host. Until a seat measures F on Pi-class hardware, F = 5,
+an assumption (Cortex-A72 at 1.5 GHz against a current desktop core) the
+finding states as one. Bytes are not scaled.
+
+## Budgets (CPU figures are Pi seconds, after F)
+
+- **B1 solver CPU per cycle**: the sum over a cycle's full solves of their
+  process CPU, at most 60 s: a tenth of one core over the shortest
+  optimisation interval the options flow accepts (10 min). Fail: above.
+- **B2 longest GIL hold** on the event loop thread: at most 100 ms, the
+  interval asyncio reports as a slow callback. Fail: above.
+- **B3 loop-thread work per cycle**: at most 0.5 s. Fail: above.
+- **B4 retained growth**: the retained-bytes slope after 200 warm-up cycles,
+  times the 52,560 cycles of a year at the shortest interval, at most 10 MiB
+  (199 bytes per cycle). Fail: above.
+- **B5 memory peak**: per solve, `rss_attrib_mb` as `tests/stress.py`
+  measures it at most 32 MB and the solving process's `rss_peak_mb` at most
+  128 MB. Fail: either above.
+- **B6 payload**: each entity's recorded attributes at most 16,384 bytes of
+  JSON (the recorder's own limit), and all recorded attribute bytes at most
+  5 MB per day at the shortest interval. Fail: either above.
+- **B7 gradient cost**: simulate-step-equivalents per gradient evaluation
+  at most the horizon's step count per simulated trajectory (the owner's
+  "96 ... not ~9,300" at the default horizon). Fail: above.
+
+Full solves per cycle carry no budget of their own: B1 prices them.

deleted file mode 100644
index e0b5636ac5..0000000000
--- a/dev/governance/roles/nudge.md
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,115 +0,0 @@
-# The orchestrator nudge
-
-This file binds the Cursor orchestrators on grok and qwen. Any other agent uses it as the reference for a timer, a heartbeat, and one turn's scan. The role contract is `dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md`. This file is the turn that contract names.
-
-Run the numbered steps every turn, in order. Do not stop the turn on a log line, a pending check, or a sentence that names work nobody is doing.
-
-A live timer may add three things, and only for that session: a dated owner mandate, seat identifiers that must not be resumed, and one pull request held open. Re-measure those. They are not copied here: a date or seat id would outlive its session.
-
-This programme keeps seat worktrees under `~/hpo-seats`. A reader on another machine substitutes the root its own dispatch names. The same holds for the state mirror and sync scratch below.
-
-## Who writes, and what stays shut
-
-You dispatch fixers, reviewers, and root-cause seats. You post verdicts, approve, merge, stamp, and update the roster, the state docs, and issue #3394 (#201's continuation). Do not hand the orchestrator role to a seat.
-
-Opus seats that die are replaced by a new Task on grok-4.7-high. Do not resume a dead Opus agent. Sonnet seats use cursor-grok-4.6-high. Haiku seats use composer-2.5.
-
-Pull requests are authored by the hpo-author App through `tools/pr/app_push.sh`. The login that reads GitHub is tvofi. The hpo-approver App posts verdicts. A code-owned path needs a tvofi review citing the session mandate. `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` refuses those paths. A merge verdict on a path that is not code-owned is approved with that script. A record pull request that only touches `dev/programme/delivery` is not code-owned. The ruleset still requires one approving review, so that record pull request is approved as tvofi and then merged.
-
-Do not push `main` with the deploy key. Do not merge with the admin flag. Do not edit `VERSION`, the manifest version, or the `RELEASE_NOTES.md` heading except through `tools/release/stamp.py`. A merge message must not close #3394. Write `Leaves #3394 open`. Never the negated form. Do not run a full `tests/derive_closures.sh` off Darwin. Use that script's single-script mode. Touch a claim file only when the branch is claiming drift. Compare a branch with three dots, never two. Run the train under `python3 -u` so its log is not block-buffered.
-
-A timer subscription dedupes by name and answers created false without replacing the prompt. Unsubscribe first, then subscribe. Do not call the two together.
-
-`--ignore-red` replaces the train's default ignore list, so name both `tests / nightly-status` and `governance / delivery-status`.
-
-## 1. Verdict and handoff
-
-Each turn, run `tools/audit/seat/bus.sh` watch once, and also fetch every open pull request head and every live `handoff/<topic>` ref. Watch-once prints only a ref that moved. A handoff already printed is still owed.
-
-For each open pull request, test whether the head contains the handoff tip. If it does not, run `tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh` this turn when a prepr slot is free and that group's fixer worktree was not written in the last 15 minutes. Run `tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh` when no pull request exists. If the push or the open refuses and no fixer is working, dispatch the fixer in this same turn. A fixer worktree with unpushed commits and no process is that handoff, not a new fixer.
-
-When the update exits 0, the printed HEAD contains the handoff. Dispatch the reviewer for that HEAD in the same turn. Do not end on a reviewer who waits.
-
-When a review ref moves, confirm that verdict when it names the contained head and carries its nonce, and post it once required checks have concluded at that head. A verdict on an ancestor is not a verdict on this head. A blocked fix review returns to the original fixer in that same turn. Do not repair the body yourself. Do not spawn a new seat for that repair. The same reviewer takes the next round. Do not update a head whose reviewer worktree under the seat root was written in the last 15 minutes.
-
-## 2. Reviewer owed
-
-This check uses the live head, not the bus line. For each open pull request whose head contains the fixer handoff, if the newest posted fix review does not name that 40-hex head, dispatch a reviewer this turn, without waiting for required checks. A head that moved since a merge verdict goes to `tools/pr/app_approve.sh --carry` first, and gets a reviewer only when the carry refuses. Do not dispatch a reviewer for a pull request whose title starts with `record:`, or for a head a fixer is still changing, or when a reviewer worktree for that pull request was written in the last 15 minutes. Do not start a second reviewer for a group that already has one. Before calling a seat stalled, read `tests/gate_lock.py`. A seat that holds the lease is not stalled.
-
-## 3. Train status, before any merge
-
-Find a live `tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py` and read its log. A live process holds every other merge. Do not merge by hand, do not arm auto-merge, and do not load a second train. An empty log, or a last line still on the ci step, is that one pull request's CI wait. Write the line and continue the scan. Do not end the turn on the train log.
-
-`TRAIN DONE` means that queue finished. Do not reload it. `TRAIN STOPPED` names the pull request, the step, and the reason. Later entries were not graded. Do not reload that queue. A head that does not contain `origin/main` after the ci step is the one restart the script names: run the train again on the pulls it had not merged. Do not restart a queue whose entries are already merged.
-
-Load a train on the hourly pitch, with `--bot-prs`, when no train is running and fewer than four preprs are running. One verdicted pull request is still a train. The record pull request merges inside the pitch, not between pitches. Verdicted means the newest posted fix review is merge for this 40-hex head, or `tools/pr/app_approve.sh` carry says the verdict carries. The train waits for CI in its own ci step, so do not wait for it. Order the queue by creation time, oldest first. Each entry carries the pull request number, the 40-hex the merge verdict names, the comment id (the comment must cite an absolute evidence path), and the issues the body intends to close.
-
-Leave out a `record:` pull request, which `--bot-prs` merges. A `*_budgets.json` or policy-path head stays in: the train routes it serial, and `--pre-flight` parks one the owner has not approved at that head (`Train.raise_hold`, `Train.policy_gate`) for step 7. Never pass `--allow-red`.
-
-The command is detached, because a background waiter dies at two hours:
-
-```
-python3 -u tools/audit/seat/merge_train.py run <queue.json> --bot-prs --pre-flight --mandate "<the session mandate cite>" --ignore-red 'tests / nightly-status' --ignore-red 'governance / delivery-status'
-```
-
-## 4. Required checks
-
-Required checks are the contexts in ruleset `main-protect-checks`. Read that ruleset every turn. The id last used to open it was 23698884. Do not trust a remembered list. `gate` is the one required check; `tests / nightly-status` and `governance / delivery-status` are not units. Pending is not a pass. DIRTY is the claim-file merge GitHub cannot run. Absorb `main` locally with the claimnotes driver.
-
-## 5. Budget files
-
-A `*_budgets.json` change never goes on the train. Merge a budget-file pull request by a mandate approval already on that head, oldest first, only when no train is running. A new head that raises a budget needs a new tvofi review citing the session mandate. A decrease is still a budgets file. Merge it directly, not on the train.
-
-## 6. Record pull requests
-
-A `record:` pull request needs no fix review and no reviewer. The nightly record beat merges it when its approver token is present, and the pitch takes it. By hand only when the beat's outcome is a `skip-` other than `skip-train-hold`: once required checks are success or skipped and no train is running, approve it as tvofi and merge it. An overlay may hold one open.
-
-## 7. Direct merge, when no train is running
-
-Direct-merge only what `--pre-flight` parked: a budgets-file or policy-path pull request whose mandate review is already on that head. Ready means required checks are success or skipped, GitHub reports it mergeable, and the newest posted fix review is merge for this head or carries. Oldest first. Anything the queue takes waits for the pitch.
-
-## 8. Prepr slots
-
-Up to four `prepr.sh` run at a time: each takes one of `tests/gate_lock.py`'s four heavy slots just before its first heavy step (a run whose heavy steps are all skipped takes none), and a fifth queues: the lease, not the tick's count, is the cap. A seat's own prepr counts. `tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh`, `tools/audit/seat/update_pr.sh`, `tools/pr/app_push.sh` and a `tests/derive_closures.sh` run each count as one. Do not recarry a branch a seat is writing. Skip a group whose fixer or reviewer worktree was written in the last 15 minutes, or whose own prepr is running. Recarry may run during a train's CI wait. It may not run while the train itself is in recarry.
-
-## 9. Conflicting or DIRTY
-
-Absorb `origin/main` into an open head only when it is DIRTY or `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` reports a conflict. A head merely behind `main` stays put. Merge-tree exit 0 and no train running: merge `origin/main` and push with `tools/pr/app_push.sh`, then `tools/pr/approve_held_runs.sh`. A content conflict stops. Name the path and return it to the fixer who owns the branch. Do not resolve it yourself.
-
-## 10. A refusal with nobody on it
-
-If a push or an open is refused and no fixer is working on that group, dispatch a fixer this turn. Do not leave the refusal for a later nudge. Do not start a second fixer for a group that already has one working. When you see yourself stating that work needs to be done and no seat is doing it, dispatch or perform that work in this turn.
-
-## 11. Stalled runs, autofix, and a red main
-
-Zero check runs is stalled zero-runs. Run `tools/pr/approve_held_runs.sh` after every App push. CodeQL on a tools-evidence diff is `tools/audit/seat/codeql-triage-poll.sh`, not a new fixer. Read the autofix summary before dispatching a fixer. `changed` means wait for the bot commit. `skip-failed-recording` means fix the script and do not re-derive. `skip-manual-repair-owed` means closures failed and the job was not under-scoped, so no bot commit is coming and the check itself is the repair. `skip-clean` means the check passed and no bot commit is coming. A selectable script with no recording is not under-scoped: add it to a derive lane or record it alone. A red `gate` on `main` outranks the queue. Revert a merge that reddened `main` only when that diff can reach the failure. Never pass `--allow-red`.
-
-## 12. After each merge
-
-`tools/audit/seat/postmerge.py` runs after every merge, from `merge_pr.sh` and from the train, and an `OWED` line it prints is the work left: rerun it with `--retry` once the cause is gone. This step keeps only what that tool cannot do. Only a decision-changing merge owes `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md` an updated-for line, in its own pull request. After a roster update, an open issue the plan does not name is scheduled, deferred, or refused. Do not file a new issue. Issues a session has already deferred stay deferred. The overlay names them.
-
-## 13. Stamps
-
-Run `tools/release/stamp.py` only when no train is waiting, the roster's stamp-unblock group is done, and the latest `ci.yml` push run's `gate` on the current `origin/main` is green. Not during a CI wait. A push-triggered green `gate` is not a nightly. `nightly-status` reads the last concluded schedule or workflow_dispatch on `main`. Do not rerun a push-triggered run as the nightly. A dependabot alert the overlay names stays open. Do not force an override the overlay forbids.
-
-## 14. Handed-off seats
-
-Do not resume a seat the session overlay names as handed off. A later refusal on another group still gets a new seat. Do not start a second fixer or reviewer while that group's worktree was written in the last 15 minutes.
-
-## 15. CI watch
-
-Each turn, read the required contexts from ruleset `main-protect-checks`, as step 4 says. For every open pull request, take the latest check run of each required context on the head oid. A conclusion of failure returns that pull request to its original fixer this turn, with the job URL and failure line, unless `merge_train.py classify <head> --pr <N>` reads it WAIT (a gate deferral). `ci-watch.sh` alerts only on a new signature, so a red it printed is still owed: the signature file is not this check. Pending, `nightly-status` and `delivery-status` are not a return. Zero check runs is stalled zero-runs: `tools/pr/approve_held_runs.sh`, not a fixer. Read the autofix summary before returning a closures or mutation failure, under the same words as step 11. Do not start a second fixer when that group's fixer worktree was written in the last 15 minutes. A pull request the overlay holds is not returned by this step.
-
-## 16. Unblocked groups
-
-Load the roster through `tools/audit/seat/roster_lib.py` at the ref `tools/audit/seat/state_docs.py` defaults. Dispatch by pull: a flow lane under its cap (A critical path 4, B product 4, C process 3, F fly-in 2) takes its eligible group of greatest critical-path depth, behind `tools/audit/seat/pr_cap.py` dispatch-gate, which enforces the total. Eligible: resume stage not-started, after-edges all done or absent, not deferred or refused, no fixer working. Brief it that group's own roster brief. Done stages are the pair `roster_lib.py` names. Register a fly-in at dispatch with `tools/audit/seat/roster_edit.py` append-group, named `R10-FLY-`. An expedite item (red main, quota exhaustion, outage, security) bypasses the caps, one at a time.
-
-## 17. State
-

-

If no sync loop is running, start one detached with `tools/audit/seat/wt_sync.sh` and the scratch at `~/hpo-orch`. Do not start a second.
-

+# The owner's standing rulings
+
+Purpose (the orchestrator's wording, confirmed by tvofi on 2026-11-15: "This is
+exactly how I see it"): this file is a holding area below policy, not a second
+rulebook. (1) An entry policy already states is dropped. (2) An entry that should
+bind every session permanently graduates into policy, or into a decision record
+when it is structural and its reasoning must be kept, and then leaves this file.
+(3) What remains is operational or temporary: the current mandate,
+round-specific direction, and preferences too fine-grained for policy. (4) The
+file should stay small and shrink over time; a growing file is a signal that
+rulings are not being promoted.
+
+Every ruling of tvofi's still in force, with its date. Quoted text is his words
+verbatim, typos kept; "as recorded" marks a ruling whose words were not kept,
+and "orchestrator's reading" marks an interpretation, never his. A ruling given
+to an orchestrator lands here in its next pull request; one superseded moves to
+the closing list, naming its successor. An entry belongs here only while no
+policy file states it (tvofi, 2026-11-15: "Also screen the rulings for overlap
+with policy, if both policy and rulings mandates something, policy is the right
+place"; "The point with this is that policy files and policy related files
+should follow good data integrity practice, no duplication, that creats risks of
+divergence"). Re-read on change after every compaction
+(`dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md` section 0).
+

diff --git a/tests/card.mjs b/tests/card.mjs
index 77765a6838..4fdf7cdbd7 100644
--- a/tests/card.mjs
+++ b/tests/card.mjs
@@ -2116,6 +2116,122 @@ const editable = () => {
     JSON.stringify(iso));
 }
 
+// #3636: a published plan reaching past the manual-plan window made "Apply this
+// plan" fail every time, because `build_override` refuses a slot starting
+// beyond now plus the window. The card trimmed at the edit floor only, so it
+// sent runs the editor itself would not let the user touch. The captured plan
+// is extended to 48 h past its first step with runs before, across, just
+// inside and past the ceiling: the published window (`applyEnd`), not the
+// zoomed visible end `editCeiling` also carries.
+{
+  const STEP = 15 * 60000;
+  const ceiling = FROZEN + 20 * HOUR;
+  const at = (h) => ceiling + h * HOUR;
+  // The forecast's `t` is local wall time with no offset, as the sensor
+  // publishes it, so extended steps are written the same way.
+  const local = (ms) => {
+    const d = new Date(ms);
+    const p = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
+    return `${d.getFullYear()}-${p(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${p(d.getDate())}` +
+      `T${p(d.getHours())}:${p(d.getMinutes())}:00`;
+  };
+  // [start, end) in hours from the ceiling, per channel.
+  const runs = {
+    dhw_power: [[-4, -3], [-2, 0.5], [1, 2], [4, 6]],
+    // Starts one step short of the ceiling: inside it on this clock, but past
+    // the server's on a browser clock a step ahead -- the skew allowance.
+    space_power: [[-4, -3], [-0.25, 1], [4, 6]],
+  };
+  const extended = (windowHours, seeded = runs) => {
+    const st = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(slotStates));
+    const first = Date.parse(plan.dhw_plan.forecast[0].t);
+    for (const [id, field] of [[DEFAULT_DHW, "dhw_power"],
+                               [DEFAULT_SPACE, "space_power"]]) {
+      if (windowHours !== undefined) {
+        st[id].attributes.manual_plan_window_hours = windowHours;
+      }
+      const fc = st[id].attributes.forecast;
+      const last = fc[fc.length - 1];
+      for (let t = Date.parse(last.t) + STEP; t < first + 48 * HOUR; t += STEP) {
+        fc.push({ ...last, t: local(t) });
+      }
+      for (const f of fc) {
+        const t = Date.parse(f.t);
+        if (t < at(-4.5)) continue;
+        f[field] = seeded[field].some(([a, b]) => t >= at(a) && t < at(b)) ? 3 : 0;
+      }
+    }
+    return st;
+  };
+  const applied = (states, geom) => {
+    const c = build(states, { what_if: true });
+    c._hass = mkHass(states);
+    c._onCardClick({});
+    if (geom) c.geomAt = () => geom;
+    called = null;
+    c.manual.apply();
+    return { card: c, data: (called && called.data) || {} };
+  };
+  const { card, data } = applied(extended());
+  const drafted = [...card.manual.draft().dhw, ...card.manual.draft().space];
+  check("the extended plan drafts runs at and past the window (#3636)",
+    drafted.some((r) => r.start >= ceiling), JSON.stringify(drafted));
+  // Only the seeded tail: the captured plan's own earlier runs are untouched.
+  const span = (slots) => (slots || [])
+    .filter((sl) => Date.parse(sl.start) >= at(-4.5))
+    .map((sl) => [Date.parse(sl.start), Date.parse(sl.end)].map(
+      (ms) => (ms - ceiling) / HOUR));
+  check("no slot sent starts at or after the manual-plan window (#3636)",
+    [...(data.dhw_slots || []), ...(data.space_slots || [])]
+      .every((sl) => Date.parse(sl.start) < ceiling),
+    JSON.stringify(data));
+  check("a run straddling the window is sent whole, later ones dropped (#3636)",
+    JSON.stringify(span(data.dhw_slots)) === JSON.stringify([[-4, -3], [-2, 0.5]]),
+    JSON.stringify(span(data.dhw_slots)));
+  check("a run starting within one step of the window is held back for clock skew (#3636)",
+    JSON.stringify(span(data.space_slots)) === JSON.stringify([[-4, -3]]),
+    JSON.stringify(span(data.space_slots)));
+  // The ceiling is the window, not the zoomed view: zoomed in so the visible
+  // end falls 3 h before the window, `editCeiling` would drop the run that
+  // straddles the window and the one before it. Design choice: what is applied
+  // does not depend on the zoom.
+  const zoomed = applied(extended(), { windowStart: 0, windowEnd: at(-3) });
+  check("a zoomed-in view does not change the applied runs (#3636)",
+    zoomed.card.manual.editCeiling() <= at(-3) &&
+      JSON.stringify(span(zoomed.data.dhw_slots)) ===
+        JSON.stringify([[-4, -3], [-2, 0.5]]),
+    JSON.stringify({ editCeiling: (zoomed.card.manual.editCeiling() - ceiling) / HOUR,
+                     dhw: span(zoomed.data.dhw_slots) }));
+  // The skew allowance is one step, not more: a run starting two steps
+  // before the window is inside the server's acceptance and is sent.
+  const twoSteps = applied(extended(undefined, {
+    dhw_power: [],
+    space_power: [[-4, -3], [-0.5, 1]],
+  })).data;
+  check("a run starting two steps before the window is sent (#3636)",
+    JSON.stringify(span(twoSteps.space_slots)) ===
+      JSON.stringify([[-4, -3], [-0.5, 1]]),
+    JSON.stringify(span(twoSteps.space_slots)));
+
+  // Null control: the captured plan ends inside the window, so the payload
+  // must be byte-identical to the one a window too wide to bind produces.
+  check("the captured plan ends inside the window (#3636)",
+    drag.manual.planEnd() < ceiling - STEP,
+    new Date(drag.manual.planEnd()).toISOString());
+  const inside = applied(slotStates).data;
+  const unbound = (() => {
+    const st = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(slotStates));
+    for (const id of [DEFAULT_DHW, DEFAULT_SPACE]) {
+      st[id].attributes.manual_plan_window_hours = 1000;
+    }
+    return applied(st).data;
+  })();
+  check("a plan wholly inside the window sends the same payload (#3636)",
+    (inside.dhw_slots || []).length > 0 &&
+      JSON.stringify(inside) === JSON.stringify(unbound),
+    JSON.stringify({ inside, unbound }));
+}
+
 // Prices are shown in the user's currency, not the author's.
 {
   const saved = drag._hass;

+# R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES re-points the streak checks to what replaced the
+# streak. A start is an edge to running from a last known class of stopped:
+# a steady running signal, folded as many confirmed True edges as you like

+    _steady_confirmed == 0 and _steady.lifetime == 0 and _steady.running,
+    f"confirmed {_steady_confirmed}, lifetime {_steady.lifetime}",
+)
+
+# The debounce is the tracker's: a changed class must hold EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S,
+# and a reading that agrees with the settled class clears the pending
+# change, so above -> below -> above inside the debounce is no edge. Null
+# control: the same walk with the third reading held past the debounce
+# confirms exactly one edge to running.
+_noncon = _FuzzEdges(settled=False)
+_noncon_edges = [

+    for _s, _v in ((0, True), (10, False), (20, True), (40, True))

+_noncon_held = _FuzzEdges(settled=False)
+_noncon_held_edges = [

+]

+    and _noncon_held_edges == [None, (NOW, True)],

 )

+# fitted draw is 2.1 x the ask at the low end of the span and 1.4 x at the top.

+_dm_ripple = [(1.15, 0.87, 1.0)[i % 3] for i in range(len(_dm_asks))]
+
+
