+    if return_c is not None:
+        cfg["floor_return_temp_entity"] = "sensor.ret"
+        live["sensor.ret"] = (str(return_c), "°C")
+    if mode is not None:
+        cfg["heat_pump_mode_entity"] = "select.mode"
+        live["select.mode"] = (mode, None)
+    if defrost is not None:
+        cfg["heat_pump_defrost_entity"] = "binary_sensor.defrost"
+        live["binary_sensor.defrost"] = (defrost, None)
+    hass = FakeHass()
+    # The notifier fires an event on a mode or defrost change; this rig's bus
+    # records nothing, so a sink stands in for it.
+    hass.bus.async_fire = lambda *_a, **_k: None
+    entry = _r9f12_entry(data=cfg, entry_id=f"ssg_{return_c}_{mode}_{defrost}")
+    seen = []
+    try:
+        for hour in range(cycles):
+            now = _ssg_start + timedelta(hours=hour)
+            _r9f12_dt.freeze(now)
+            for name, (value, unit) in live.items():
+                hass.states.set(name, FakeState(value, unit=unit) if unit else FakeState(value))
+            _r9f12_seed_prices(hass, now)
+            if hour == 0:
+                _r9f12_aio.run(_r9f12_integ.async_setup_entry(hass, entry))
+                coord = entry.runtime_data
+            _r9f12_aio.run(coord.async_refresh())
+            seen.append(coord._current_state.slab_temperature)
+        kwh = sum(float(p) for p in coord._optimization_result.power_schedule) * 0.25
+    finally:
+        _r9f12_dt.freeze(None)
+    return seen, kwh, {i[1]: i[2] for i in getattr(hass, "issues", [])}
+
+
+_ssg_warm = _ssg_cycles(38.0)
+_ssg_none = _ssg_cycles(None)
+_ssg_ok = _ssg_cycles(26.0)
+R.check(
+    "#3616: a 38 C heat-pump return in the floor-return field no longer plans "
+    "zero space heating for a room below its comfort band",
+    _ssg_warm[1] > 1.0,
+    f"planned {_ssg_warm[1]:.3f} kWh, slab {[round(s, 2) for s in _ssg_warm[0]]}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "and a refused reading leaves the slab to the model exactly as an install "
+    "with no floor-return sensor does",
+    _ssg_warm[0] == _ssg_none[0] and _ssg_warm[1] == _ssg_none[1],
+    f"refused {_ssg_warm[0]} {_ssg_warm[1]} / unconfigured {_ssg_none[0]} {_ssg_none[1]}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "and a repair issue names the sensor and the bound",
+    _ssg_warm[2].get(_ssg.ISSUE_FLOOR_RETURN_IMPLAUSIBLE, {}).get(
+        "translation_placeholders", {}).get("entity") == "sensor.ret"
+    and _ssg_warm[2][_ssg.ISSUE_FLOOR_RETURN_IMPLAUSIBLE][
+        "translation_placeholders"]["bound"] == "12",
+    f"{sorted(_ssg_warm[2])}",
+)
+# Null control: a plausible floor-loop reading (6.4 K above the room) still
+# seeds the slab unchanged, converging on the merge's return + 1 K fixed point,
+# raises nothing, and plans heat as before.
+R.check(
+    "null control: a plausible floor-loop return still seeds the slab, to the "
+    "return + 1 K fixed point, and raises no repair",
+    abs(_ssg_ok[0][-1] - 27.0) < 0.05 and _ssg_ok[0] != _ssg_none[0]
+    and _ssg.ISSUE_FLOOR_RETURN_IMPLAUSIBLE not in _ssg_ok[2],
+    f"slab {[round(s, 2) for s in _ssg_ok[0]]}, issues {sorted(_ssg_ok[2])}",
+)
+# A plausible reading during a hot-water run or a defrost is the pump's own
+# circuit water, not the floor's: it seeds nothing, and raises nothing.
+_ssg_dhw = _ssg_cycles(26.0, mode="DHW (Hot Water)")
+_ssg_dhw_none = _ssg_cycles(None, mode="DHW (Hot Water)")
+_ssg_frost = _ssg_cycles(26.0, defrost="on")
+_ssg_frost_none = _ssg_cycles(None, defrost="on")
+_ssg_both = _ssg_cycles(26.0, mode="Heating + DHW", defrost="off")
+R.check(
+    "a hot-water-only run does not seed the slab from the return",
+    _ssg_dhw[0] == _ssg_dhw_none[0]
+    and _ssg.ISSUE_FLOOR_RETURN_IMPLAUSIBLE not in _ssg_dhw[2],
+    f"{_ssg_dhw[0]} vs {_ssg_dhw_none[0]}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "nor does a defrost",
+    _ssg_frost[0] == _ssg_frost_none[0],
+    f"{_ssg_frost[0]} vs {_ssg_frost_none[0]}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "control: a heating mode with the defrost flag off seeds as with no signals",
+    _ssg_both[0] == _ssg_ok[0],
+    f"{_ssg_both[0]} vs {_ssg_ok[0]}",
+)
+# The bound at its edge, through the production predicate.
+R.check(
+    "the bound: 12 K above the room is a floor loop, anything warmer is not",
+    not _ssg.above_room(32.0, 20.0) and _ssg.above_room(32.1, 20.0)
+    and _ssg.SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K == 12.0,
+)
+# The option text states the bound the code applies, in every language.
+import json as _ssg_json  # noqa: E402
+from pathlib import Path as _ssg_Path  # noqa: E402
+
+_ssg_cc = _ssg_Path(_ssg.__file__).parent
+
+
+def _ssg_find(node):
+    """Every ``data_description`` text for the floor-return field, at any depth."""
+    if isinstance(node, dict):
+        text = (node.get("data_description") or {}).get("floor_return_temp_entity")
+        return ([text] if text else []) + [t for v in node.values() for t in _ssg_find(v)]
+    return []
+
+
+_ssg_texts = [
+    t for name in ("strings.json", "translations/en.json", "translations/de.json",
+                   "translations/sv.json")
+    for t in _ssg_find(_ssg_json.loads((_ssg_cc / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
+]
+R.check(
+    "every floor-return option text names the bound the guard applies",
+    len(_ssg_texts) == 12
+    and all(f"{_ssg.SLAB_SEED_MAX_ABOVE_ROOM_K:g} K" in t for t in _ssg_texts),
+    f"{len(_ssg_texts)} texts",
+)
+
+
+
+# --- R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: the start counter fed from running-signal edges ---
+# Part D of Bankaifan's outside pull request 3420, on the approved design
+# (design/R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES). The counter folds the confirmed edges of
+# running_signal, the one owner of the running signal in every duty mode,
+# instead of sampling the meter once per refresh in _record_accuracy. Every
+# check drives the production coordinator or module over the fake bus; timers
+# are fired by the replay when due, as Home Assistant fires them.
+import asyncio as _sce_aio  # noqa: E402
+
+from harness import FakeEntry as _SceEntry  # noqa: E402
+from homeassistant.util import dt as _sce_dt  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer import running_signal as _sce_rs  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.const import DEFAULT_OPTIMIZATION_INTERVAL as _SCE_PERIOD_MIN  # noqa: E402
+from dataclasses import replace as _sce_dc_replace  # noqa: E402
+
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import immersion_level_kw as _sce_over_kw  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import immersion_over as _sce_io  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model import on_threshold_kw as _sce_on_kw  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.wear import EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S as _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.wear import RiseHold as _SceRiseHold  # noqa: E402
+from heatpump_optimizer.wear import StartCounter as _SceStarts  # noqa: E402
+
+R.section("R10-START-COUNTER-EDGES: the start counter fed from running-signal edges")
+
+_SCE_T0 = datetime(2026, 2, 3, 6, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
+_SCE_PERIOD_S = 60 * _SCE_PERIOD_MIN
+
+
+class _SceRig:
+    """A live coordinator over the fake bus, its clock, its due timers and its refreshes."""
+
+    def __init__(self, states, priced=False, **config):
+        _sce_dt.freeze(_SCE_T0)
+        money = {"compressor_replacement_cost": 50000.0, "compressor_rated_starts": 100000} if priced else {}
+        self.c = HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator(
+            FakeHass(states), _SceEntry(data=dict(_T2_DATA, **money, **config)))
+        self.now, self.armed = _SCE_T0, {}
+        self.saves = 0
+        inner = self.c._schedule_ledger_save
+
+        def counted():
+            self.saves += 1
+            inner()
+        self.c._schedule_ledger_save = counted
+        self._seen()
+
+    def _seen(self):
+        for entry in getattr(self.c.hass, "timers", []):
+            self.armed.setdefault(id(entry), (self.now, entry))
+
+    def at(self, when):
+        """Advance the clock to ``when``, firing each timer due on the way, once."""
+        while True:
+            due = [(armed_at + timedelta(seconds=entry[0]), key, entry) for key, (armed_at, entry)
+                   in self.armed.items() if entry in getattr(self.c.hass, "timers", [])]
+            due = sorted((d for d in due if d[0] <= when), key=lambda d: d[0])
+            if not due:
+                break
+            fire_at, key, entry = due[0]
+            self.now = max(self.now, fire_at)
+            _sce_dt.freeze(self.now)
+            self.c.hass.timers.remove(entry)
+            del self.armed[key]
+            entry[1](self.now)
+            self._seen()
+        self.now = when
+        _sce_dt.freeze(when)
+
+    def set(self, entity, value, when, unit=None):
+        """A state change of ``entity`` at ``when``: the listeners hear it, as the bus delivers it."""
+        self.at(when)
+        old = self.c.hass.states.get(entity)
+        self.c.hass.states.set(entity, FakeState(value, unit=unit))
+        if old is not None and old.state == value:
+            return  # no change, no state_changed event
+        for ids, action in list(getattr(self.c.hass, "state_listeners", [])):
+            if entity in ids:
+                action(SimpleNamespace(data={"new_state": self.c.hass.states.get(entity)}))
+        self._seen()
+
+    def refresh(self, when):
+        self.at(when)
+        _sce_aio.run(self.c._update_current_state())
+        self._seen()
+
+    def load(self, payload):
+        async def _load(_p=payload):
+            return _p
+        self.c._ledger_store.async_load = _load
+        _sce_aio.run(self.c._async_load_ledger())
+
+    @property
+    def counter(self):
+        return self.c._start_counter
+
+
+def _sce_meter_trace(phases, perturb=None, every_s=60, refreshes=True, rig=None):
+    """Replay a meter-only install: ``phases`` is [(minutes, kW)], read every ``every_s``;
+    ``perturb`` (start minute, stop minutes) drops the draw to 0 inside one phase.
+    A refresh runs every default optimization interval. Returns the rig."""
+    rig = rig or _SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("0.0", unit="kW")}, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")
+    rig.load(None)
+    t, refresh_at = 0, _SCE_PERIOD_S
+    for minutes, kw in phases:
+        for s in range(t, t + minutes * 60, every_s):
+            value = kw
+            if perturb is not None and perturb[0] * 60 <= s < (perturb[0] + perturb[1]) * 60:
+                value = 0.0
+            if refreshes and s >= refresh_at:
+                rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=refresh_at))
+                refresh_at += _SCE_PERIOD_S
+            rig.set("sensor.kw", f"{value:.1f}", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=s), unit="kW")
+        t += minutes * 60
+    rig.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=t + 60))
+    return rig
+
+
+# The control trace: every on and off phase spans at least two refresh
+# periods, so the retired sampled path saw each one (two consecutive samples
+# a phase), and no start falls within one period of a month boundary.
+_SCE_ON_KW = 2.0
+_SCE_PHASES = [(90, 0.0), (120, _SCE_ON_KW), (90, 0.0), (150, _SCE_ON_KW), (120, 0.0), (90, _SCE_ON_KW), (60, 0.0)]
+_SCE_ON_PHASES = sum(1 for _m, kw in _SCE_PHASES if kw > 0)
+_sce_control = _sce_meter_trace(_SCE_PHASES)
+# The perturbation: one stop and restart inside one refresh period (5 min off,
+# 40 minutes into the second on phase, between two refreshes).
+_sce_perturbed = _sce_meter_trace(_SCE_PHASES, perturb=(90 + 40, 5))
+R.check(
+    "the control trace (every phase at least two refresh periods long) counts one start per on "
+    "phase; one stop and restart inside one refresh period counts exactly one more",
+    _sce_control.counter.lifetime == _SCE_ON_PHASES
+    and _sce_perturbed.counter.lifetime == _SCE_ON_PHASES + 1
+    and _sce_control.counter.month_count("2026-02") == _SCE_ON_PHASES,
+    f"control {_sce_control.counter.lifetime}, perturbed {_sce_perturbed.counter.lifetime}, "
+    f"on phases {_SCE_ON_PHASES}",
+)
+R.check(
+    "the counted starts are what the cycling cost and the plan never read: the effective "
+    "cycling cost is the same with no start and with every start counted",
+    _SceRig({}, priced=True, wear_autotune_enabled=True).c._effective_cycling_cost()
+    == _sce_meter_trace(_SCE_PHASES, rig=_SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("0.0", unit="kW")}, priced=True,
+                        wear_autotune_enabled=True, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")).c._effective_cycling_cost(),
+)
+
+# Lifecycle: the listener is armed in __init__, before the ledger store is
+# read; an edge confirmed before the read is queued, and the restore replays
+# it over the stored count on every exit of the load.
+def _sce_early(payload, released=False):
+    rig = _SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("0.0", unit="kW")}, priced=True, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "2.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=2), unit="kW")
+    for k in (0, 1):  # the meter's rise is held for two refreshes (S7)
+        rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=3, seconds=k))
+    queued = list(rig.counter.queued or [])
+    if released:
+        rig.c._release_registrations()
+    rig.load(payload)
+    wear = rig.c._ledger.line("2026-02", "wear")
+    return rig, queued, (wear or {}).get("sek", 0.0)
+
+
+_sce_stored, _sce_stored_q, _sce_stored_wear = _sce_early(
+    {"ledger": {"months": {}}, "starts": {"lifetime": 7, "months": {"2026-01": 7}, "running": False}})
+_sce_fresh, _sce_fresh_q, _sce_fresh_wear = _sce_early(None)
+_sce_gone, _sce_gone_q, _sce_gone_wear = _sce_early(
+    {"ledger": {"months": {}}, "starts": {"lifetime": 7, "months": {"2026-01": 7}, "running": False}}, released=True)
+R.check(
+    "an edge confirmed before the ledger load lands survives the restore: on a stored payload it "
+    "adds to the stored count and books its wear, on a fresh install it is the first start, and on a "
+    "load landing after the release it is counted in memory and books and saves nothing",
+    [cls for _t, cls in _sce_stored_q] == [False, True]
+    and (_sce_stored.counter.lifetime, _sce_stored.counter.months) == (8, {"2026-01": 7, "2026-02": 1})
+    and abs(_sce_stored_wear - 0.5) < 1e-9 and _sce_stored.saves == 1
+    and _sce_stored.counter.queued is None
+    and (_sce_fresh.counter.lifetime, abs(_sce_fresh_wear - 0.5) < 1e-9, _sce_fresh.saves) == (1, True, 1)
+    and (_sce_gone.counter.lifetime, _sce_gone_wear, _sce_gone.saves) == (8, 0.0, 0),
+    f"stored {_sce_stored.counter.lifetime} {_sce_stored_wear} {_sce_stored.saves}; fresh "
+    f"{_sce_fresh.counter.lifetime} {_sce_fresh_wear} {_sce_fresh.saves}; released "
+    f"{_sce_gone.counter.lifetime} {_sce_gone_wear} {_sce_gone.saves}",
+)
+
+
+_sce_free = _sce_meter_trace(_SCE_PHASES)
+R.check(
+    "a counted start books money, never energy, and only at a nonzero price: the priced install's wear "
+    "line carries 0 kWh, and the default install (no replacement cost) counts its starts with no wear line",
+    (_sce_stored.c._ledger.line("2026-02", "wear") or {}).get("kwh") == 0.0
+    and _sce_free.counter.lifetime == _SCE_ON_PHASES
+    and "wear" not in _sce_free.c._ledger.months.get("2026-02", {}).get("lines", {}),
+    f"{_sce_stored.c._ledger.line('2026-02', 'wear')} {_sce_free.c._ledger.months.get('2026-02', {}).get('lines')}",
+)
+
+
+class _SceRaises:
+    async def async_load(self):
+        raise RuntimeError("store")
+
+
+_sce_raise = _SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("2.0", unit="kW")}, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")
+for _sce_k in (1, 2):  # the meter's rise is held for two refreshes (S7)
+    _sce_raise.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=_sce_k))
+_sce_raise.c._ledger_store = _SceRaises()
+_sce_raise_err = None
+try:
+    _sce_aio.run(_sce_raise.c._async_load_ledger())
+except RuntimeError as err:
+    _sce_raise_err = err
+R.check(
+    "a load that raises still restores the counter and replays the queue",
+    _sce_raise.counter.queued is None and _sce_raise.counter.lifetime == 1,
+    f"{_sce_raise_err!r} {_sce_raise.counter.lifetime} {_sce_raise.counter.queued}",
+)
+_sce_cut = _SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("0.0", unit="kW")}, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")
+_sce_cut.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=1))
+_sce_cut.set("sensor.kw", "2.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=2), unit="kW")
+_sce_cut_armed = len(getattr(_sce_cut.c.hass, "timers", []))
+_sce_cut.c._release_registrations()
+R.check(
+    "the release drops the listener, the timer of a change still pending, the subscribers and their ticks, and a "
+    "second release is harmless; null control, the change was pending with its timer armed",
+    _sce_cut_armed == 1 and not _sce_cut.c.hass.state_listeners and not _sce_cut.c.hass.timers
+    and not _sce_rs.signal_for(_sce_cut.c).subscribers and not _sce_rs.signal_for(_sce_cut.c).ticks
+    and _sce_cut.c._release_registrations() is None,
+    f"{_sce_cut_armed} {_sce_cut.c.hass.timers}",
+)
+
+# A stored payload of the shape the sampled path wrote continues: the
+# lifetime and the months are not reset, and a compressor still running
+# across the upgrade is not counted again.
+_sce_cont = _SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("2.0", unit="kW")}, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")
+_sce_cont.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=1))
+_sce_cont.load({"ledger": {"months": {}}, "starts": {"lifetime": 41, "months": {"2026-02": 5}, "running": True}})
+_sce_cont_kept = (_sce_cont.counter.lifetime, dict(_sce_cont.counter.months))
+_sce_cont.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=10), unit="kW")
+_sce_cont.set("sensor.kw", "2.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=20), unit="kW")
+for _sce_k in (21, 22):  # the meter's rise is held for two refreshes (S7)
+    _sce_cont.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=_sce_k))
+R.check(
+    "the stored lifetime and month counts continue across the change: a compressor running "
+    "through the restart is no new start, and the next real start adds one",
+    _sce_cont_kept == (41, {"2026-02": 5})
+    and (_sce_cont.counter.lifetime, _sce_cont.counter.months) == (42, {"2026-02": 6}),
+    f"{_sce_cont_kept} {_sce_cont.counter.lifetime} {_sce_cont.counter.months}",
+)
+
+# Duty mode off (the default): nothing arbitrates, and a frequency sensor that
+# holds 40 Hz fires no further event; the timer confirms the start.
+_sce_hold = _SceRig({"sensor.freq": FakeState("0")}, compressor_freq_sensor="sensor.freq")
+_sce_hold.load(None)
+_sce_hold.set("sensor.freq", "40", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=5))
+_sce_hold_pending = _sce_rs.running_now(_sce_rs.signal_for(_sce_hold.c))
+_sce_hold_before = _sce_hold.counter.lifetime
+_sce_hold.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=5, seconds=_SCE_DEBOUNCE_S))
+R.check(
+    "in duty mode off a frequency held at 40 Hz with no later event is confirmed by the timer "
+    "at the debounce, and counted from its first reading",
+    _sce_hold.c._ctx._config.pump_duty_mode == "off"
+    and _sce_hold_pending is None and _sce_hold_before == 0
+    and _sce_hold.counter.lifetime == 1
+    and _sce_rs.running_now(_sce_rs.signal_for(_sce_hold.c)) is True
+    and not getattr(_sce_hold.c.hass, "timers", []),
+    f"{_sce_hold_pending} {_sce_hold_before} {_sce_hold.counter.lifetime}",
+)
+
+# The debounce with its timer armed: a meter blip over the on-threshold that
+# reverts before EDGE_DEBOUNCE_S is no start, one that outlasts it is one.
+# Every trace above reads at 60 s or longer, so its timer is always due before
+# the next reading; here the revert lands while the timer is still pending.
+def _sce_blip(seconds):
+    rig = _SceRig({"sensor.kw": FakeState("0.0", unit="kW")}, heat_pump_power_entity="sensor.kw")
+    rig.load(None)
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "2.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=10), unit="kW")
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=10, seconds=seconds), unit="kW")
+    rig.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=20))
+    return rig.counter.lifetime, len(getattr(rig.c.hass, "timers", []))
+
+
+_sce_blips = {s: _sce_blip(s) for s in (5, _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S - 1, _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S + 1)}
+R.check(
+    "a meter blip shorter than the debounce counts no start (5 s and one second under it), and one "
+    "second over it counts one; no timer outlives either",
+    _sce_blips == {5: (0, 0), _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S - 1: (0, 0), _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S + 1: (1, 0)},
+    f"{_sce_blips}",
+)
+
+# An unavailable or non-numeric signal counts nothing, and is no transition:
+# running -> unavailable -> running is no start; stopped -> unknown -> running is one.

+# Immersion (design section 2): a meter-only install at the default interval.
+# The meter reads no signal while the element runs, by the latch or by the

+    rig.c._current_action = {**rig.c._current_action, "power": 2.0, "dhw_power": 0.0}
+    params = rig.c._ctx._thermal_params
+    return rig, _sce_on_kw(params), _sce_over_kw(params)
+
+
+def _sce_kw(x):

+# S1: the element cuts in with the compressor off; over from its first reading.
+_sce_s1, _sce_on, _sce_over = _sce_element_rig()
+_sce_s1.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(_sce_over + 1.0), _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=1), unit="kW")

+_sce_s1.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=2 * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+_sce_s1_latched = _sce_s1.c._immersion_active
+_sce_s1.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=2 * _SCE_PERIOD_S + 60), unit="kW")
+_sce_s1.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=2 * _SCE_PERIOD_S + 120))

+_sce_s5.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=8), unit="kW")
+_sce_s5.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=10))
+# S3: the compressor runs, the element latches, the compressor stops under it:

+_sce_s4.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=_SCE_PERIOD_S))

+# The confirm timer is one per pending change (running_signal._arm_timer): a

+# thermal_model.immersion_over is strict at each of its three bounds: a

+# S7 (owner ruling D1, 2026-11-15): a meter reporting its window's average
+# gives an element cut-in, compressor off, one partial report between the
+# on-threshold and the over level; it holds one report period, at least the
+# debounce, so it is a confirmed rise before over arrives. On the meter a rise
+# counts only once two refreshes read the signal settled running; the no-class
+# edge over brings drops it first. Six offsets inside a 60 s and a 30 s window
+# (offset 0 fills its window and is over from its first report), a refresh
+# landing between the partial's confirmation and over, the element running
+# three refresh periods; then a real start on the same rig counts from its
+# second refresh. The cut-out of a short element, never latched, falls
+# through a partial from no class and stops: no start either; nor does a
+# second refresh landing while over is still pending.
+def _sce_s7(window_s, offset_s):
+    rig, _on, over = _sce_element_rig()
+    level = over + 1.0
+    rise = _SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=_SCE_PERIOD_S - _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S - 15)
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level * (window_s - offset_s) / window_s), rise, unit="kW")
+    rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=_SCE_PERIOD_S))
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level), rise + timedelta(seconds=window_s), unit="kW")
+    for k in (2, 3, 4):
+        rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+    cut = _SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=4 * _SCE_PERIOD_S + 60)
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level * offset_s / window_s), cut, unit="kW")
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", cut + timedelta(seconds=window_s), unit="kW")
+    for k in (5, 6, 7):
+        rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+    false = rig.counter.lifetime
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "2.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=7 * _SCE_PERIOD_S + 60), unit="kW")
+    seen = []
+    for k in (8, 9):
+        rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+        seen.append(rig.counter.lifetime)
+    return false, *seen
+
+
+def _sce_s7_quick(window_s):
+    rig, _on, over = _sce_element_rig()
+    level = over + 1.0
+    rise = _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=5)
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level / 2), rise, unit="kW")
+    rig.refresh(rise + timedelta(seconds=_SCE_DEBOUNCE_S + 1))
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level), rise + timedelta(seconds=window_s), unit="kW")
+    rig.refresh(rise + timedelta(seconds=window_s + 1))
+    rig.at(rise + timedelta(minutes=5))
+    return rig.counter.lifetime
+
+
+def _sce_s7_cutout(window_s):
+    rig, _on, over = _sce_element_rig()
+    level = over + 1.0
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level), _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=1), unit="kW")
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level / 2), _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=5), unit="kW")
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=5, seconds=window_s), unit="kW")
+    for k in (1, 2, 3):
+        rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+    return rig.counter.lifetime, rig.c._immersion_active
+

+# The controls, on the same rig and refreshes: a real start counts once, in
+# the month of its first reading, from its second refresh; a run stopping
+# before that counts once, at its stop.
+def _sce_s7_real(stop_s=None):
+    rig, _on, _over = _sce_element_rig()
+    rise = _SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=_SCE_PERIOD_S - 300)
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", "2.0", rise, unit="kW")
+    if stop_s is not None:
+        rig.set("sensor.kw", "0.0", rise + timedelta(seconds=stop_s), unit="kW")
+    seen = []
+    for k in (1, 2):
+        rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=k * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+        seen.append(rig.counter.lifetime)
+    return *seen, dict(rig.counter.months)
+

+_sce_s7_rows = {(w, round(w * k / 6)): _sce_s7(w, w * k / 6) for w in (60, 30) for k in range(6)}

+# wear.RiseHold alone: each edge it passes on keeps its own time; a held rise
+# released by its refreshes is the rise's, and a short run is the rise's then

+# A refresh's own re-read moves the class with no meter event: the element's
+# latch, or the commanded draw that makes the same reading the element's.
+# The held rise must hear the class as this refresh re-reads it, so the
+# re-read comes before the tick (running_signal.refresh). Null control, the
+# same rig with nothing moving counts the rise at its second refresh.
+def _sce_reread(move):
+    rig, _on, over = _sce_element_rig()
+    level = over + 1.0 if move == "commanded" else 2.0
+    if move == "commanded":
+        rig.c._current_action = {**rig.c._current_action, "power": 0.0, "dhw_power": 0.0}
+    rig.set("sensor.kw", _sce_kw(level), _SCE_T0 + timedelta(minutes=1), unit="kW")
+    rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=_SCE_PERIOD_S))
+    if move == "commanded":
+        rig.c._current_action = {**rig.c._current_action, "power": 2.0}
+    elif move == "latch":
+        rig.c._immersion_active, rig.c._immersion_clear_count = True, 0  # as _detect_immersion latches
+    rig.refresh(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=2 * _SCE_PERIOD_S))
+    rig.at(_SCE_T0 + timedelta(seconds=2 * _SCE_PERIOD_S + 2 * _SCE_DEBOUNCE_S))
+    return rig.counter.lifetime
+

+_sce_reread_rows = {m: _sce_reread(m) for m in ("commanded", "latch", None)}

+    "latch changing, no meter event) while a rise is held counts no start: the tick hears the class "
+    "this refresh re-reads; null control, the same rig with nothing moving counts the rise once",
+    _sce_reread_rows == {"commanded": 0, "latch": 0, None: 1},
+    f"{_sce_reread_rows}",
+)
+_sce_dt.freeze(None)
+
+
 sys.exit(R.close("FEATURE CHECKS"))

+@contract(

+def _call_later_cancel():
+    from homeassistant.core import callback
+    from homeassistant.helpers.event import async_call_later
+

+        pass
+

+    cancel = async_call_later(hass, 30.0, callback(lambda now: None))
+    assert len(hass.timers) == 1 and hass.timers[0][0] == 30.0
+    cancel()
+    assert hass.timers == []
+    cancel()
+    try:
+        async_call_later(hass, 1.0, lambda now: None)
+    except TypeError:
+        return

diff --git a/tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/event.py b/tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/event.py
index db3248ee63..28f0a71738 100644
--- a/tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/event.py
+++ b/tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/event.py
@@ -38,3 +38,28 @@ def async_track_state_change_event(hass, entity_ids, action):
             listeners.remove(entry)
 
     return _unsub
+
+
+def async_call_later(hass, delay, action):
+    """Record a one-shot timer on ``hass.timers`` as ``[delay, action]``.
+
+    No lane runs a loop to fire it: a test fires a timer by calling its
+    action with a time, as upstream's does at expiry. The returned cancel
+    removes the entry, so an armed timer is visible and a cancelled one is
+    gone; twice is harmless, as upstream's. A plain function that is neither
+    ``@callback`` nor a coroutine is refused, as the state tracker refuses it.
+    """
+    if not (getattr(action, "_hass_callback", False) or inspect.iscoroutinefunction(action)):
+        raise TypeError(f"{action!r} is neither @callback nor a coroutine function")
+    timers = getattr(hass, "timers", None)
+    if timers is None:
+        timers = []
+        hass.timers = timers
+    entry = [delay, action]
+    timers.append(entry)
+
+    def _cancel():
+        if entry in timers:
+            timers.remove(entry)
+
+    return _cancel

+def open_cards_cli():
+    """(marked, unmarked): `--open-cards --round 8` run whole, as a subprocess
+    of this file, on two commits of a scratch repository whose round-8 record
+    differs only in C2 and C3's `gates_finders`: booleans in the first, absent
+    and the string "true" in the second. C1 is accepted, non-gating, unmerged.
+    Both commits carry one roster whose open group G1 is marked non-gating, so
+    the group half lists G1 and names nothing UNMARKED: the exit code and the
+    UNMARKED lines measured here are the card half's alone."""
+    prev, path = records(8)
+    cards = {"C1": {"decision": "accepted", "ruling": "R1", "gates_finders": False, "merged": "0" * 40},
+             "C2": {"decision": "accepted", "ruling": "R2", "gates_finders": True},
+             "C3": {"decision": "accepted", "ruling": "R3", "gates_finders": True},
+             "C4": {"decision": "rejected", "ruling": "R4"}}
+    unmarked = copy.deepcopy(cards)
+    del unmarked["C2"]["gates_finders"]
+    unmarked["C3"]["gates_finders"] = "true"
+    from throwaway_git import throwaway_git_init  # the one way to build a scratch repo; main() put tests/ on the path
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
+        env = throwaway_git_init(d, "-q")
+        git = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", d, *a], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
+        runs = []
+        for cs in (cards, unmarked):
+            for f, body in ((OBJECTIVE, {"terms": [], "objects": {}}), (prev, {"terms": {}}),
+                            (path, {"round": 8, "reads": prev, "cards": cs}),
+                            (f"{roster_lib.ROSTERS_DIR}/wave-r8-groups.json",
+                             {"groups": [{"group": "G1", "gates_finders": False, "resume": {"stage": "not-started"}}]})):
+                (Path(d) / f).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+                (Path(d) / f).write_text(json.dumps(body))
+            git("add", "-A")
+            git("commit", "-q", "-m", "record")
+            runs.append(subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(Path(__file__).resolve()), "--repo", d, "--ref", git("rev-parse", "HEAD"),
+                                        "--roster-ref", git("rev-parse", "HEAD"), "--round", "8", "--open-cards"], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True))
+    return tuple(runs)
+
+
+def json_or_none(text):
+    try:
+        return json.loads(text)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+

diff --git a/tools/audit/enumerate.py b/tools/audit/enumerate.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..dba42026bf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tools/audit/enumerate.py
@@ -0,0 +1,956 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Print one audit universe, one item per line, so a finder can report `universe=N examined=n`.
+
+Usage: python3 -I tools/audit/enumerate.py <universe> [--repo DIR] [options]
+  d0-grid [--plane price-weather]   tests/profiles.py price x weather, x zones x dhw x plant x horizon
+  d0-modules             package-internal import closure of optimizer.py + dhw_planner.py, plus coordinator.py
+  d1-lifecycle           async_track_* / async_call_later / listener / task registrations and the entry points
+  d1-stores              store.py DOMAINS keys, and one `upgrade` line per earlier *_STORE_VERSION /
+                         CONFIG_ENTRY_VERSION step
+  d1-inputs              every configured entity slot: a config_flow.py `_F` key behind an entity selector,
+                         and each key entry_config.py's FACTORY_KEPT keeps as an entity assignment
+  d1-solve-state         every `self.<attr>` the solve-thread entries (SOLVE_FNS) touch
+  d1-excepts             every except handler, broad or narrow
+  d1-parsers             defs named *parse*, and json.loads / .json() / async_subscribe sites
+  d2-identities [--cells]   dev/audit/config/identities.json, one line per identity; --cells crosses each
+                         with its grid (population axes, tests/golden.py SCENARIOS, or levels the register states)
+  d3-sites [--state S] [--by-file] [--ast]   the mutation universe, `<file>:<line> <kind> <state>`, joined
+                         to the ledger through tests/mutation_table.py's own `inventory` and
+                         `disposition_matches`; --ast is the ledger-free fallback (if/ifexp/minmax/except)
+  d8-cells               strings.json entity name / state / attribute, once per translation file
+  d9-collections         coordinator.py `self.<attr>` bound to a container, once per class and attribute
+  d9-attributes          classes defining or assigning extra_state_attributes
+  d9-solves              calls of the solver entry, then of each function holding one, to a fixed point
+  d12-cells [--pairs]    every level `check_scopes.py --population` reads, the card and the blueprints
+                         (--pairs: every pair of levels from two axes), each `not run` until a ledger row
+  --ledger TSV           with any universe: each line beside its ledger row's asserting test, or `not run`
+                         (rows: item, test; for d12-cells: cell, source, test); a row naming no item,
+                         an unlisted source or no test is refused
+  d14-classes [--status open]   dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json entries that carry a status
+  d15-installs           dev/audit/config/bundles.json, one line per bundle an install sent
+  d16-writes [--cells]   actuator `services.async_call` and `log_held` sites; --cells crosses each
+                         with the PUMP_DUTY_MODES parsed from const.py and the four lifecycle conditions
+  d17-features           services.yaml keys, strings.json steps/fields/entities, blueprints
+  --briefs               the acceptance of a brief that names a universe: every `enumerate.py <universe>`
+                         a dev/governance/dimensions/D*.md cites, with its --cells or --pairs, runs
+                         non-empty; an unknown universe or a tree citing none is refused
+Stdout is the universe only (deterministic, sorted; `wc -l` is its size); a second identical item on
+one line gets a ` #2` suffix so no two lines are equal. Diagnostics go to stderr.
+Exit 0 on success. Exit 2 with a message on stderr when a source is missing or yields zero items: an
+empty universe is a refusal, never a pass.
+Null control: --self-test runs every universe on the live tree (>=1 line, sorted, no duplicates), and
+per universe plants a fake repo (--repo) whose count it states, deletes one item and reads the count
+move, then empties or removes the source and reads the refusal. It prints `SELF-TEST passed (N arms)`
+or names the failing arm and exits 1.
+"""
+import argparse, ast, collections, contextlib, io, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+PKG = "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer"
+OBJECTIVE, IDENTITIES, BUNDLES = "dev/audit/config/objective.json", "dev/audit/config/identities.json", "dev/audit/config/bundles.json"
+# the conditions the actuator-write dimension drives
+CONDITIONS = ("running", "restart", "upgrade", "unavailable")
+# D0.md step 4's axes; the last two plants are the cells round 10's escapes showed no seat drove
+TOPOLOGY, DHW, HORIZON_H = ("single-zone", "two-zone"), ("dhw", "no-dhw"), (6, 24, 48)
+PLANT = ("plain", "valve-storage", "wood", "manual-valve-buffer", "flow-setpoint-behind-valve")
+USER_PLATFORMS = ("switch", "button", "climate", "datetime", "number", "select")
+LIFE_CALLS = {"async_call_later", "async_on_unload", "async_create_task", "async_create_background_task",
+              "async_add_executor_job", "async_listen", "async_listen_once", "add_update_listener"}
+ENTRY_FNS = ("async_setup", "async_setup_entry", "async_unload_entry", "async_remove_entry",
+             "async_migrate_entry", "async_update_options")
+# D1.md step 4's solve-thread entries, D9.md's solver entry, and what counts as a retained collection
+SOLVE_FNS, SOLVER_ENTRY = ("_solve_record", "_solve_hubs"), "_multi_start_minimize"
+CONTAINERS = {"dict", "list", "set", "deque", "defaultdict", "OrderedDict", "Counter"}
+# decision 0018 section 1: the four sources that examine a generality cell
+SOURCES = ("simulation", "bundle", "install-report", "property-test")
+
+
+class Refuse(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def pkg_files(repo):
+    return sorted((repo / PKG).glob("*.py"))
+
+
+def rel(repo, p):
+    return p.relative_to(repo).as_posix()
+
+
+def parse(p):
+    return ast.parse(p.read_text())  # a missing source is an OSError, which run() refuses
+
+
+def scoped(tree):
+    """Like walk, but a def/class node's children see the def's dotted name."""
+    def go(node, q):
+        for c in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
+            yield c, q
+            if isinstance(c, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
+                yield from go(c, c.name if q == "<module>" else f"{q}.{c.name}")
+            else:
+                yield from go(c, q)
+    yield from go(tree, "<module>")
+
+
+def fname(call):
+    f = call.func
+    return f.id if isinstance(f, ast.Name) else f.attr if isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) else ""
+
+
+def const_assign(tree, name):
+    """The value node of a module-level `name = ...` / `name: T = ...`, or None."""
+    for n in tree.body:
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == name for t in n.targets):
+            return n.value
+        if isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(n.target, ast.Name) and n.target.id == name and n.value:
+            return n.value
+
+
+def d16(repo, cells=False, **_):
+    out = []
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        for n, q in scoped(parse(p)):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Call):
+                f = n.func
+                if isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and f.attr == "async_call" and isinstance(f.value, ast.Attribute) and f.value.attr == "services":
+                    out.append(f"write {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {q}")
+                if fname(n) == "log_held":
+                    out.append(f"hold {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {q}")
+    if cells:
+        v = const_assign(parse(repo / PKG / "const.py"), "PUMP_DUTY_MODES")
+        modes = [e.value for e in getattr(v, "elts", []) if isinstance(e, ast.Constant)]
+        out = [f"{s} | duty={m} | {c}" for s in out for m in modes for c in CONDITIONS]
+    return out
+
+
+def d17(repo, **_):
+    out, base = [], repo / PKG
+    out += [f"service {m}" for m in re.findall(r"^([a-z_]+):", (base / "services.yaml").read_text(), re.M)]
+    s = json.loads((base / "strings.json").read_text())
+    for sec, kstep, kfield in (("config", "config-step", "config-field"), ("options", "options-step", "option")):
+        for step, body in s.get(sec, {}).get("step", {}).items():
+            out.append(f"{kstep} {step}")
+            out += [f"{kfield} {step}.{k}" for k in (body.get("data") or {})]
+    ent = s.get("entity", {})
+    out += [f"entity {pl}.{k}" for pl in USER_PLATFORMS for k in ent.get(pl, {})]
+    return out + [f"blueprint {b}" for b in sorted(tracked(repo)) if b.startswith("blueprints/")]
+
+
+def d14(repo, status=None, **_):
+    p = repo / "dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json"
+    return [f"{v['status']} {v.get('kind', '?')} {k}" for k, v in json.loads(p.read_text()).items()
+            if isinstance(v, dict) and "status" in v and status in (None, v["status"])]
+
+
+def d0grid(repo, plane=None, **_):
+    tree = parse(repo / "tests/profiles.py")
+    lits = {}
+    for fn in ("prices", "weather"):
+        lits[fn] = sorted({c.value for f in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(f, ast.FunctionDef) and f.name == fn
+                           for n in ast.walk(f) if isinstance(n, ast.Compare) and isinstance(n.left, ast.Name)
+                           and n.left.id == "profile" for c in n.comparators if isinstance(c, ast.Constant)})
+    pw = [f"{a}/{b}" for a in lits["prices"] for b in lits["weather"]]
+    if plane == "price-weather":
+        return pw
+    return [f"{x}/{t}/{d}/{pl}/{h}h" for x in pw for t in TOPOLOGY for d in DHW for pl in PLANT for h in HORIZON_H]
+
+
+def imports(path, base):
+    out = set()
+    for n in ast.walk(parse(path)):
+        names = []
+        if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom):
+            if n.level == 1 and n.module:
+                names = [n.module.split(".")[0]]
+            elif n.level == 1:
+                names = [a.name for a in n.names]
+            elif n.level == 0 and n.module and n.module.startswith(PKG.replace("/", ".")):
+                tail = n.module[len(PKG):].lstrip(".")
+                names = [tail.split(".")[0]] if tail else [a.name for a in n.names]
+        elif isinstance(n, ast.Import):
+            names = [a.name[len(PKG) + 1:].split(".")[0] for a in n.names if a.name.startswith(PKG.replace("/", ".") + ".")]
+        out |= {x for x in names if (base / f"{x}.py").is_file()}
+    return out
+
+
+def d0modules(repo, **_):
+    base = repo / PKG
+    seen, todo = set(), ["optimizer", "dhw_planner"]
+    while todo:
+        m = todo.pop()
+        if m not in seen:
+            seen.add(m)
+            todo += sorted(imports(base / f"{m}.py", base))
+    if not (base / "coordinator.py").is_file():
+        raise Refuse(f"missing source {base / 'coordinator.py'}")
+    return [f"{PKG}/{m}.py" for m in seen | {"coordinator"}]
+
+
+def d1stores(repo, **_):
+    out = []
+    st = parse(repo / PKG / "store.py")
+    d = const_assign(st, "DOMAINS")
+    if not isinstance(d, ast.Dict):
+        raise Refuse("no DOMAINS dict literal in store.py")
+    for k in d.keys:
+        if isinstance(k, ast.Constant):
+            out.append(f"store {k.value}")
+        elif isinstance(k, ast.Name):
+            v = const_assign(st, k.id)
+            out.append(f"store {v.value if isinstance(v, ast.Constant) else k.id}")
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        r = rel(repo, p)
+        for n in parse(p).body:
+            tg = n.targets[0] if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and len(n.targets) == 1 else getattr(n, "target", None)
+            if isinstance(n, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)) and isinstance(tg, ast.Name) and isinstance(n.value, ast.Constant) \
+                    and type(n.value.value) is int and (tg.id.endswith("STORE_VERSION") or (tg.id == "CONFIG_ENTRY_VERSION" and p.name == "const.py")):
+                v = n.value.value
+                out += [f"upgrade {r}:{tg.id} v{k}->{v}" for k in range(1, v)] or [f"upgrade {r}:{tg.id} v{v} (no earlier version)"]
+    return out
+
+
+def d1excepts(repo, **_):
+    out = []
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        for n, q in scoped(parse(p)):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.ExceptHandler):
+                ts = n.type.elts if isinstance(n.type, ast.Tuple) else [n.type]
+                broad = n.type is None or any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id in ("Exception", "BaseException") for t in ts)
+                out.append(f"{rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {'broad' if broad else 'narrow'} {q}")
+    return out

+def d1life(repo, **_):
+    out = []
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        t = parse(p)
+        for n, q in scoped(t):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Call):
+                k = fname(n)
+                if k.startswith("async_track_") or k in LIFE_CALLS:
+                    out.append(f"{k} {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {q}")
+        if p.name == "__init__.py":
+            out += [f"entry {n.name}" for n in t.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and n.name in ENTRY_FNS]
+    return out

+
+def d3(repo, state=None, by_file=False, ast_only=False, **_):
+    rows = []  # (file, "file:line kind", state)
+    if ast_only:
+        for p in pkg_files(repo):
+            for n, _q in scoped(parse(p)):
+                k = ("if" if isinstance(n, ast.If) else "ifexp" if isinstance(n, ast.IfExp) else "except" if isinstance(n, ast.ExceptHandler)
+                     else "minmax" if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and fname(n) in ("min", "max", "clip") else None)
+                if k:
+                    rows.append((rel(repo, p), f"{rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {k}", None))
+    else:
+        mt = repo / "tests/mutation_table.py"
+        if not mt.is_file():
+            raise Refuse(f"missing source {mt} (use --ast for the ledger-free fallback)")
+        sys.path.append(str(repo / "tests"))
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr):
+            import mutation_table as m
+            b, inv = m.load_budgets(), m.inventory()
+        kb, tr = b.get("killed_by", {}), b.get("survivor_triage", {})
+        for s in inv:
+            a = s["anchor"]
+            st = "killed" if m.disposition_matches(kb.get(a), s) else "triaged" if m.disposition_matches(tr.get(a), s) else "unrecorded"
+            if state in (None, st):
+                rows.append((s["file"], f"{s['file']}:{s['line']} {s['kind']}", st))
+    if by_file:
+        c = collections.Counter(f for f, _l, _s in rows)
+        if ast_only:
+            return [f"{f} {c[f]}" for f in c]
+        return [f"{f} {c[f]} " + " ".join(str(sum(1 for r in rows if r[0] == f and r[2] == s)) for s in ("killed", "triaged", "unrecorded")) for f in c]
+    return [f"{l} {s}" if s else l for _f, l, s in rows]
+
+
+
+def flow_slots(repo):
+    """The keys config_flow.py's `_F` rows offer through an entity selector: a row whose widget is a
+    call of EntitySelector or of a def returning one, its key a name or a comprehension's loop name
+    over a tuple of names. An entity selector in no such row is refused: the census would be short."""
+    t = parse(repo / PKG / "config_flow.py")
+    defs = [d for d in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(d, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))]
+    fac = {d.name for d in defs if any(isinstance(r, ast.Return) and isinstance(r.value, ast.Call)
+                                       and fname(r.value) == "EntitySelector" for r in ast.walk(d))}
+    inside = {id(n) for d in defs if d.name in fac for n in ast.walk(d)}
+    loops = {}  # id(an _F call) -> {loop name: [the tuple's names]}
+    for c in ast.walk(t):
+        if isinstance(c, (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp, ast.SetComp)):
+            b = {g.target.id: [e.id for e in g.iter.elts] for g in c.generators if isinstance(g.target, ast.Name)
+                 and isinstance(g.iter, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)) and all(isinstance(e, ast.Name) for e in g.iter.elts)}
+            loops.update({id(n): b for n in ast.walk(c.elt)})
+    keys, rows = [], set()
+    for n in ast.walk(t):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and fname(n) == "_F":
+            a = {**dict(zip(("step", "key", "default", "widget"), n.args)), **{k.arg: k.value for k in n.keywords}}
+            w, k = a.get("widget"), a.get("key")
+            if isinstance(w, ast.Call) and (fname(w) in fac or fname(w) == "EntitySelector"):
+                rows.add(id(w))
+                if not isinstance(k, ast.Name):
+                    raise Refuse(f"config_flow.py:{n.lineno}: an entity selector row whose key is no name")
+                keys += loops.get(id(n), {}).get(k.id) or [k.id]
+    for n in ast.walk(t):
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and id(n) not in inside and id(n) not in rows and (fname(n) in fac or fname(n) == "EntitySelector"):
+            raise Refuse(f"config_flow.py:{n.lineno}: an entity selector outside an `_F` row is in no census")
+    return keys
+
+
+def wiring_slots(repo):
+    """The keys entry_config.py's FACTORY_KEPT keeps for the reason its one comprehension gives (an
+    entity assignment): the const.py names that comprehension's startswith/endswith tests select,
+    and the dict entries FACTORY_KEPT spreads that give the same reason. Another test is refused."""
+    t = parse(repo / PKG / "entry_config.py")
+    fk = const_assign(t, "FACTORY_KEPT")
+    comps = [c for c in ast.walk(fk) if isinstance(c, ast.DictComp)] if fk else []
+    if len(comps) != 1 or not isinstance(comps[0].value, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(comps[0].generators[0].target, ast.Tuple):
+        raise Refuse("entry_config.py: no FACTORY_KEPT holding one comprehension over (name, key): re-read the entity rule")
+    c = comps[0]
+    reason, (nv, kv) = c.value.value, [e.id for e in c.generators[0].target.elts]
+    tests = []
+    for e in [x for i in c.generators[0].ifs for x in (i.values if isinstance(i, ast.BoolOp) else [i])]:
+        if isinstance(e, ast.Call) and fname(e) == "isinstance" and getattr(e.args[0], "id", None) == kv:
+            continue
+        if not (isinstance(e, ast.Call) and fname(e) in ("startswith", "endswith") and isinstance(e.func.value, ast.Name)
+                and e.func.value.id in (nv, kv) and len(e.args) == 1 and isinstance(e.args[0], ast.Constant)):
+            raise Refuse(f"entry_config.py:{e.lineno}: FACTORY_KEPT's entity rule holds a test this census cannot read")
+        tests.append((e.func.value.id == nv, fname(e), e.args[0].value))
+    keys = []
+    for n in parse(repo / PKG / "const.py").body:
+        tg = n.targets[0] if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and len(n.targets) == 1 else getattr(n, "target", None)
+        v = getattr(n, "value", None)
+        if isinstance(tg, ast.Name) and isinstance(v, ast.Constant) and isinstance(v.value, str) \
+                and all(getattr(tg.id if on_name else v.value, how)(arg) for on_name, how, arg in tests):
+            keys.append(tg.id)
+    for d in [x for x in ast.walk(fk) if isinstance(x, ast.Dict)]:
+        for k, v in zip(d.keys, d.values):
+            src = const_assign(t, v.id) if k is None and isinstance(v, ast.Name) else None
+            pairs = zip(src.keys, src.values) if isinstance(src, ast.Dict) else [(k, v)] if k is not None else []
+            keys += [kk.attr if isinstance(kk, ast.Attribute) else kk.id for kk, vv in pairs
+                     if isinstance(kk, (ast.Attribute, ast.Name)) and isinstance(vv, ast.Constant) and vv.value == reason]
+    return keys
+
+
+def d1inputs(repo, **_):
+    """Step 3's inputs: every configured entity slot, by what the code treats as one: a key the
+    options flow offers through an entity selector, or one a factory reset keeps as an entity
+    assignment. A key in both prints once."""
+    return [f"input {k}" for k in sorted(set(flow_slots(repo)) | set(wiring_slots(repo)))]
+
+
+def d1solve(repo, **_):
+    """Step 4's reads: every `self.<attr>` the solve-thread entry functions touch."""
+    out, found = set(), set()
+    for n, _q in scoped(parse(repo / PKG / "coordinator.py")):
+        if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and n.name in SOLVE_FNS:
+            found.add(n.name)
+            out |= {f"{n.name} self.{a.attr}" for a in ast.walk(n)
+                    if isinstance(a, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(a.value, ast.Name) and a.value.id == "self"}
+    if set(SOLVE_FNS) - found:
+        raise Refuse(f"coordinator.py lacks {sorted(set(SOLVE_FNS) - found)}: the solve-thread entry moved, re-point SOLVE_FNS")
+    return sorted(out)
+
+
+def d1parsers(repo, **_):
+    """Step 6's parsers: a def whose name holds `parse`, and each json.loads / .json() / async_subscribe site."""
+    out = []
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        for n, q in scoped(parse(p)):
+            if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and "parse" in n.name:
+                out.append(f"def {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {n.name}")
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Call):
+                f, k = n.func, fname(n)
+                if k == "loads" and isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(f.value, ast.Name) and f.value.id == "json":
+                    out.append(f"json {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {q}")
+                elif k == "json" and isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and not n.args:
+                    out.append(f"response {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {q}")
+                elif k == "async_subscribe":
+                    out.append(f"subscribe {rel(repo, p)}:{n.lineno} {q}")
+    return out
+
+
+def tracked(repo):
+    r = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    fs = r.stdout.split("\n") if r.returncode == 0 and (repo / ".git").exists() else []
+    return {f for f in fs if f} or {rel(repo, Path(d) / f) for d, _, names in os.walk(repo) for f in names}
+
+
+def population_axes(repo):
+    """{axis: [levels]} as `check_scopes.py --population` reads them, by its own reader, and the
+    two totals it prints; a binary axis key is its own axis with levels present and absent."""
+    obj = repo / OBJECTIVE
+    sys.path.append(str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+    import check_scopes
+    lines, ok = check_scopes.population(json.loads(obj.read_text()).get("population", []), tracked(repo), lambda f: (repo / f).read_text())
+    if not ok:
+        raise Refuse("the population is unreadable: " + "; ".join(l for l in lines if l.startswith("UNREADABLE")))
+    axes, totals = {}, {}
+    for l in lines:
+        if "\t" not in l:
+            k, _, v = l.partition(": ")
+            totals[k] = int(v)
+            continue
+        name, _, rest = l.partition("\t")
+        n, _, lv = rest.partition("\t")
+        if n == "NO-READ":
+            print(f"NO-READ axis {name}: no cell until {OBJECTIVE} declares its levels", file=sys.stderr)
+        elif n.endswith("binary axes"):
+            axes.update({k: ["absent", "present"] for k in lv.split(",")})
+        else:
+            axes[name] = lv.split(",")
+    return axes, totals
+
+
+def golden_scenarios(repo):
+    v = const_assign(parse(repo / "tests/golden.py"), "SCENARIOS")
+    return [k.value for k in getattr(v, "keys", []) if isinstance(k, ast.Constant)]
+
+
+def d2(repo, cells=False, **_):
+    """The identity register, one line per identity, or under --cells one per identity and
+    grid cell. A grid axis is a population axis by name, `golden` (tests/golden.py SCENARIOS),
+    or an inline {"axis", "levels"} the register states because no source holds it."""
+    p = repo / IDENTITIES
+    rows, out, pop = json.loads(p.read_text()).get("identities", []), [], None
+    for r in rows:
+        if not (re.fullmatch(r"M\d+", str(r.get("step"))) and r.get("id") and r.get("identity") and r.get("grid")):
+            raise Refuse(f"{IDENTITIES}: an identity needs step, id, identity and a non-empty grid: {r}")
+        grid = []
+        for g in r["grid"]:
+            if isinstance(g, dict):
+                name, lv = g.get("axis"), g.get("levels")
+            elif g == "golden":
+                name, lv = g, golden_scenarios(repo)
+            else:
+                pop = pop or population_axes(repo)[0]
+                name, lv = g, pop.get(g)
+            if not lv:
+                raise Refuse(f"{IDENTITIES}: identity {r['id']} names grid axis {name!r}, which has no level")
+            grid.append((name, lv))
+        if not cells:
+            out.append(f"{r['step']} {r['id']} grid=" + "x".join(n for n, _ in grid))
+            continue
+        combos = [[]]
+        for name, lv in grid:
+            combos = [c + [f"{name}={x}"] for c in combos for x in lv]
+        out += [f"{r['step']} {r['id']} | " + " ".join(c) for c in combos]
+    return out
+
+
+def d8(repo, **_):
+    """Entity by state by language: every name, state, attribute and attribute state strings.json
+    declares under `entity`, once per translation file (a file lacking the key is still a cell)."""
+    sj, tr = repo / PKG / "strings.json", repo / PKG / "translations"
+    langs = sorted(f.stem for f in tr.glob("*.json"))  # no translation file is no cell, which run() refuses
+    facets = []
+    for pl, ents in json.loads(sj.read_text()).get("entity", {}).items():
+        for k, body in ents.items():
+            facets.append(f"{pl}.{k} name")
+            facets += [f"{pl}.{k} state={s}" for s in body.get("state", {})]
+            for a, ab in body.get("state_attributes", {}).items():
+                facets.append(f"{pl}.{k} attr={a}")
+                facets += [f"{pl}.{k} attr={a}:state={s}" for s in (ab.get("state", {}) if isinstance(ab, dict) else {})]
+    return [f"{lang} {f}" for f in facets for lang in langs]
+
+
+def d9collections(repo, **_):
+    """Every `self.<attr>` of a coordinator.py class bound to a container literal, comprehension
+    or constructor, once per class and attribute, at its first binding."""
+    first = {}
+    for n, q in scoped(parse(repo / PKG / "coordinator.py")):
+        tg = n.targets if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) else [n.target] if isinstance(n, ast.AnnAssign) and n.value else []
+        v = getattr(n, "value", None)
+        kind = ({ast.Dict: "dict", ast.List: "list", ast.Set: "set", ast.DictComp: "dict", ast.ListComp: "list", ast.SetComp: "set"}.get(type(v))
+                or (fname(v) if isinstance(v, ast.Call) and fname(v) in CONTAINERS else None))
+        for t in tg:
+            if kind and isinstance(t, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(t.value, ast.Name) and t.value.id == "self" and "." in q:
+                first.setdefault(f"{q.split('.')[0]}.{t.attr}", f"{kind} {PKG}/coordinator.py:{n.lineno}")
+    return [f"{k} {v}" for k, v in first.items()]
+
+
+def d9attributes(repo, **_):
+    """Every class that publishes attributes: one defining or assigning `extra_state_attributes`."""
+    out = []
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        for c in ast.walk(parse(p)):
+            if isinstance(c, ast.ClassDef) and any(
+                    (isinstance(m, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and m.name == "extra_state_attributes")
+                    or (isinstance(m, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)) and any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == "_attr_extra_state_attributes"
+                                                                          for t in (m.targets if isinstance(m, ast.Assign) else [m.target])))
+                    for m in c.body):
+                out.append(f"{rel(repo, p)}:{c.lineno} {c.name}")
+    return out
+
+
+def d9solves(repo, **_):
+    """The solve paths: each call of SOLVER_ENTRY, then each call of, or bare reference to (a
+    function handed to an executor is never called by name), a function that holds one, upward
+    by name inside the solver's own module; a site in another module is an entry into the
+    solver, printed and not climbed (a name shared with an unrelated function stops there)."""
+    sites, home = [], None
+    for p in pkg_files(repo):
+        t = parse(p)
+        if any(isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == SOLVER_ENTRY for n in t.body):
+            home = rel(repo, p)
+        called = {id(n.func) for n in ast.walk(t) if isinstance(n, ast.Call)}
+        for n, q in scoped(t):
+            if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and fname(n):
+                sites.append((fname(n), "", rel(repo, p), n.lineno, q))
+            elif isinstance(n, (ast.Name, ast.Attribute)) and isinstance(n.ctx, ast.Load) and id(n) not in called:
+                sites.append((n.id if isinstance(n, ast.Name) else n.attr, " (ref)", rel(repo, p), n.lineno, q))
+    names, grown = {SOLVER_ENTRY}, set()
+    while names != grown:
+        grown = set(names)
+        names |= {q.split(".")[-1] for callee, _how, f, _line, q in sites if callee in grown and f == home and q != "<module>"}
+    return [f"{'solve' if callee == SOLVER_ENTRY else 'path'} {callee} <- {f}:{line} {q}{how}" for callee, how, f, line, q in sites if callee in names]
+
+
+def d12(repo, pairs=False, **_):
+    """The generality cells: every level `--population` reads, the card and each blueprint,
+    and under --pairs every pair of levels from two axes. The level and pair counts are asserted
+    against the command's own."""
+    axes, totals = population_axes(repo)
+    cells = [f"level {a}={x}" for a, lv in axes.items() for x in lv]
+    if len(cells) != totals.get("LEVELS"):
+        raise Refuse(f"{len(cells)} level cells against the population's LEVELS: {totals.get('LEVELS')}")
+    names = sorted(axes)
+    if pairs:
+        pc = [f"pair {a}={x} & {b}={y}" for i, a in enumerate(names) for b in names[i + 1:] for x in axes[a] for y in axes[b]]
+        if len(pc) != totals.get("PAIRS"):
+            raise Refuse(f"{len(pc)} pair cells against the population's PAIRS: {totals.get('PAIRS')}")
+        cells += pc
+    surf = [f"surface card {f}" for f in sorted(tracked(repo)) if f.startswith(f"{PKG}/www/") and f.endswith(".js")]
+    surf += [f"surface blueprint {f}" for f in sorted(tracked(repo)) if f.startswith("blueprints/")]
+    if not surf:
+        raise Refuse("no card and no blueprint is tracked")
+    return cells + surf
+
+
+def d15(repo, **_):
+    """The installs that sent a bundle, one line per bundle: its date, the round that read it and
+    the steps run on it. A round's examined count is its own lines; the universe is every line."""
+    p = repo / BUNDLES
+    out = []
+    for b in json.loads(p.read_text()).get("bundles", []):
+        if not (b.get("install") and re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", str(b.get("date"))) and isinstance(b.get("round"), int)
+                and isinstance(b.get("steps"), list) and b.get("evidence")):
+            raise Refuse(f"{BUNDLES}: a bundle needs install, date (YYYY-MM-DD), round, steps and evidence: {b}")
+        if not (repo / b["evidence"]).exists():
+            raise Refuse(f"{BUNDLES}: evidence {b['evidence']} of {b['install']} {b['date']} is not in the tree")
+        out.append(f"{b['install']} {b['date']} round={b['round']} steps={','.join(b['steps']) or 'none'}")
+    return out
+
+
+UNIVERSES = {"d16-writes": d16, "d17-features": d17, "d14-classes": d14, "d0-grid": d0grid, "d0-modules": d0modules,
+             "d1-stores": d1stores, "d1-excepts": d1excepts, "d1-lifecycle": d1life, "d1-inputs": d1inputs,
+             "d1-solve-state": d1solve, "d1-parsers": d1parsers, "d2-identities": d2, "d3-sites": d3, "d8-cells": d8,
+             "d9-collections": d9collections, "d9-attributes": d9attributes, "d9-solves": d9solves,
+             "d12-cells": d12, "d15-installs": d15}
+
+
+def joined(name, items, ledger):
+    """Each item beside its ledger row, or `not run`: the census with the test that drives each
+    line. A row is item and asserting test, tab-separated; a generality cell also names, between
+    them, which of decision 0018's four sources examined it, and prints `not run` with no ledger."""
+    cell = name == "d12-cells"
+    if not ledger and not cell:
+        return items
+    rows = {}
+    for i, l in enumerate(Path(ledger).read_text().splitlines() if ledger else (), 1):
+        c = [x.strip() for x in l.split("\t")]
+        if not l.strip() or l.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        if len(c) != 2 + cell or not c[-1] or (cell and c[1] not in SOURCES):
+            raise Refuse(f"{ledger}:{i}: a row is the item, " + (f"its source ({', '.join(SOURCES)}), " if cell else "")
+                         + "and its asserting test, tab-separated; a run that asserts nothing examines nothing")
+        if c[0] not in items:
+            raise Refuse(f"{ledger}:{i}: {c[0]!r} is no item of this universe as printed (check its options)")
+        rows[c[0]] = "\t".join(c[1:])
+    return [f"{x}\t{rows.get(x, 'not run')}" for x in items]
+
+
+def run(name, repo, ledger=None, **kw):
+    try:
+        lines = joined(name, sorted(_dedupe(UNIVERSES[name](Path(repo), **kw))), ledger)
+    except OSError as e:
+        raise Refuse(f"missing or unreadable source: {e}")
+    if not lines:
+        raise Refuse(f"{name} yields zero items: an empty universe is a refusal")
+    return lines
+
+
+def _dedupe(lines):
+    seen = collections.Counter()
+    for l in lines:
+        seen[l] += 1
+        yield l if seen[l] == 1 else f"{l} #{seen[l]}"
+
+
+def briefs(repo):
+    """One `ok` line per (brief, cited command); Refuse on a citation that names no universe,
+    one whose universe refuses, or a tree whose briefs cite none."""
+    out, bad = [], []
+    for f in sorted((repo / "dev/governance/dimensions").glob("D*.md")):
+        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", f.read_text())
+        for u, flags in sorted(set(re.findall(r"enumerate\.py (d\d+-[a-z-]+)((?: --(?:cells|pairs))*)", text))):
+            opt = {k: True for k in re.findall(r"--(cells|pairs)", flags)}
+            try:
+                if u not in UNIVERSES:
+                    raise Refuse("no such universe")
+                with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
+                    run(u, repo, **opt)
+                out.append(f"ok {f.stem} {u}{flags}")
+            except Refuse as e:
+                bad.append(f"{f.stem} cites `enumerate.py {u}{flags}`: {e}")
+    if bad or not out:
+        raise Refuse("; ".join(bad) or "no dimension brief cites a universe")
+    return out
+

+def cut(path, old, new=""):
+    """An edit of the planted repo that refuses to match nothing."""
+    def go(root):
+        t = (root / path).read_text()
+        if old not in t:
+            raise AssertionError(f"self-test edit of {path} matched nothing: {old!r}")
+        (root / path).write_text(t.replace(old, new, 1))
+    return go
+
+
+def put(path, text):
+    return lambda root: (root / path).write_text(text)
+
+
+def rm(*paths):
+    return lambda root: [(root / p).unlink() for p in paths]
+
+
+def both(*fs):
+    return lambda root: [f(root) for f in fs]
+
+
+def edit_json(path, fn):
+    def go(root):
+        d = json.loads((root / path).read_text())
+        fn(d)
+        (root / path).write_text(json.dumps(d))
+    return go

+def self_test():
+    arms, fails = 0, []
+
+    def arm(name, got, want):
+        nonlocal arms
+        arms += 1
+        if got != want:
+            fails.append(f"{name}: got {got!r}, want {want!r}")
+
+    def count(u, t, **opt):
+        try:
+            with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
+                return len(run(u, t, **opt))
+        except Refuse:
+            return "Refuse"
+
+    live = Path(".")
+    for u in UNIVERSES:
+        for opt in ({}, *[o for n, o, *_ in PLANTED if n == u and o and "ast_only" not in o], *([{"plane": "price-weather"}] if u == "d0-grid" else [])):
+            try:
+                with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
+                    ls = run(u, live, **opt)
+            except Refuse as e:
+                ls = []
+                fails.append(f"live {u} {opt}: {e}")
+            arm(f"live {u} {opt}", (len(ls) >= 1, ls == sorted(ls), len(ls) == len(set(ls))), (True, True, True))
+    try:
+        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
+            d3_all = run("d3-sites", live)
+            by_state = {st: run("d3-sites", live, state=st) for st in ("killed", "triaged", "unrecorded") if any(l.split(" #")[0].endswith(" " + st) for l in d3_all)}
+            by_file = [l.split() for l in run("d3-sites", live, by_file=True)]
+        arm("live d3-sites: the --state filters partition the universe", sorted(l for ls in by_state.values() for l in ls), d3_all)
+        arm("live d3-sites: each --state filter holds only its state", all(l.split(" #")[0].endswith(" " + st) for st, ls in by_state.items() for l in ls), True)
+        arm("live d3-sites --by-file: each file's three state counts sum to its total, and the totals to the universe",
+            (all(int(r[1]) == sum(map(int, r[2:5])) for r in by_file), sum(int(r[1]) for r in by_file)), (True, len(d3_all)))
+    except Refuse as e:
+        fails.append(f"live d3-sites options: {e}")
+    try:
+        arm("live briefs", len(briefs(live)) >= 1, True)
+    except Refuse as e:
+        fails.append(f"live briefs: {e}")
+    arm("every universe has a planted arm", sorted({n for n, *_ in PLANTED}), sorted(UNIVERSES))
+    for u, opt, n, delete, after, empty in PLANTED:
+        for label, edit, want in (("planted", None, n), ("one item deleted", delete, after), ("source emptied", empty, "Refuse")):
+            t = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+            try:
+                plant(t)
+                if edit:
+                    edit(t)
+                arm(f"{u} {opt or ''} {label}", count(u, t, **opt), want)
+            finally:
+                shutil.rmtree(t, ignore_errors=True)
+    t = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+    try:
+        plant(t)
+        arm("d0-grid plane", run("d0-grid", t, plane="price-weather"), ["p1/w1", "p2/w1"])
+        arm("d14 open", run("d14-classes", t, status="open"), ["open production A"])
+        arm("d1-stores lines: DOMAINS keys, each earlier step of CONFIG_ENTRY_VERSION and of a *_STORE_VERSION, a v1 store once",
+            run("d1-stores", t), ["store a", "store b", f"upgrade {PKG}/const.py:CONFIG_ENTRY_VERSION v1->3", f"upgrade {PKG}/const.py:CONFIG_ENTRY_VERSION v2->3",
+                                  f"upgrade {PKG}/store.py:LEDGER_STORE_VERSION v1->2", f"upgrade {PKG}/store.py:MAP_STORE_VERSION v1 (no earlier version)"])
+        arm("d1-inputs lines: a flow key behind an entity selector (one outside the CONF_*_ENTITY shape, two a loop binds), "
+            "and a key the reset keeps as an entity assignment by the wiring's rule or its literal entry",
+            run("d1-inputs", t), [f"input {k}" for k in ("CONF_A_ENTITY", "CONF_B_ENTITY", "CONF_F_SENSOR", "CONF_H1", "CONF_H2", "CONF_W_SENSOR")])
+        for label, edit in (("an entity selector outside an `_F` row", cut(CF, "ROWS = (", "LOOSE = _entity_of('x')\nROWS = (")),
+                            ("an entity selector row whose key is no name", cut(CF, "_F('s', CONF_A_ENTITY,", "_F('s', 'a_entity',")),
+                            ("a wiring rule holding a test the census cannot read", cut(f"{PKG}/entry_config.py", "key.endswith('_entity')", "key[-7:] == '_entity'")),
+                            ("a FACTORY_KEPT holding a second comprehension", cut(f"{PKG}/entry_config.py", "**_WIRING})", "**_WIRING, **{k: 'other' for k in ()}})")),
+                            ("an isinstance test on the loop's name, not its value", cut(f"{PKG}/entry_config.py", "isinstance(key, str)", "isinstance(name, str)"))):

+                shutil.rmtree(g, ignore_errors=True)
+        arm("d1-excepts lines carry broad or narrow", [l.split()[1] for l in run("d1-excepts", t)], ["broad", "narrow"])
+        arm("d1-lifecycle lines: an async_track_* call, a LIFE_CALLS call and every entry point",
+            run("d1-lifecycle", t), sorted([f"async_create_task {X}:12 f", f"async_track_time_interval {X}:11 f", *[f"entry {f}" for f in ENTRY]]))
+        arm("d16-writes lines: the .services.async_call sites and log_held, not an async_call on another receiver",
+            run("d16-writes", t), [f"hold {X}:4 f", f"write {X}:2 f", f"write {X}:3 f"])
+        arm("d1-parsers lines: a parse def, json.loads, a bare .json() and async_subscribe, not a .json(x) with an argument",
+            run("d1-parsers", t), [f"def {PKG}/p.py:2 parse_a", f"json {PKG}/p.py:3 parse_a", f"response {PKG}/p.py:5 g", f"subscribe {PKG}/p.py:7 g"])

+up to the base (PR mode) or the head (push mode), the target is
+  nonproduction_merges - step * floor(n / every_merges), never below 0,
+compared against target plus nonproduction_merges' band, again by merge count,
+never hours. It refuses only a candidate that is not production and not
+exempted: a production candidate cannot raise the metric, and in push mode the
+target is a report line, so the schedule passing the window turns no check on
+main red. The caps above stay the ceiling in both modes. No file, no target.

 - [`approve_held_runs.sh`](instruments/approve_held_runs.sh.md) — approves the workflow runs GitHub holds `action_required` on a branch
 - [`check_scopes.py`](instruments/check_scopes.py.md) — proves the finder scopes are disjoint and complete within each dimension
+- [`enumerate.py`](instruments/enumerate.py.md) — prints one audit universe, one item per line, so a finder reports examined over a command's output
 - [`text_ledger.py`](instruments/text_ledger.py.md) — enumerates every unit a D5 or D6 seat judges and refuses a ledger that skips one
 - [`fold_ledger.py`](instruments/fold_ledger.py.md) — folds a round's JUDGE.json and sweeps into `bugclasses.json`
 - [`judge_batch.py`](instruments/judge_batch.py.md) — re-runs every finding's harness, perturbation and null control serially under the gate lease

 - [`plan_public.py`](instruments/plan_public.py.md) — stages the ongoing round's plan page from the newest state ref for the public site, refusing a page that would publish a host path or a tool's attribution
 - [`bottleneck_check.py`](instruments/bottleneck_check.py.md) — prints one `BOTTLENECK:` line per flow metric past the owner's threshold, with a suggested action the orchestrator decides on, and nothing when none is
-- [`scorecard.py`](instruments/scorecard.py.md) — ten report-only convergence lines (gate and run health, first-verdict yield, machinery blocks, train skips, hotfix share, size, escapes, detection delay, seat cost), each but the hotfix naming measure held to a null control, written daily to `S/beatd/scorecard.txt`
+- [`scorecard.py`](instruments/scorecard.py.md) — report-only convergence lines (gate and run health, first-verdict yield, machinery blocks, train skips, hotfix share, size, escapes, detection delay, seat cost, and round_metrics.py's reads over the open round), each but the hotfix naming measure held to a null control, written daily to `S/beatd/scorecard.txt`
+- [`round_metrics.py`](instruments/round_metrics.py.md) — decision 0018's flow reads per round and per week (merges by class, lead_time from the roster-entry commit per class, product_green with the gate's check count, restore, runner seconds and tokens per merge), unread on no input, and the producer of the scorecard's inputs
 - [`plant_recall.py`](instruments/plant_recall.py.md) — plants a held-out seat's objective bugs into the baseline export before the finders, refusing an unsound plant list, and counts recall after the judge (found / planted, whole, per space and per kind), unread on no input
 - [`finder_overlap.py`](instruments/finder_overlap.py.md) — seats a twin finder on one scopes.json seat's universe and estimates the bugs there from the two seats' judged-real overlap, with both models, unread on no input
 - [`outside_intake.py`](instruments/outside_intake.py.md) — lists submissions by outside users since a cursor with what each is owed (triage, answer, reply), and answers or refuses one, marked so none is answered twice

+#: ci-attempt flags a run at this attempt or more; gate.py's ATTEMPT_CAP (45) is where the hooks stop.
+CI_ATTEMPT_ALARM = 20
+CI_RUN = re.compile(r"(\d+) (\d+) (\S+) ?([\d,]*)")
+
+
+def ci_attempt(ctx: Ctx) -> None:
+    """One line per ci.yml run at attempt CI_ATTEMPT_ALARM or more among the newest 100, named with its PR."""
+    got = ctx.need("ci-attempt", "repo")
+    if got is None:
+        return
+    rc, out, _ = ctx.run(["gh", "api", f"repos/{got[0]}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?per_page=100", "--jq",
+                          '.workflow_runs[] | "\\(.id) \\(.run_attempt) \\(.head_branch) \\([.pull_requests[].number] | join(","))"'],
+                         ctx.repo, ctx.env)
+    if rc != 0:
+        return write_job(ctx, "ci-attempt", [f"ci-attempt: UNREADABLE gh rc={rc}"])
+    lines = []
+    for ln in out.splitlines():
+        m = CI_RUN.fullmatch(ln.strip())
+        if m and int(m[2]) >= CI_ATTEMPT_ALARM:
+            prs = " ".join(f"#{n}" for n in m[4].split(",") if n) or "no pull request"
+            lines.append(f"CI-ATTEMPT: run {m[1]} at attempt >= {CI_ATTEMPT_ALARM} on {m[3]} ({prs})")
+    write_job(ctx, "ci-attempt", lines)
+
+

 DARWIN_LEASE_LABEL = "darwin-selftest"

-       "outside-intake": outside_intake, "bottleneck": bottleneck, "scorecard": scorecard,
+       "outside-intake": outside_intake, "cp-owed": cp_owed, "bottleneck": bottleneck, "scorecard": scorecard,
+       "ci-attempt": ci_attempt,
        "darwin-selftest": darwin_selftest}

@@ -33,8 +33,15 @@ smallest sample that may trip it, so that one verdict or one merge never fires:

-new line and the wake fires once per trip; a metric back inside its threshold
-is forgotten, and its next trip prints afresh. The memory is keyed by the
+new line and the wake fires once per trip -- unless its live value is more
+than a quarter worse (WORSE) than the value that first line printed: then the
+live line prints, so the digest never shows a stale value that hides a
+worsening metric (owner ruling 2026-11-13, card P8; the process convergence
+audit's row a7, where "merge-wait 2.1 h" re-printed while it stood at 4.2 h).
+The first line stays the reference, so a held breach prints the live line on
+every beat it is past WORSE, and its first line again once it is not. Lower
+is worse for yield and throughput, higher for the rest. A metric back inside
+its threshold is forgotten, and its next trip prints afresh. The memory is keyed by the

+#: A held breach prints its live line once its value is worse than the first printed one by more than this share.
+WORSE = 0.25
+LOWER_IS_WORSE = {"yield", "throughput"}
+
+
+class Line(str):
+    """A breach line carrying the value it printed (None on an UNREADABLE line)."""
+    value: float | None = None
+
+
+def _line(text: str, value: float) -> Line:
+    ln = Line(text)
+    ln.value = value
+    return ln

     return f"BOTTLENECK-UNREADABLE: {metric} -- {why}"
 
 
+def worse(metric: str, first: float | None, live: float | None) -> bool:
+    """Whether `live` is worse than `first` by more than WORSE, in the metric's own direction."""
+    if first is None or live is None:
+        return False
+    if metric in LOWER_IS_WORSE:
+        return live < first * (1 - WORSE)
+    return live > first * (1 + WORSE)
